Correlate each clause's source contribution with its mean cross-task contribution (Spearman, attenuation-corrected using split-half reliability of both quantities across seeds). Fit a mixed model predicting cross-task contribution from clause type, controlling for source contribution and clause length.
(7) Zero-rollout clause library. Leave-one-target-out: rank clauses by mean measured portability on the 7 training targets, greedily assemble a prefix (stopping at a token cap) with redundancy filtering, apply to the held-out target with zero optimization. Compare against the cold-start GEPA budget curve at 0/10/25/50/100/300 rollouts on the same target and report the 'rollout equivalence' with a bootstrap interval. Also test library-as-seed: initialize GEPA with the library prefix and compare its budget curve to cold start.
(8) Mechanism split. Report task accuracy and output-format compliance as separate metrics throughout, so we can say whether portable clauses buy correctness or only contract adherence.
Baselines and Ablations:
Baselines: (i) cold-start GEPA budget curve on each target — the reference the library must be priced against, and the winner at large budget by construction; (ii) whole-prompt warm start / zero-shot transfer of the best source prompt (the obvious cheap alternative; if it matches the clause library, clause-level decomposition adds nothing); (iii) a hand-written generic prompt-engineering checklist of matched token length, written without seeing any optimization run — the baseline most likely to beat us, since it tests whether harvesting was necessary at all; (iv) length-matched neutral filler and (v) sham (semantically inverted) clauses, controlling for token count and for 'any extra structure helps'; (vi) random clauses drawn from the library instead of top-portability ones; (vii) portability-oracle selection on the held-out target (upper bound).
Ablations: portability estimated from 1 vs 7 source tasks; clause type restricted to a single type at a time (contract-only, error-avoidance-only, content-only libraries) to see which type carries the effect; insertion position (prefix vs suffix vs interleaved); domain-scrubbed vs raw clauses, with a source-identification leakage test; second executor (Llama-3.1-8B) on a 4×4 sub-matrix to test whether portability rankings are executor-specific; segmentation granularity (sentence vs bullet vs paragraph).
Falsifiable Predictions: If the hypothesis holds: (a) within-source contributions are dominated by a few clauses, with task-specific-content clauses accounting for ≥ 50% of total source gain; (b) the Spearman correlation between source contribution and mean cross-task contribution is low, ≈ 0.0–0.3 attenuation-corrected, while clause type explains substantially more variance (mixed-model ΔR² ≥ 0.15 over a source-contribution-only model); (c) content clauses show mean cross-task delta ≤ 0, with ≥ 15% of content-clause×target cells negative beyond the noise floor, while output-contract and error-avoidance clauses show mean cross-task delta of +1 to +4 points and are positive on a majority of targets; (d) the zero-rollout leave-one-target-out clause library is worth 25–75 cold-start GEPA rollouts (bootstrap CI excluding zero) and beats the length-matched filler and sham-clause controls by ≥ 2 points; (e) at least half the library's gain survives when format-compliance-driven items are removed from the metric. Refutation: the hand-written generic checklist matches the harvested library (harvesting is unnecessary); or filler/sham controls match it (the effect is token count, not content); or source contribution predicts cross-task contribution as well as type does (no dissociation — optimizers just find universally good text); or the library's rollout equivalence CI includes zero.
Measurement and Noise Control: Four disjoint splits per task: GEPA feedback set, GEPA validation set, an attribution set (used for all clause-level scoring), and a never-touched test set used only for the final library-vs-cold-start comparison, so clause selection never sees the reporting data. Every clause-level measurement is paired: the same executor, decode seed, example order and example subset are used for the with- and without-clause conditions, so deltas are within-item differences; we report per-example paired differences and use a paired bootstrap over examples clustered by task. Attribution set = 200 examples; with binary accuracy at p≈0.5 and paired scoring, a single clause×target cell detects ≈ 4-point effects at 80% power, so no individual cell is interpreted alone — all claims are made over aggregates of ≥ 15 cells (type-level means, n ≈ 15–40 cells, detect ≈ 1.2 points) or across 8 leave-one-target-out folds × 3 seeds = 24 paired observations for the library comparison (detects ≈ 1.5 points given the measured ~3-point run SD). Split-half reliability across GEPA seeds is reported for both source and cross-task contribution vectors *before* any correlation is interpreted, and correlations are attenuation-corrected against it. Anything below the treatment-free null-replicate floor is reported as null regardless of p-value; rollout equivalence is always an interval, never a point.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) Clauses interact: a clause's marginal effect depends on its context, so leave-one-out and random-subset estimates can disagree; we report both and treat large disagreement as evidence of non-additivity, which is itself a finding about whether 'portable components' is even the right abstraction. (2) Segmentation is LLM-mediated and granularity-dependent; the granularity ablation bounds this but cannot eliminate it. (3) With 200-example attribution sets, per-cell power is low; the design compensates with aggregation, which means we can characterize clause *types* far better than individual clauses. (4) Eight tasks give eight generalization units; conclusions are stated at the level of these clusters. (5) The hand-written checklist baseline may match the harvested library, reducing the paper to a decomposition study plus a negative result on harvesting — still informative, and we would report it as such. (6) Portability may be executor-specific; only a reduced second-model replication is affordable. (7) The zero-rollout library is not expected to beat well-funded cold-start optimization, and we frame the result as a price in rollouts, not a win.

Name: coadaptation_transplant_ccr
Title: Who Broke It, the Instruction or the Memory? A Transplant Diagnostic for Prompt–Memory Co-Adaptation, and a Counterfactual Routing Fix
Short Hypothesis: When a reflective prompt optimizer evolves instructions while a self-editing memory is injected, every failure is attributed to the instruction by construction, because the reflector only ever sees traces that already contain memory. The consequence is not merely inefficiency: the reported gain of current practice is *conditional on the exact bank it was tuned against*. Instructions optimized with memory present become memory-dependent — they lose more when memory is removed, truncated, or rebuilt from a different task mix — and this dependence is a separate, measurable quantity from accuracy. A cheap counterfactual replay (re-run each failed training episode with the retrieved memory removed) separates instruction-attributable from memory-attributable failures, and routing each failure to the corresponding artifact (instruction rewrite vs. memory edit) removes most of the dependence without giving up in-distribution accuracy — something a blind regularizer (memory dropout, injection-budget capping) cannot do, because it removes the dependence by removing the memory's contribution.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **Reflective/evolutionary prompt optimizers.** MIPRO (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024) frames credit assignment across modules and between instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations; GEPA and successors add reflective natural-language mutation. All treat the demonstration slot as a static, optimizer-owned artifact, not as a bank that a separate write path is concurrently rewriting, and none tests whether the resulting instruction is conditionally dependent on that slot's presence.

(2) **Instruction-vs-exemplar credit.** Adv-ICL (ACL 2024) reports "w/o instruction" and "w/o demonstration" ablations; "Teach Better or Show Smarter?" compares instruction and exemplar optimization. These ablate at *evaluation* time within a single optimization regime. Detecting co-adaptation requires the transplant design — optimize under regime A, evaluate under regime B — which none of them runs, and none involves retrieved agent experience.

(3) **Agentic memory and joint context evolution.** ExpeL, Reflexion, A-Mem, ReasoningBank, AdaMEM (2606.05684), Mem-pi (2605.21463) build and inject experience against a fixed prompt; harm from injection is attributed to memory content, never to a prompt tuned around that memory. Agentic Context Engineering (ACE, surveyed in 2507.21046) is exactly the system our critique targets: one incremental-update loop doing offline prompt optimization *and* online memory adaptation, with no attribution between them. CoWork-X (2602.05004) co-evolves a skill library with an optimizer but regularizes drift rather than attributing failures.

(4) **Counterfactual credit assignment — the conceptual ancestor.** "Remove the suspect input and see if the outcome flips" descends from COMA-style counterfactual baselines and hindsight credit assignment in multi-agent RL, and this lineage is now active in LLM agents: HiMPO (2606.16285) uses a local memory-state counterfactual plus hindsight relevance to credit memory-*writing* actions; Memory-R2 (2605.21768) disentangles current-session memory operations from inherited corruption; TreeMem (2605.04811) and CCPO do per-component counterfactual credit in multi-agent pipelines; CANTANTE (2605.13295) compares alternative trajectories with a prompted LLM to attribute outcome differences across generic workflow components; UCOB (2606.29502) uses skill-conditioned vs. no-skill context views for credit-aware self-distillation. **We concede that the counterfactual-replay signal itself is not new**, and we do not claim it. All of these either update weights over numeric rewards or attribute across workflow components; none asks whether a *natural-language instruction produced by a reflective optimizer* has silently absorbed the memory bank, and none measures the resulting dependence.

(5) **Attribution inside a prompt-optimization loop.** Environment-Grounded APO for game agents (2606.17838) is the closest application-side match: its attribution stage asks whether a failure's root cause was the "Descriptor" (a perception/context-providing module) or the agent's own behavior before rewriting the prompt. That Descriptor is a fixed perception module, not a self-editing experience bank, and the paper never evaluates the rewritten prompt outside the regime it was written in — which is the measurement that turns this from a routing heuristic into a claim about a failure mode of current practice.

Our contribution is therefore (a) the diagnostic — co-adaptation exists, is separable from accuracy, and means published memory+optimizer gains are bank-conditional — and (b) the demonstration that a counterfactual routing signal, not a blind regularizer, is what removes it.
Abstract:
Agent frameworks increasingly pair a reflective prompt optimizer, which rewrites instructions from failed trajectories, with a self-editing memory that injects distilled past experience. The composition has a structural flaw no current system addresses: the reflector observes only trajectories in which memory was already present, so a failure caused by a misleading retrieved item is indistinguishable from a failure caused by a bad instruction, and the optimizer patches the instruction either way. We predict this produces co-adaptation — instructions that encode compensations for the specific bank they were tuned against, and are consequently brittle when memory is absent, truncated, or rebuilt. The sharp version of the claim is that current practice's headline gain is *rented, not owned*: it is conditional on the exact bank, and largely disappears under a same-size, same-retriever bank rebuilt from a different task-family mix.

We test this with a transplant design on tool-augmented multi-hop QA: instructions are optimized under memory-present and memory-absent regimes with paired optimizer seeds, then evaluated under memory-absent, same-bank, shifted-bank, and truncated-injection regimes, so co-adaptation appears as a difference-in-differences interaction separable from raw accuracy. We then test counterfactual credit routing (CCR): each failed training episode is replayed once with retrieved memory removed; persistent failures go to the instruction reflector, vanishing failures become memory-edit proposals. CCR is compared at matched rollout budget against the base optimizer with memory, two blind regularizers that a reviewer would reach for first (memory dropout during optimization, and capping the injection budget to k=2 during training), a soft two-view reflector that sees both traces without hard routing, and a random-routing ablation that spends the same edits without the counterfactual signal. The whole program is one primary environment, one primary model, and 107k episode-equivalents — about five days on a single 4×A100 node — with a pre-registered cut order. We report paired McNemar tests with fix/break decompositions, paired-seed optimizer statistics, null decoding and null optimizer replicates that fix the noise floor, and we pre-commit to reporting a null interaction term with its minimum detectable effect as the primary negative outcome.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED throughout:** ReAct scaffold, retriever and similarity function, base memory bank construction (ExpeL-style write path run once on the training split, then frozen except where a condition is explicitly allowed to edit it), decoding temperature and seed schedule, tool stack, step limit, and the reflector/judge model. Only the optimization regime and the credit-assignment rule vary.

**PRIMARY ENVIRONMENT AND MODEL (the only quantitatively load-bearing setting):** E1 = tool-augmented multi-hop QA (HotpotQA distractor + MuSiQue, agent issues search calls, 4–8 model calls per episode), agent = Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct served with vLLM. Splits: 400 train / 150 optimizer-validation / 500 held-out test, disjoint. Reflector and judge = one frontier API model, identical across all conditions.

**SECONDARY, BEST-EFFORT, EXPLICITLY NOT LOAD-BEARING:** E2 = ALFWorld, directional replication of B3 vs. B6 only. M2 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, replication of the Part 1 diagnostic only. WebShop and Qwen3-32B are cut.

**MEMORY BANKS.** Bank_A: written from the E1 train split. Bank_B (shift): same size, same write path, same retriever, built from a disjoint pool with a different task-family mix. T_trunc uses Bank_A at k=2 instead of k=7.

**PART 1 — DOES CO-ADAPTATION EXIST (primary claim).**
Optimize instructions with a fixed reflective optimizer under two training regimes at identical rollout budget: R_mem (top-k=7 retrieved items injected in every training rollout, Bank_A) and R_nomem (no memory during training). Five optimizer seeds per regime, **paired**: seed s in R_mem and seed s in R_nomem share data order, minibatch composition, and candidate-proposal temperature, so the regime difference is a within-seed contrast.
Evaluate all 10 resulting instructions, plus the unoptimized prompt with and without memory (B0/B1) and a write-path-hygiene-only baseline (B1b), under four fully instance-paired test regimes: T_nomem, T_mem (Bank_A, k=7), T_shift (Bank_B, k=7), T_trunc (Bank_A, k=2). n=500 paired test instances.
Headline quantity: DiD = [acc(R_mem @ T_mem) − acc(R_mem @ T_nomem)] − [acc(R_nomem @ T_mem) − acc(R_nomem @ T_nomem)].
Second diagnostic: the T_mem→T_shift drop, compared across regimes (the "rented gain" test).
Third, a text-level readout: an independent judge classifies each optimized instruction's clauses as memory-referential (how to consume, trust, or override retrieved experience) vs. task-substantive; we test whether memory-referential clause count predicts per-run DiD across the 10 runs.

**PART 2 — DOES THE COUNTERFACTUAL SIGNAL CARRY INFORMATION.**
Sample 200 failed training episodes from R_mem runs. Replay each with memory removed, 3 decoding seeds; label memory-attributable if without-memory success rate exceeds with-memory by a fixed margin. Compare against (a) two human annotators reading both traces on a 120-episode subset, (b) retrieval-similarity thresholding, (c) an LLM judge asked directly, from the single with-memory trace, whether memory caused the failure. Metrics: Cohen's kappa vs. human labels, precision/recall of memory-attributable detection.

**PART 3 — THE METHOD (secondary claim).**
CCR: during optimization, each failed minibatch episode is replayed once without memory. Persistent failures form the reflection pool for instruction mutation exactly as in the base optimizer. Vanishing failures mark the specific retrieved items present in the failing trace; on accumulating evidence across episodes those items are pruned or rewritten by the write path. The instruction reflector never sees memory-attributable failures. Candidate proposal, Pareto-style selection, and validation minibatches are unchanged.

Conditions, all at matched total agent-rollout budget (counterfactual replays are charged to CCR, so baselines receive proportionally more optimization rollouts), all seeds paired with Part 1 seeds:
- **B0/B1/B1b** — no optimization: no memory / memory injected / memory-hygiene-only bank (contradiction pruning + call-balance rebalancing, no instruction optimization). Evaluation only.
- **B2** = R_nomem, **B3** = R_mem (current practice), reused from Part 1, 5 seeds each.
- **B4 Memory dropout** — candidates scored on minibatches where memory is present with p=0.5. The blind-regularizer answer. 5 seeds.
- **B6 CCR (ours).** 5 seeds.
- **B10 Training-time injection cap** — optimize with k=2 throughout (the "volume is the causal lever" fix, promoted from an evaluation probe to a competing intervention). 3 seeds.
- **B9 Soft two-view reflection** — reflector is shown both the memory-present and memory-absent trace of each failure and left to weight them; no hard routing, no memory edits. The gradient-free analogue of UCOB/HiMPO's two-view idea, and the cleanest separation of "counterfactual signal" from "hard exclusion". 3 seeds.
- **B5 Random routing** — same number of failures diverted from the instruction pool to the memory-edit path, chosen uniformly at random. Holds routing volume fixed, removes only the signal. 3 seeds.
- **B7 CCR, instruction routing only** — memory-attributable failures dropped, bank never edited. Separates "protect the reflector" from "fix the bank"; also the safety condition if routed edits degrade the bank. 3 seeds.
- **B8 Oracle routing** — reported only on the Part 2 attribution subset as an upper bound on routing value; **no full seed sweep** (reviewer-requested trim).

Part 3 evaluation uses three regimes (T_nomem, T_mem, T_shift); T_trunc is Part 1 only.

**COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (E1 episode-equivalents; one E1 episode ≈ 6 LLM calls).**
- Part 1 optimization: 10 runs × 800 rollouts = 8,000
- Part 1 evaluation: 13 prompts × 4 regimes × 500 = 26,000
- Part 2 attribution: 200 × 3 replays = 600
- Part 3 optimization: (B4 5 + B6 5 + B10 3 + B9 3 + B5 3 + B7 3) = 22 runs × 800 = 17,600
- Part 3 evaluation: 22 prompts × 3 regimes × 500 = 33,000
- Null decoding replicates: 6 prompt×regime cells re-run at a new seed × 500 = 3,000
- **E1 subtotal: 88,200 episodes**
- E2 ALFWorld (best effort): 6 runs × 300 + 6 × 2 regimes × 150 = 3,600 episodes, ≈4× cost ⇒ 14,400 equiv.
- M2 Llama-8B diagnostic (best effort): 6 runs × 800 + 6 × 2 regimes × 400 = 9,600 episodes, ≈0.5× cost ⇒ 4,800 equiv.
- **Total ≈ 107,000 E1 episode-equivalents.**
At a conservative 0.5 episodes/s node-aggregate throughput (2 vLLM replicas, TP=2, high concurrency), that is ~60 GPU-hours of wall clock; we budget 5 days including restarts. API: ~40 optimization runs × 20 reflection iterations × 3 candidate proposals × ~7k tokens ≈ 17M tokens ≈ $150, plus judging and attribution baselines ≈ $40. Under the stated few-hundred-dollar budget.
**Pre-registered cut order** if a pilot shows throughput below 0.35 ep/s: drop M2, then E2, then reduce B5/B7/B9/B10 to 2 seeds, then reduce Part 3 test n to 400. Part 1 and the B3-vs-B6-vs-B4 5-seed comparison are never cut; if they cannot be run, the paper is not written.
Baselines and Ablations:
**Baselines that could plausibly win, and would kill the method claim.**
(i) **B4 memory dropout** — if randomizing memory presence in the optimizer's scoring minibatches closes the interaction gap as well as CCR *without* costing T_mem accuracy, the attribution machinery is unnecessary and we say so. This is the single most likely way the method claim dies. Our prediction is that it closes the gap by sacrificing the memory's contribution (loses at T_mem), which is a different outcome, not a hedge.
(ii) **B10 training-time k=2 cap** — the track's own prior finding was that injection volume, not content, was the causal lever for harm. If simply capping k during optimization removes co-adaptation at no cost, the routing story is redundant. Added at reviewer request.
(iii) **B9 soft two-view reflection** — reflector sees both traces, decides for itself. Isolates whether CCR's benefit comes from the counterfactual signal per se or from hard exclusion of memory-attributable failures plus bank repair. Added at reviewer request; it is the strongest baseline, since it is what a competent engineer would build after reading UCOB or CANTANTE.
(iv) **B3 at T_mem alone** — likely the best in-distribution configuration. Our claim is about the interaction and about shift, not about beating B3 on its home turf.
(v) **B1b pure write-path hygiene** — wins if all the value is on the memory side and instruction optimization is decoration.

**Ablations isolating the mechanism.**
B5 random routing holds routing *volume* fixed and deletes only the counterfactual signal: if B5 = B6, the benefit is reflector-noise reduction, not attribution. B7 separates protecting the reflector from repairing the bank, and is the safety condition if routed edits damage Bank_A. B8 oracle routing (subset only) bounds what a perfect attributor buys.

**Budget matching is load-bearing.** CCR spends ~1.3–1.6× rollouts per failure; all baselines get proportionally more optimization steps. Every condition is additionally reported on wall-clock-matched and API-token-matched axes.

**Controls.** Frozen-memory ablation (bank never edited during R_mem optimization) to confirm co-adaptation is not merely tracking bank drift; shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check; instruction-paraphrase control to confirm the interaction is not generic prompt fragility.
Falsifiable Predictions:
**P1 (primary — co-adaptation exists).** On E1, the DiD interaction is ≥5 accuracy points and positive in ≥4 of 5 paired optimizer seeds. Instructions optimized with memory lose substantially more when memory is removed than memory-free instructions gain from having it.
**P2 (the sharp, disagreeable one — the gain is rented).** From T_mem to T_shift (same size, same retriever, different task-family mix), R_mem instructions drop at least twice as much as R_nomem instructions, with an absolute gap ≥4 points, such that R_mem's advantage over R_nomem at T_shift is ≤1 point. That is: the published-style headline gain of optimizer+memory is conditional on the specific bank and does not survive a benign bank rebuild.
**P3.** Memory-referential clause count in optimized instructions correlates with per-run DiD magnitude, Spearman ρ > 0.5 across the 10 Part 1 runs.
**P4.** The counterfactual attributor reaches κ > 0.5 against human labels; retrieval-score thresholding stays below 0.2 and the single-trace LLM judge below 0.35.
**P5 (method).** CCR reduces the interaction term relative to B3 by ≥5 points absolute (paired-seed MDE 3.3, see below), stays within 1.5 points of B3 at T_mem, and beats B3 by ≥3 points at T_shift, at matched rollout budget.
**P6 (mechanism — what separates CCR from a regularizer).** B4 and B10 also reduce the interaction, but do so by ≥2 points of T_mem accuracy relative to CCR; B5 random routing shows no interaction reduction beyond noise; B9 soft two-view captures less than half of CCR's interaction reduction. Stated positively: **hard exclusion plus bank repair, not the mere availability of the counterfactual to the reflector, is what buys the robustness.**

**Refutations, pre-committed.** DiD below 2 points with a CI covering zero across five paired seeds kills the co-adaptation claim and we publish it with the stated MDE. If B4 or B10 matches B6 on *every* regime including T_mem, the routing contribution collapses to "a blind regularizer would have done it" and that is the reported finding. If B5 matches B6, the counterfactual signal is inert and the paper reduces to "reflectors benefit from fewer failures". If B9 ≥ B6, the contribution is the diagnostic alone and the two-view reflector is the recommended fix — we report that rather than defending CCR. A DiD in the 2–5 point band is reported as inconclusive, not as evidence either way.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Two variance sources are separated.

**(a) Evaluation variance.** Every test instance is run under every condition with the same seed schedule; all evaluation comparisons are within-instance. Primary test: exact McNemar on fix/break counts with Holm correction across the condition family. Every reported delta carries its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention.

**(b) Optimizer variance — the larger and usually ignored source.** Optimizer seeds are *paired across conditions* (same data order, same minibatch composition, same proposal temperature), so condition contrasts are within-seed differences. Condition-level comparisons use a mixed-effects logistic model with test instance and optimizer seed as crossed random effects; CIs from a cluster bootstrap resampling optimizer seeds, not just instances.

**Null replicates.** For E1 we re-run six identical prompt×regime cells under a different decoding seed and report the distribution of apparent deltas; no effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. We also run a **null optimizer replicate** — two seeds of the same condition compared against each other — which sets the floor for any cross-condition optimizer claim. Prior pilot work in this setting saw re-scoring drift of 5–14 points, so this is not optional.

**Minimum detectable effects, stated before running.**
- Instance-paired McNemar, n=500, expected discordant-pair rate 15%: SE of the net delta ≈ 1.7 points; 80% power at α=0.05 detects ≈4.8 points. This is why P1 is stated at 5.
- DiD across 5 *paired* optimizer seeds, with the between-seed SD of the paired difference estimated from the null optimizer replicates (assumed 2.0–2.5 points): 80% power detects ≈3.3–4.1 points. The pairing is what makes the method claim (P5) powered at all; an unpaired design would have MDE ≈5, and we would have been unable to detect halving of a 6-point interaction.
- Honest limit: if the Part 1 interaction comes in below 8 points, P5 as stated (≥5 points absolute reduction) is not achievable and we will report the CCR-vs-B3 comparison as inconclusive with its MDE rather than reframing the threshold post hoc.
- E2 and M2 are directional only, MDE ≈7 points; no quantitative claim rests on them.

**Attribution reliability.** Human labels come from two annotators with reported agreement; the clause-classification judge is validated on a 100-instruction human subset and treated as supporting, not primary, evidence.
Preprint Collision Check:
The fresh search returned six 2026 preprints on counterfactual credit assignment in LLM agents, and they change the positioning materially. **We concede the counterfactual-replay signal is prior art and no longer claim it as the contribution.**

- **HiMPO (2606.16285)** — memory-state counterfactual as the primary credit signal plus hindsight relevance filtering, for optimizing memory *writing*. **Collides on mechanism**, not on claim: it is an RL/policy-optimization method over numeric rewards for write actions; it never asks what happens to a natural-language instruction optimized in the memory's presence, and it computes no interaction term.
- **Memory-R2 (2605.21768)** — disentangles current-session memory operations from inherited corruption and later overwrites, training the memory manager and fact extractor jointly. Names the same class of confound but keeps it *inside* the memory system; the prompt is not a party to the attribution.
- **CANTANTE (2605.13295)** — contrastive credit attribution over alternative trajectories with a prompted LLM judge, for generic agentic workflow components. **This is the closest match to CCR's routing rule** and we now cite it as such; it does not treat a self-editing memory as one of the components, does not evaluate the rewritten artifact outside its training regime, and makes no co-adaptation claim.
- **Environment-Grounded APO for game agents (2606.17838)** — closest on the application side: its attribution stage asks whether a failure's root cause was the context-providing "Descriptor" or the agent's own prompt-driven behavior, inside a prompt-optimization loop. The Descriptor is a fixed perception module, not a co-evolving experience bank, and the transplant evaluation is absent.
- **UCOB (2606.29502)** — skill-conditioned vs. no-skill views for credit-aware self-distillation; weight-updating, and the views repair a teacher assumption. Its gradient-free analogue is now an explicit baseline (B9), not our method.
- **TreeMem (2605.04811)**, **CCPO**, **"Unifying Temporal and Structural Credit Assignment in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Prompt Optimization" (2605.30227)** — component-level credit in multi-agent pipelines and role/aggregation prompts. Structurally similar machinery, different decomposition axis.
- **ACE / self-evolving agent survey (2507.21046)** — ACE runs joint offline prompt optimization and online memory adaptation in one incremental-update loop with no attribution between them. This is the deployed instance of the failure mode we test, and we now cite it as the motivating target rather than only as related work.
- **"Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems" (2605.28732)** — title-level overlap; only its reference list was retrievable. Flagged as unverified residual risk.
- **"Counterfactual Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation" (ICLR 2026 poster)** — title overlap on counterfactual+retrieval; targets answer generation, not credit routing inside an optimizer. Abstract still unretrieved.

**Verdict.** Both search rounds converge: no retrieved work applies counterfactual/entanglement-aware attribution to disentangle a *reflective natural-language prompt optimizer* from a *co-evolving self-editing memory*, and none measures whether optimized instructions have become bank-dependent. The novel object here is the transplant/DiD diagnostic and the P2 claim that current practice's gain is bank-conditional; the routing rule is now positioned as the *fix implied by* the diagnostic, with CANTANTE/HiMPO/UCOB acknowledged as the mechanism's ancestors and B9 as their gradient-free stand-in. **Both search sessions were rate-limited before I could run targeted OpenReview queries on "transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation"** — the paper's most load-bearing methodological move remains the least-verified item, and I state that plainly rather than treating the silence as evidence.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Feasibility was the reviewers' main objection and is now addressed by arithmetic, not prose.** One primary environment, one primary model, 107k episode-equivalents, ~5 days on the stated node, ~$190 API, with a pre-registered cut order that never touches Part 1 or the B3/B4/B6 5-seed comparison. E3/WebShop and Qwen3-32B are cut outright; E2 and Llama-8B are demoted to best-effort directional checks that carry no claim.
2. **The method claim is under-powered if the diagnostic effect is small.** With 5 paired seeds the CCR-vs-B3 MDE is ~3.3 points; if the Part 1 interaction lands below 8 points, P5 is not testable and we say so rather than moving the goalposts. The diagnostic, which is instance-paired and cheap, carries the paper.
3. **Short-horizon tasks may give instructions little of the policy to carry.** Mitigated by ALFWorld as a directional check and by pre-stating the 2–5 point inconclusive band.
4. **Counterfactual replays assume with/without-memory episodes are comparable**, which weakens in long-horizon settings where trajectories diverge early. Mitigated by 3 decoding seeds per replay and a margin threshold; attribution κ is reported per environment.
5. **Budget matching is imperfect** — replays are cheap rollouts while baselines get extra full optimization steps. Three matched axes are reported (rollouts, wall clock, API tokens).
6. **Routed memory edits could degrade the bank**, making CCR lose even at T_mem; B7 (routing without bank edits) isolates this.
7. **Model specificity.** A model heavily trained to defer to context may co-adapt far more than one that ignores it; per-model curves, never a pooled headline. The Llama-8B replication is the only evidence on this axis and is explicitly weak.
8. **The clause classification is judge-based and subjective**; reported with human agreement on a 100-instruction subset and treated as supporting evidence for P3 only.
9. **Novelty risk is concentrated in the diagnostic**, and one targeted search query for exactly that design could not be run. If a transplant-style memory-ablation evaluation turns up as an appendix in a concurrent paper, our remaining distinct contributions are P2 (the bank-conditionality claim with shift), the mechanism separation in P6, and the noise-floor protocol.

Name: collection_policy_coupling_collapse
Title: Rich Get Richer, Twice: The Collection Policy — Not Content Quality — Drives Diversity Collapse When Self-Editing Memory and Prompt Optimization Share the Same Episodes
Short Hypothesis: Degradation in self-evolving agents is caused by the *collection policy*: the episodes that generate new memory items (and new instructions) are themselves executed while conditioned on the current memory, so retrieved items reproduce themselves and the bank's effective support contracts. Content quality is not the lever. Two sharp predictions follow. (1) At matched content volume, growth rate, task draws and write path, a bank grown from memory-OFF episodes preserves retrievable diversity and tail-task accuracy, while the standard coupled loop contracts and accrues a tail-concentrated, break-dominated harm — and content-side write gates (verification/self-consistency) do *not* fix it. (2) Coupling a second self-editing artifact to the same retrieval-conditioned episodes compounds the harm: a reflective prompt optimizer evolved against a contracting bank writes instructions that presuppose the contracted support, so the evolved instruction *transfers* the damage even when paired with a diverse bank. A 50% mixing rate of decoupled collection episodes is the one-line fix.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **The loop as a named object.** CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739, 2026) states our exact structural premise — "retrieval determines which memories receive usage signals, while updated memory bank reshape future retrieval" — and treats it as a coupling to *exploit* via joint optimization. This is the strongest adjacency and it is a competing hypothesis, not a scoop: CoEvo-Mem asserts the loop is an efficiency mechanism (usage signals concentrate the bank on what works); we assert it is a preferential-attachment pathology that costs tail coverage. Neither paper runs the arbitrating experiment, which is a decoupled-collection arm at matched content volume. "The Trap of Trajectory" (arXiv 2605.09330) also names the write-back loop, but its causal object is a *content* property (spurious feature–outcome correlations), its measurement is per-item bias, and its remedy is debiasing; it runs no decoupled-collection control and no distributional measurement.

(2) **Degradation attributed to content.** OEP (arXiv 2605.18930) shows locally-correct-but-non-transferable experiences poison the store; "Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget?" (arXiv 2605.09315) documents capability erosion across evolution channels. Both establish the phenomenon and both localize it in what was written, never in what the writes were conditioned on.

(3) **Write-time admission control.** EDV (arXiv 2606.24428), ConsistencyGate (arXiv 2607.22962), Selective Memory Retention (arXiv 2606.29178). These gate content correctness/consistency. Our claim is that a perfectly verified, non-hallucinated, non-spurious item can still be an amplification of what was already retrieved, so these gates should leave the contraction intact. They are our primary competing baseline (arm B2), and a natural stronger competitor is a *diversity*-admission gate (arm B3), which the literature has not separated from correctness gating.

(4) **Diversity collapse elsewhere in the stack.** DecentMem (arXiv 2605.22721) reports diversity collapse in self-evolving multi-agent systems but attributes it to centralized cross-agent sharing; xMemory (arXiv 2602.02007) diagnoses top-k retrieval collapsing "into a single dense region" as a retrieval-side redundancy problem, fixed by hierarchical decoupled retrieval (our read-side alternative, tested implicitly by B1/B3); "Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web" (arXiv 2602.16136) documents dominance/homogenization in RAG caused by *external* synthetic pollution. None isolates a single agent's own read→write coupling.

(5) **Model collapse.** Shumailov et al. (Nature 2024), Alemohammad et al. (Self-Consuming Generative Models Go MAD), SIGMA (arXiv 2601.03385), LLM Web Dynamics (arXiv 2506.15690) supply the formalism — diversity/tail loss under recursive self-generation and fresh-data mixing ratio as the knob — strictly in the weight-training or network-simulation regime. Transplanting it to an append-only text store is not entailed: a memory bank never overwrites the base model, so contraction can act only through retrieval competition, which is exactly why coupled-vs-decoupled collection is the right test.

(6) **Prompt optimization.** MIPRO, GEPA and reflective-evolution successors treat the prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over it. They are normally evaluated against a *static* task distribution. Our second prong asks what happens when the optimizer's own evaluation signal is generated by an agent reading a bank that the optimizer's episodes are simultaneously reshaping — the co-adaptation question the track poses, and one that no prompt-optimization paper we found tests.
Abstract: Self-evolving agents write distillations of their own episodes into a memory bank and retrieve from it on later episodes; a 2026 wave of results shows this degrades performance and attributes the degradation to a property of the written content — hallucinated, spurious, self-confirming, non-transferable — so every proposed remedy is a write-time content filter. We argue the causal variable is the collection policy, not the content. Because episodes are executed while conditioned on retrieved items, the distillations written back are downstream of what was retrieved; retrieval frequency is self-reinforcing and the bank's effective support contracts. We test this with a decoupling design: banks grown over identical cycles from identical task draws with an identical write path and identical write counts, differing only in whether the collecting episodes ran with memory in context. We then make the track's coupling question first-class by crossing that factor with a reflective prompt optimizer, giving a 2×2 over which self-editing channel is coupled to the retrieval-conditioned episodes, and we add an instruction/bank transplant test: if the optimizer's instruction has co-adapted to a contracted support, it should carry the harm to a healthy bank. We measure bank contraction (embedding effective rank, retrieval-count Gini, cluster coverage) against a size-matched random-bank null, and split downstream accuracy into head and tail task clusters with fix/break decompositions. Competing baselines are a correctness-gated write path, a diversity-gated write path, and coupled-but-random retrieval, each of which would win if the mechanism is content quality, coverage-at-write-time, or memory presence per se. A null on coupled-versus-decoupled refutes us and vindicates the content-side account; a coupled arm that beats decoupled on head accuracy with no tail deficit vindicates the "loop as efficiency mechanism" account of CoEvo-Mem. The whole design is one environment, three growth cycles, ~35k episodes on a single 4×A100 node and under $150 of API spend.
Experiments:
HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: ReAct scaffold, tool stack (a local dense+BM25 Wikipedia retriever), step limit, decoding temperature and seed schedule, the encoder and similarity function used for memory retrieval, the **deployment-time** retrieval protocol (top-k=4, identical in every arm at every evaluation), the write path (identical ExpeL-style distillation prompt and identical success criterion), the training-instance draw sequence, episodes per cycle, and items written per cycle. Arms differ only in how the *collecting* episodes were run and, in the 2×2, whether the instruction is evolved.

ENVIRONMENT (one, deliberately). E1: tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a long-tailed task mixture assembled from HotpotQA (distractor), MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA. Instances are clustered by reasoning template × entity domain into ~20 clusters by embedding k-means plus a frontier-model label on cluster centroids; the training draw distribution is skewed so the five largest clusters cover ~65% of draws. Episodes cost 4–8 model calls. ALFWorld and a second model scale are cut (see changes_made and Risk Factors); long-horizon and cross-scale generality are declared limitations, not claimed.

REGIME (declared, not hidden). Bank starts at 40 items and grows by ≤40 per cycle to ≤160 by cycle 3; deployment k=4. This is a small-bank, high-skew, low-k regime chosen so that contraction, if it exists, is measurable within three cycles. We state this as a design choice and report the measured per-cycle contraction rate so the result can be extrapolated to larger banks rather than asserted for them. The separate "accelerated stress regime" from the previous version is deleted.

MODEL. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as the agent throughout. A frontier API model performs offline distillation, prompt-optimizer reflection, and cluster labeling — identically across all arms.

CYCLE PROTOCOL. A shared cycle-0 seed bank is built per seed from 200 memory-off episodes (identical starting point for every arm within a seed). Then three growth cycles. Each cycle: draw 200 training instances (same draw sequence in every arm and seed), run the agent under the arm's collection policy, sample W=40 successful episodes uniformly at random, distill, append. W is capped at the per-seed minimum across arms if any arm cannot produce 40 successes; raw success counts are reported. Bank size trajectories are therefore identical across arms by construction.

ARMS. Core 2×2 (collection policy × instruction policy), 3 seeds each:
- A1 Coupled memory / frozen instruction — the standard self-evolving loop.
- A2 Decoupled memory / frozen instruction — collecting episodes run with NO memory in context; same tasks, same episode count, same write path, same bank size. The core control.
- A3 Coupled memory / co-evolved instruction — GEPA-style reflective optimizer evolves the ReAct system instruction each cycle using failure traces from that cycle's (memory-conditioned) episodes; both self-editing channels coupled.
- A4 Decoupled memory / co-evolved instruction — optimizer evolves against memory-off episodes; bank grown from the same episodes.

Competitors and mechanism ablations, frozen instruction, 2 seeds each:
- B1 Coupled-random-retrieval: collecting episodes still see memory, but items are sampled uniformly from the bank instead of top-k. Separates "similarity-biased retrieval is self-reinforcing" from "any injected memory contracts the bank."
- B2 Content gate (EDV/ConsistencyGate-style): fully coupled, writes must pass verification + self-consistency. If degradation is about content, B2 should track A2.
- B3 Diversity-admission gate: fully coupled, an item is written only if it increases measured bank coverage (marginal gain in effective rank / minimum distance to existing items), independent of correctness. The cheapest competing fix.
- M50 Mixing: 50% of each cycle's collecting episodes run memory-off, 50% coupled. The deployable fix.
- F0 Frozen bank: cycle-0 bank, never grown, evaluated at cycle 3 (evaluation only, no growth cost). Controls for "it is all bank size."

TRANSPLANT TEST (the co-adaptation probe, 3 seeds): evaluate A3's evolved instruction with A4's bank, and A4's evolved instruction with A3's bank. If the harm lives in the bank alone, instruction source should not matter; if the optimizer has co-adapted to a contracted support, A3's instruction should underperform A4's on tail *even on the healthy bank*.

EVALUATION. Frozen held-out test set, n=400, stratified 50/50 head (five largest clusters) / tail, fully paired at the instance level, identical seed schedule for all arms. Evaluations: cycle 0 (shared across arms, once per seed), cycle 2 (A1 and A2 only, trajectory evidence), cycle 3 (all arms + F0 + transplant cells). A no-memory frozen-instruction agent is evaluated once per seed as the common reference for fix/break tables. All results are reported stratum-wise and reweighted to the natural frequency profile. Primary endpoint: cycle-3 tail accuracy, A1 vs A2, paired. Secondary: the 2×2 interaction on tail accuracy (compounding) and the transplant contrast.

BANK-LEVEL CONTRACTION METRICS (no LLM cost; computed every cycle for every arm and seed): (a) effective rank / participation ratio of the item-embedding covariance, under two independent encoders; (b) Gini over per-item retrieval counts accumulated during collection; (c) cluster coverage — distinct clusters represented in top-k retrievals across a fixed 300-query probe set spanning all clusters; (d) redundancy — mean nearest-neighbour similarity among newly written items and novel-n-gram rate versus the cycle-0 bank; (e) size-matched random-bank null: the same metrics for an equal-size bank sampled uniformly from the union of all arms' items, resampled 100×, fixing the value each metric takes under no contraction.

MEDIATION. Mixed-effects model of tail correctness on effective rank and cluster coverage, controlling for bank size and injected token count, pooled over arms/seeds/cycles. The mechanism claim requires that entering contraction metrics substantially attenuates the coupled-arm tail deficit.

COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (the envelope is hard; here is the full accounting).
Collection/training episodes: shared seed banks 3×200 = 600; core arms 4 arms × 3 seeds × 3 cycles × 200 = 7,200; non-core arms 4 × 2 × 3 × 200 = 4,800; prompt-optimizer selection minibatches (A3, A4) 2 arms × 3 seeds × 3 cycles × 6 candidates × 40 instances = 4,320. Subtotal 16,920.
Evaluation episodes: cycle-0 shared 3×400 = 1,200; no-memory reference 3×400 = 1,200; cycle-2 (A1,A2) 2×3×400 = 2,400; cycle-3 core 4×3×400 = 4,800; cycle-3 non-core 4×2×400 = 3,200; F0 3×400 = 1,200; transplant 2 cells ×3×400 = 2,400; null replicates 4 cells ×400 = 1,600. Subtotal 18,000.
Total ≈ 34,900 episodes × ~6 calls = ~210k generations of an 8B model. On 4×A100 with vLLM (4 replicas, 32–64 concurrent episodes, 200–400 output tokens/call) this is ~4–6 GPU-hours of pure generation and ~3–4 days wall clock including local retrieval, orchestration and restarts. Frontier API: 2,520 distillation calls (~7M tokens), 108 optimizer reflection calls on long traces (~1M tokens), cluster labeling (~0.3M tokens) ≈ $120–150 total, inside the few-hundred-dollar budget. Nothing in the design is contingent on spare capacity; there are no optional arms.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) B2, correctness-gated writes under a fully coupled loop. If verified/self-consistent writes match A2 on tail accuracy and on contraction metrics, the mechanism is content quality and the write-gating literature is right. This is the most likely way the hypothesis dies.
(ii) A1 itself, in the CoEvo-Mem reading: conditioning writes on retrieval concentrates the bank on what actually gets used, an efficiency story rather than a collapse story. Signature: coupled beats decoupled on head accuracy with no tail deficit. We report this as a substantive refutation, not a null.
(iii) B3, diversity-admission gate. If a write-time coverage constraint fully substitutes for decoupling, the cheaper fix wins and "decouple the collection policy" is the wrong recommendation — the mechanism claim survives partially (contraction is the mediator) but the intervention claim does not.
(iv) F0 frozen bank. If a never-grown bank matches everything, the study is about bank size, not the loop.
(v) B1 coupled-random-retrieval. Isolates similarity-biased self-reinforcement from mere memory presence. If B1 contracts as much as A1, the amplification is not retrieval-driven and our account is wrong at the mechanism level even if the phenomenon reproduces.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.
A2 is the core control: identical tasks, episode count, write path and bank-size trajectory; self-generated content in both arms; only the feedback removed. The equalized write-count cap removes the differential-success-rate confound (raw counts also reported). The size-matched random-bank null fixes the no-contraction reference for every diversity metric, so declining effective rank cannot be an artifact of bank growth. Head/tail stratification separates "memory gets worse" from "memory gets narrower" — narrowing predicts preserved head, degraded tail, which generic degradation does not. The A3/A4 transplant cells separate contraction stored in the bank from contraction absorbed into the evolved instruction. A shuffled-provenance placebo (item texts relabelled across arms, retrieval unchanged) confirms measured differences track item content rather than bookkeeping. All arms are reported on matched collection-episode, wall-clock and injected-token axes.
Falsifiable Predictions:
If the collection-policy account holds:
1. Bank effective rank in A1 falls ≥30% from cycle 0 to cycle 3 relative to the size-matched random-bank null, while A2 falls <10%, with direction consistent across all 3 seeds and both encoders.
2. Retrieval-count Gini in A1 exceeds 0.6 by cycle 3 and top-k cluster coverage over the probe set drops ≥25%, while A2 stays flat (within the random-bank null band).
3. The downstream signature is asymmetric: at cycle 3, A1 tail accuracy is ≥6 points below A2 (paired, clears the stated MDE), while head accuracy differs by <4 points in either direction (equivalence margin, see Measurement). The harm shows up as a rising *break* count against the no-memory reference on tail instances, not merely as missing fixes.
4. Content gating does not rescue: B2's cycle-3 tail accuracy is within 3 points of A1 and its effective-rank decline is within 10 percentage points of A1's, i.e. B2 tracks A1 and not A2. B1 (random retrieval under a coupled loop) contracts substantially less than A1 (≥half the A1→A2 gap recovered), showing the amplification is retrieval-similarity-driven.
5. Mixing works with a visible, non-linear benefit: M50 recovers ≥two-thirds of the A1→A2 tail gap.
6. **Compounding (the coupling claim).** A3 (both channels coupled) has the lowest tail accuracy of the 2×2, and the negative interaction term exceeds 8 points — the honest MDE for a 2×2 interaction at our n. If the interaction is smaller than that, we report the main effects and explicitly declare the compounding claim underpowered rather than asserting it.
7. **Transplant.** A3's evolved instruction, paired with A4's diverse bank, loses ≥4 points of tail accuracy relative to A4's instruction on the same bank. This is the sharp form of co-adaptation: the instruction, not just the bank, carries the contraction.
8. Mediation: entering effective rank and cluster coverage attenuates the coupled-arm tail deficit by ≥half.

REFUTATION CONDITIONS. If A1 and A2 are indistinguishable at cycle 3 on both contraction metrics and tail accuracy, the coupling account is dead, self-generated content per se is what matters, and we report that as the primary result in support of the write-gating literature. If B2 matches A2 on all endpoints, the mechanism is content quality and our framing is wrong. If A1 beats A2 on head with no tail deficit, the loop is an efficiency mechanism (CoEvo-Mem's premise) and we say so. If B3 matches A2, the correct fix is diversity-aware writing, not decoupled collection. If contraction metrics move exactly as predicted but tail accuracy does not follow, the bank narrows without measurable downstream cost at this horizon — a real but much weaker finding, and we pre-commit to reporting it as such. If the transplant contrast is null while the bank contrast holds, contraction lives entirely in the bank and the optimizer is an innocent bystander.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Three variance sources, handled separately.

(a) EVALUATION VARIANCE. Every arm at every cycle is evaluated on the same held-out instances with the same seed schedule, so all arm comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar on paired fix/break tables, Holm-corrected across the arm family within each cycle and stratum; every delta is reported with its fix/break decomposition, because a flat net accuracy hiding growing symmetric churn is a distinct finding.

(b) BANK-TRAJECTORY VARIANCE, the source specific to this study. Core arms (A1–A4) are grown three independent times with the same training-instance draw sequence and different decoding seeds; non-core arms twice. Arm effects come from a mixed-effects logistic model with crossed random intercepts for test instance and bank trajectory; CIs from a cluster bootstrap resampling trajectories as well as instances. Because cycle 0 is by construction identical across arms, the cycle-3 arm contrast *is* a difference-in-differences and any constant trajectory offset cancels.

(c) NULL REPLICATES. Four arm-cycle cells (A1 and A2 at cycle 3, two extra decoding seeds each) are re-run with no treatment change; the distribution of apparent deltas gives the empirical noise floor. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. This is load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment. Contraction metrics have their own null: the size-matched random bank, resampled 100× per cycle.

MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECTS, and what we therefore do not claim. With 200 paired tail instances per arm-cycle-seed and an expected 12–18% discordant-pair rate, a single cell detects ≈7 points at 80% power. Pooling 3 trajectories in the mixed model, with a between-trajectory SD of 2–3 points estimated from the null replicates, the A1-vs-A2 tail contrast is detectable at ≈5–6 points; prediction 3 is stated at 6. The head stratum at the same n cannot certify equivalence tighter than ≈4 points, so "head unaffected" is an equivalence claim at a 4-point margin and anything inside that band is reported as inconclusive. The 2×2 interaction has roughly twice the standard error of a main effect, giving an MDE of ≈8–10 points; prediction 6 is stated at 8 and we pre-commit to declaring it underpowered otherwise rather than reporting a suggestive interaction as support. The transplant contrast (3 seeds, 400 paired instances, same-bank comparison) supports a ≈4-point MDE on tail. Non-core arms at 2 seeds support only ≈7–8 point contrasts and their predictions (4, 5) are stated at that resolution. The 50/50 head/tail stratification is deliberate: the natural tail frequency would leave the decisive slice underpowered; all frequency-weighted numbers are reported as reweighted estimates with their own bootstrap intervals.
Preprint Collision Check:
The literature search run for this revision returned one work that is a direct mechanistic adjacency and several partial ones.

**Closest: CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739, 2026).** It names our exact structural loop — "retrieval determines which memories receive usage signals, while updated memory bank reshape future retrieval" — and calls it a fundamental feedback loop that prior methods overlook. This is the strongest threat and I will not minimize it: the mechanistic premise is essentially identical. It does not collide on the *claim*, because CoEvo-Mem treats the loop as a resource to co-optimize and predicts it helps; we predict it is a preferential-attachment pathology whose cost is tail coverage. Neither their paper nor any other runs the arbitrating experiment — a decoupled-collection arm at matched content volume, growth rate and write path — and CoEvo-Mem reports no bank-level diversity measurement and no head/tail decomposition. Our design is set up so that CoEvo-Mem's premise is a live outcome (baseline (ii)): if coupled beats decoupled on head with no tail deficit, they are right and we say so. That said, a reviewer is entitled to read our contribution as "testing CoEvo-Mem's premise adversarially," and that is a fair characterization of prong 1.

**Partial collisions.** "The Trap of Trajectory" (arXiv 2605.09330) names the write-back loop but localizes causation in a content property (spurious correlations), measures per-item bias, and fixes it by debiasing; no decoupled control, no distributional measurement. DecentMem (arXiv 2605.22721) reports diversity collapse in self-evolving multi-agent systems but attributes it to centralized cross-agent memory sharing, a different cause with a different fix. xMemory (arXiv 2602.02007) diagnoses top-k retrieval "collapsing into a single dense region" as a static retrieval-side redundancy problem; this is the read-side alternative explanation our B1/B3 arms are designed to separate from write-side coupling. "Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web" (arXiv 2602.16136, WWW 2026) documents dominance/homogenization in RAG but from external synthetic pollution, not an internal loop. OEP (2605.18930), "Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget?" (2605.09315), EDV (2606.24428) and ConsistencyGate (2607.22962) are content-quality accounts and content-side gates; the latter two are implemented as arm B2. ReasoningBank (2509.25140) and the 2026 memory surveys (2602.06052, 2603.07670) presume the loop is benign; 2603.07670 notes that observability into which items are retrieved versus written-but-never-read is "almost entirely absent in agent memory practice," which is an engineering observation adjacent to our Gini/coverage instrumentation but not a collapse claim.

**Gap that survives the search.** No retrieved work isolates the collection policy — whether the collecting episodes were conditioned on retrieval — as the causal variable, none frames the dynamic as preferential attachment with a measurable contraction rate against a size-matched null, and none crosses it with prompt optimization or runs an instruction/bank transplant. The prompt-optimization prong appears unaddressed entirely: I found no work testing what a reflective optimizer does when its own evaluation episodes are reshaping the memory it is optimizing against.

**Honest caveat.** I could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions, and a memory-off collection ablation could plausibly appear in an appendix of a sibling preprint. If CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready contains a decoupled-collection ablation, prong 1 becomes a replication-plus-mediation result and prong 2 (compounding and transplant) carries the contribution.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Three cycles may be too short.** We deleted the separate accelerated stress regime and instead chose a primary regime (40-item seed bank, ≤160 items, k=4, strongly skewed draws) in which contraction is plausibly measurable within three cycles. This is declared, not hidden, and it bounds generality: a null at cycle 3 is evidence about this regime, and we report the measured per-cycle contraction rate so readers can extrapolate rather than assume.
2. **Single environment, single model scale.** ALFWorld and the 14B replication are cut for the compute envelope. Long-horizon and cross-scale generality are stated as limitations; the paper claims a mechanism in an 8B-class tool-QA agent, not a universal law. We would rather run one adequately powered environment than two underpowered ones.
3. **Differential success rates** change how many items each arm would write; we equalize by capping at the per-seed minimum and subsampling uniformly, which departs slightly from pure deployment practice. Both equalized and raw-count trajectories are reported.
4. **Head/tail clusters are defined by us**, and a bad definition could manufacture the asymmetry. Clusters are fixed in advance from the training pool by automatic embedding clustering plus a frontier-model label on centroids, frozen before any evaluation, with taxonomy and cluster sizes published and a human check of 150 assignments reported with kappa.
5. **Diversity metrics are encoder-dependent**; effective rank is reported under two independent encoders, and the size-matched random-bank null — not the absolute value — is the reference.
6. **The compounding claim is the least powered part of the design.** A 2×2 interaction at our n needs ~8 points to be certified; we pre-commit to reporting an unresolved interaction as unresolved. The transplant test is the better-powered route to the same co-adaptation claim, which is why it was added.
7. **Contraction without downstream cost** is a plausible outcome and much weaker; we pre-commit to reporting it as "the bank narrows without measurable cost at this horizon."
8. **The prompt optimizer is one specific reflective/evolutionary instantiation** (GEPA-style instruction evolution, 6 candidates/cycle, 40-instance selection minibatches). A different optimizer with a larger search budget might co-adapt differently; the optimizer budget is held identical across A3 and A4 so the *contrast* is clean even if the absolute optimizer strength is modest.

Name: commit_then_consult_slot_discipline
Title: Anchoring, Not Overload: Commitment Order Explains Why Optimized Instructions and Agent Experience Memory Fight Each Other
Short Hypothesis: Harm from injected agent memory is a *slot violation resolved by order*: retrieved experience that is directive (imperative procedural content) occupies the demonstration slot but functions as an instruction, and because it arrives before the agent has committed to anything, it overrides plans the agent would otherwise have executed correctly. Three consequences, all testable at fixed injected-token count. (1) Ordering fix: commit-then-consult — draft and log a plan/answer with no memory, then revise against your own logged draft plus the *identical* retrieved items — sharply cuts breaks while preserving fixes, which the injection-volume account predicts it cannot. (2) Slot fix: routing the directive content out of the memory slot into the optimizer-owned instruction slot, where GEPA vets it against a training signal, neutralizes the same harm, and the two fixes are redundant rather than additive because they target one mechanism. (3) The risky coupling prediction: prompt optimization and memory are *anti-synergistic under memory-first ordering* — a GEPA-optimized instruction gives the agent a stronger correct prior to abandon, so memory harm gets **larger**, not smaller, after instruction optimization, and the anti-synergy disappears under commit-then-consult.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **Memory-harm mechanism papers.** MemHarness (2607.28272) attributes negative transfer to verbatim replay and fixes item *content*; "When Continual Learning Moves to Memory" (2604.27003) attributes it to experiences *competing for context* (the volume account); "Selective Memory Retention" (2606.29178) fixes the *write* path; ActMem (2603.00026) attributes it to similarity-based retrieval lacking causal structure; "Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory" (2603.02473) crosses write strategies with retrievers and finds retrieval quality dominates write strategy. Every one of these changes *what is in the context*. None changes *when the agent commits relative to seeing it*, and none reports a fix/break decomposition that separates "memory failed to help" from "memory overrode a correct plan."

(2) **The mirror-image finding.** "LLM Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers" (2601.22436) shows agents often *ignore* condensed experience, tracing this to semantic limits of condensation and internal biases that suppress experience. Its causal story runs opposite to ours (under-use vs. override). It is the strongest evidence that our effect is model- and item-dependent, which is why directiveness is a measured covariate here and not an assumption: their "suppression" regime and our "override" regime should separate along it.

(3) **Retrieval gating.** MemCon (2607.13591), AdaMEM (2606.05684), "To Retrieve or To Think?" (2601.08747), and meta-cognitive memory management (2601.07470) decide *whether/when/how much* to retrieve. We always retrieve everything and change only commitment order; gating cannot preserve fixes on instances it gates away.

(4) **Draft-then-verify and knowledge-conflict RAG.** Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) is structurally the closest ancestor of our A2: draft first, then verify. It verifies against the model's own generated questions, has no external experience memory, and is a factuality method, not an adjudication between competing accounts of agent-memory harm. Astute RAG / Madam-RAG (2504.13079) generate internal-knowledge passages alongside retrieved documents and reconcile in a single pass; Self-Refine and Speculative RAG draft *after* retrieval. We do not claim draft-then-revise is new machinery. We implement the closest such method as a numbered condition (A5) and the compute-matched no-memory version as another (A4). The claim is causal and comparative — that a *logged pre-retrieval commitment*, at token-matched injection, is what removes procedural override in an agent memory loop — plus the interaction with instruction optimization, which none of this literature touches.

(5) **Prompt optimization.** MIPRO and GEPA treat a prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over both; ExpeL/Reflexion/ReasoningBank/ExpRAG (2603.18272) fill the demonstration slot from accumulated experience. The composition is deployed but unexamined: no paper we found asks whether an *optimized* instruction makes memory more or less dangerous. Our anti-synergy prediction is the direct answer, and it is the opposite of what "the two components fail on disjoint slices, so combine them" would lead one to expect.
Abstract:
Agentic memory systems retrieve distilled past experience and place it in the agent's context before it acts. A 2026 wave of results shows this frequently hurts, and every proposed remedy edits the memory: prune it, reconstruct it, restructure retrieval, or retrieve less. We propose that a large share of the harm is neither content nor volume but **order**. Retrieved experience that reads as a directive ("always search the entity page first") is instruction-shaped content sitting in the demonstration slot; presented before the agent has committed to anything, it functions as a command rather than as evidence, and the agent abandons plans it would have executed correctly. A pilot is consistent with this: injecting a retrieved bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven — a one-sided signature noise does not produce.

We test the anchoring account with an intervention that changes only ordering: **commit-then-consult**, where the agent first produces and logs a plan/answer with no memory, then sees its own logged draft alongside the *identical* retrieved items. The deciding pass contains the same memory tokens as the standard agent, so the volume account predicts no benefit. We then push the account into the space the track cares about: if the harm is instruction-shaped content in the wrong slot, then (i) routing directives into the optimizer-owned instruction slot should fix it the same way, redundantly rather than additively, and (ii) **GEPA-optimized instructions should make memory-first injection more harmful, not less**, because a better instruction is a better prior to abandon. That anti-synergy, and its disappearance under commit-then-consult, is our sharpest and riskiest prediction. Fully paired McNemar designs, null replicates, a stated minimum detectable effect, a directly implemented single-pass reconciliation baseline, a content-rewriting baseline, and a smaller-k baseline that could each refute us.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED ACROSS ALL CONDITIONS:** ReAct scaffold, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from a training split with an ExpeL-style write path, then frozen), decoding temperature and seed schedule, tool stack, step limit, prompt boilerplate. Only commitment ordering, memory variant, and instruction source differ.

**ENVIRONMENTS.** E1 (primary, carries all quantitative claims): tool-augmented multi-hop QA, HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue, agent issues search calls, 4–8 model calls/episode. E2 (replication only): ALFWorld, reduced grid, commitment is a subgoal sequence. **WebShop is dropped** — it added a third environment without a claim.

**MODELS.** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct primary (E1 + E2). Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the core E1 contrasts. **The 32B model is dropped**; the prediction is now "direction replicates on the second model," not "2 of 3." A frontier API model does offline write-path distillation, GEPA reflection, item annotation, and content rewriting — identically across conditions.

**BANK UTILITY PRECHECK (150-instance dev split).** Standard memory-first must flip ≥4% of instances wrong→right vs. no-memory; otherwise fix-preservation is untestable. We also inject the gold trajectory of the nearest training task on this dev split as an oracle ceiling on the bank's content value. Both numbers are reported, not used as gates in silence. Also on dev only: a position control (memory placed immediately before the action step rather than at context head) to rule out primacy artifacts.

**E1 CONDITION GRID (fully paired; every test instance under every condition).**
*Base-instruction ordering arm:*
- A0 No memory, single pass. Reference for all fix/break tables.
- A1 Memory-first, k=7. Standard deployment; the thing we claim is anchored.
- A2 **Commit-then-consult (ours).** Pass 1: no memory, produce answer + supporting trace, logged verbatim. Pass 2: task + own logged draft + identical k=7 items; keep or revise. Deciding-pass memory tokens identical to A1.
- A3 Draft-hidden second pass. Same two-pass structure, same memory, draft withheld. Isolates *having committed* from *getting a second pass*. Critical ablation.
- A4 Two-pass self-refine, no memory. Compute-matched, memory-free control.
- A5 **Single-pass reconciliation baseline (Astute-RAG / CoVe style; added at reviewer request).** One pass: state what you would do absent the retrieved experience, then reconcile against the k=7 items and answer. Same tokens, no logged commitment boundary. This is the cheap competitor that could beat us.
- A6 **Content-rewriting baseline (MemHarness style; added at reviewer request).** Retrieved items rewritten offline by the API model conditioned on the query, then injected memory-first. Run on a 300-instance subset for cost; reported with its own reduced MDE.
- A7 Volume fix: memory-first, k=3. The competing account's remedy and the strongest practical baseline.
- A8 Self-consistency control: A1 sampled twice with majority vote, matched to A2's call budget. Ensures the method is never credited for spending more compute.

*Coupling arm (the track's question).* One GEPA run on the train split optimizes the instruction with **no memory in the loop** (instruction-only, no demo search), producing I\*.
- G0 I\*, no memory. Isolates the optimizer's own contribution.
- G1 I\* + memory-first k=7. **The anti-synergy test.**
- G2 I\* + commit-then-consult.
- G3 **Directive routing.** An annotator extracts imperative/procedural content from bank items; a second, budget-capped GEPA run merges the surviving directives into the instruction slot; the memory slot retains episodic residue only; memory-first ordering. Tests whether the harm is *where the directive lives*.
- G4 G3 + commit-then-consult. Tests redundancy: if ordering and routing fix one mechanism, G4 ≈ G3 ≈ A2, not better than each.

**E2 (ALFWorld) grid:** A0, A1, A2, A3, A7 only, n=200, 2 seeds. Directional replication.
**Second model (Llama-3.1-8B) on E1:** A0, A1, A2, A3, G0, G1, G2, n=600, 1 seed.

**PRIMARY ANALYSIS.** For every condition, the paired fix/break table against its matched no-memory reference (A0 for the base arm, G0 for the coupling arm). Headline endpoints: (i) break count A2 vs. A1; (ii) fix count A2 vs. A1, non-inferiority at a pre-registered 2-point margin; (iii) the ordering × optimization interaction on break rate (A1−A0 vs. G1−G0). Net accuracy is secondary: a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention.

**MECHANISM READOUTS.** (a) Override rate: fraction of instances where the memory-conditioned first action differs from the no-memory first action, with accuracy conditional on divergence, for A1, A2, G1, G2. (b) Revision quality in A2/G2: helped/hurt ratio among instances the agent chose to revise. (c) Directiveness: LLM annotation of each item as imperative/directive vs. descriptive/episodic, validated against 150 human labels with Cohen's kappa; we test whether A1 break rate rises with top-1 item directiveness at controlled token count, and whether the directiveness→break slope *steepens* under I\* (the mechanism-level form of the anti-synergy claim).

**COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (hard envelope: 4×A100 80GB, days not weeks).**
E1: 13 full-n conditions × 600 = 7,800 episodes at seed 1; A6 subset 300; extra seeds — {A0,A1,A2,A3} at 3 seeds (+4,800) and {G0,G1,G2} at 2 seeds (+1,800). E1 total ≈ **14,700 episodes ≈ 125k model calls** (single-pass ≈6.5 calls/episode, two-pass ≈12). E2: 5 conditions × 200 × 2 seeds = 2,000 episodes ≈ 40k calls (longer horizons). Second model: 7 × 600 = 4,200 episodes ≈ 31k calls (8B, faster). GEPA: 2 runs × ~800 rollouts = 1,600 episodes. **Total ≈ 22,500 episodes / ~200k model calls.** At pilot-measured vLLM throughput on this node (~1.5–3k calls/hour for a 14B with tensor-parallel 2 and two replicas), this is **≈2.5–3 days of node time**, leaving headroom for reruns. API spend: ~1,000 distillation calls, ~1,350 annotation calls (1,200 items + 150 validated), ~2,100 content rewrites, ~200 long-context GEPA reflection calls ≈ **$150–250**, inside the stated budget. Cut relative to the previous version: WebShop, the 32B model, an asymmetric-revision-bar condition, a k=3 commit-then-consult condition, an oracle test condition (demoted to dev precheck), and one seed on the coupling arm.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
- A7 (k=3, memory-first): pilot evidence says retrieving less already eliminates harm. If A7 matches A2 on *both* breaks and fixes, the volume account wins and we report it.
- A5 (single-pass reconciliation, Astute-RAG/CoVe style): the reviewer-named closest existing technique, now an actual run condition. If A5 matches A2, the logged commitment boundary is doing nothing and the contribution reduces to "prompt it to consider its own view first" — a real result, reported as such.
- A6 (MemHarness-style situation-conditioned rewriting): if content rewriting beats ordering, the content account wins.
- A4 (two-pass self-refine, no memory): if it matches A2, the effect is deliberation, not ordering, and the paper collapses.
- A8 (self-consistency at matched calls): guards against crediting extra compute.
- G0 (GEPA instructions, no memory): if G0 dominates everything with memory, the practical recommendation for the track is "optimize instructions and drop the bank," which is itself a decisive answer to the division-of-labour question.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.**
- A3 (draft hidden) is the critical one: two-pass structure and memory tokens fixed, only the logged commitment removed. Any A2−A3 gap is attributable to the anchor.
- G3 vs. A1: same directive content, different slot, same ordering. Isolates slot from order.
- G4 vs. G3 and A2: tests the redundancy prediction that follows from a single mechanism. If G4 is meaningfully better than both, we have two mechanisms, not one, and say so.
- G1−G0 vs. A1−A0: the interaction, i.e. whether optimization amplifies anchoring.
- Directiveness regression and override-rate readouts: non-accuracy evidence that the failure is override rather than load.

**COST ACCOUNTING.** Every condition reported on three matched axes: agent calls, wall clock, total tokens. A2 roughly doubles E1 calls; A8 and A4 exist so the comparison is never compute-flattering.
Falsifiable Predictions:
If the anchoring/slot account is right:
1. **P1 (ordering).** A2's break count on E1 is at most half A1's (e.g. ~10% of instances → <5%), exact McNemar p<0.05, same direction across 3 seeds and on Llama-3.1-8B.
2. **P2 (fixes preserved).** A2's fix count is non-inferior to A1's within a 2-point margin. A loss of 2–3 points is pre-registered as *inconclusive*, not as success.
3. **P3 (the anchor, not the second pass).** A3 recovers less than half of A2's break reduction.
4. **P4 (anti-synergy — the risky coupling claim).** Memory-first harm is *larger* under optimized instructions: break rate of G1 (vs. G0) exceeds break rate of A1 (vs. A0) by a factor ≥1.5 and ≥3 absolute points, with a bootstrap CI on the difference-in-differences excluding zero; and G2 (vs. G0) restores the break rate to at or below A2's. Correspondingly, the directiveness→break slope is steeper under I\* than under the base instruction.
5. **P5 (redundancy).** G3's break rate is within 2 points of A2's, and G4 improves on neither by more than 2 points — one mechanism, two entry points.
6. **P6 (override signature).** A1's override rate exceeds 25% with conditional accuracy on overridden instances below unconditional no-memory accuracy; A2 cuts the override rate by ≥1/3 and raises conditional accuracy.

**REFUTATION.** If A2's break count is statistically indistinguishable from A1's at identical memory tokens, the anchoring account is dead and the volume/content accounts stand — reported as a clean negative that strengthens the competing literature.
