If A2 cuts breaks but loses >3 points of fixes, the method merely teaches the agent to ignore memory, which is no better than not retrieving. If A5 matches A2, the commitment boundary is inert and the finding is a prompt-level one. If A7 matches A2 everywhere, the recommendation reduces to "retrieve less." If P4 inverts — optimized instructions *reduce* memory harm — the division of labour is benign, GEPA and memory are complementary as the field assumes, and our slot-violation framing is wrong; that is a publishable correction to our own thesis and we will report it as one.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Fully paired: every test instance runs under every condition with the same seed schedule; all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar on paired outcome tables (A2 vs. A1 for breaks; A2 vs. A1 for fixes as non-inferiority at a 2-point margin), Holm-corrected across the condition family, with the full fix/break decomposition printed beside every delta. The interaction (P4) is a difference-in-differences of paired break proportions on the same instances, with CIs from a 10k-resample instance-level bootstrap, and confirmed by a mixed-effects logistic model with instance random intercept and terms for memory, optimization, and their product.

**NOISE FLOOR.** For each environment and model, identical conditions re-run under different decoding seeds serve as null replicates; we report the distribution of apparent deltas and claim no effect that does not exceed its 95th percentile. This is load-bearing, not decorative: prior pilot work in this setting saw 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets, and a treatment-free null replicate produced the same apparent gain as the best real treatment.

**MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT, stated per claim.**
- P1 (break endpoint, one-sided, n=600): with A1 breaks near 60/600 and a predicted halving, ~30 one-sided discordant events give power >0.9 at α=0.05. This is the best-powered arm and it carries the main claim.
- Net accuracy (secondary): with an expected 12–18% discordance rate, McNemar detects ≈4 points at 80% power. We do not claim net-accuracy effects below that.
- P2 (fix non-inferiority): detectable only to ≈3 points at this n. Pre-registered: a 2–3 point fix loss is reported as inconclusive.
- P4 (interaction): the weakest arm. With 600 instances × 3 seeds (base) / 2 seeds (coupling) pooled in the mixed model, the difference-in-differences is powered to detect roughly a doubling of break rate (e.g. 6%→12% or 10%→20%), not a 2-point shift. We therefore state P4 as a *ratio* prediction (≥1.5× and ≥3 absolute points) rather than a fine-grained one, and a CI overlapping zero is reported as inconclusive on the coupling with the ordering claim standing independently.
- E2 (n=200, MDE ≈7 points) and the second model are directional replication only; no primary claim rests on them alone.
- Directiveness annotation validated on 150 human-labelled items with Cohen's kappa; treated as supporting evidence.
Preprint Collision Check:
Grounded in the search just run plus three earlier rounds. Named closest recent work and verdicts:

- **"LLM Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers" (2601.22436) — closest, does not collide, and constrains us.** It is a controlled-intervention study of when agents fail to integrate condensed experience, but its finding is that agents *ignore or suppress* experience, attributing this to semantic limits of condensation and internal biases plus regimes where priors suffice. That is the mirror image of override. It does not manipulate commitment order, does not decompose fixes vs. breaks, and does not touch instruction optimization. Its existence is a genuine risk to P6 (there may be model/item regimes where suppression dominates override), which is exactly why directiveness is a measured covariate and why per-model curves are reported rather than pooled.
- **ActMem (2603.00026) — competing account, no collision.** Attributes negative transfer to surface-similarity retrieval and fixes it with event-centric causal memory structure; changes what is retrieved, never when the agent commits.
- **"Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory" (2603.02473, v2 Apr 2026) — closest methodologically, no collision, and partly supportive.** It crosses write strategies with retrievers and finds retrieval quality dominates write strategy. That is consistent with our pilot finding that write-path repairs neutralized but did not convert the harm; it locates the problem on the read side but never varies commitment order, and its utilization axis is retrieval quality, not slot or sequence.
- **ExpRAG (2603.18272)** is the standard inject-then-decide architecture we take as A1. **MemEvoBench (2604.15774)** is safety/poisoning-focused. **"Learning How to Remember" (ACL Findings 2026, 2601.07470)** and the **CBR-for-LLM-agents review (2504.06943)** are management/framing work. None tests ordering.
- From earlier rounds: **MemHarness (2607.28272)** (content rewriting — now implemented as A6), **"When Continual Learning Moves to Memory" (2604.27003)** (the volume account our token-matched contrast is built to adjudicate against), **MemCon (2607.13591) / AdaMEM (2606.05684) / "To Retrieve or To Think?" (2601.08747)** (gating whether/when, not order), **Astute RAG / Madam-RAG (2504.13079)** (single-pass reconciliation — now implemented as A5), **Speculative RAG / Self-Refine** (drafting after retrieval — A4).
- **Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) — flagged by a reviewer, added here, and conceded as the closest structural ancestor.** CoVe drafts then verifies, so we do not claim draft-then-revise as new machinery. CoVe verifies against self-generated questions with no external experience store, targets factuality, and never compares token-matched orderings or adjudicates competing accounts of agent-memory harm. We now run its nearest agent-memory analogue (A5) as a numbered condition rather than distinguishing it in prose.

**Honest gap.** The search budget was again exhausted before an OpenReview/ICLR-2026 and ACL/EMNLP-2025-26 proceedings sweep for "plan-before-memory" or "ordering ablation" appendices. I assume a nontrivial probability that a draft-then-consult ordering appears as an appendix ablation somewhere. Nothing retrieved in either round isolates ordering/commitment timing as the causal lever, and nothing at all reports the ordering × instruction-optimization interaction (P4), which is now the paper's sharpest claim and, on current evidence, unclaimed.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Zero-fix bank.** If the bank produces essentially no fixes, as in the pilot, the fix-preservation half of the claim is untestable. The dev-split utility precheck and oracle ceiling detect this; we report both rather than proceeding quietly.
2. **A5 may suffice.** The single-pass reconciliation baseline is now in the grid precisely because it might match A2. If it does, our contribution shrinks to a prompt-level finding plus the coupling result. We took that risk deliberately rather than leaving the competitor in prose.
3. **Compute asymmetry.** A2 roughly doubles E1 calls. A4 and A8 control for it, but the honest framing is "ordering is a cheaper fix than curation, not a free one."
4. **P4 is the least-powered arm.** The interaction is powered to detect a doubling of break rate, not a small shift, and rests on a single GEPA run per arm — the optimized instruction I\* is one draw, so a null could be an artifact of that draw. We report I\*'s own gain (G0 vs. A0) and the per-seed break rates so the reader can judge; we do not claim a null interaction as evidence of no coupling.
5. **Suppression regimes.** Per 2601.22436, some models under-use rather than over-follow experience. In such a regime A1 breaks will be low and P1 becomes untestable, not false. The precheck exposes this before the grid runs, and strong model dependence is reported as a finding, not averaged away.
6. **Coarse commitment in ALFWorld.** A pass-1 plan may be too vague to anchor. We require a concrete subgoal sequence and report E2 separately rather than pooling.
7. **Order and volume are not fully separable internally.** Token-matching controls the input, not the model's internal attention allocation, so a strong A2 result is evidence for ordering rather than proof; the override-rate and directiveness readouts triangulate.
8. **Prompt-surface tuning.** The pass-2 and routing prompts are fixed in advance on a 100-instance dev split and reported verbatim; A5 checks whether a much simpler single-pass variant suffices.
9. **Negative-result exposure.** If ordering does nothing, the contribution rests on the measurement protocol and on the coupling result — which is why null replicates and per-claim MDEs are load-bearing.

Name: compile_dont_retrieve
Title: Compile, Don't Retrieve: The Query-Conditioned Read in Agentic Experience Memory Is Inert
Short Hypothesis: The per-query, query-conditioned read in agentic experience memory contributes nothing. At matched token budget and matched offline compute, experience items retrieved *for this query* are worth no more than (a) items retrieved for a **different** query, (b) a **single fixed set** of items chosen once and prepended to every query, or (c) **no items at all** when the same bank has been compiled offline into one fixed instruction. This holds even though the agent demonstrably reads and imitates the injected items at comparable rates in every condition — the dissociation between following and benefit is the core evidence. Consequence: the value of an experience bank is a query-independent prior, so retrieval-time injection is strictly dominated (equal accuracy, higher per-query tokens, defeated prefix caching, plus an entire vector-store stack), and the ablation row in ExpeL that credits retrieved trajectories should not survive a token-matched control.
Related Work:
**(1) Query-conditioned experience memory — the target class.** ExpeL (AAAI 2024, arXiv:2308.10144) is canonical and, critically, already contains *both* halves of the question: a query-independent global insight list and a query-conditioned set of retrieved successful trajectories, with an ablation crediting both. A-Mem (NeurIPS 2025) organizes memories dynamically and retrieves top-k per query, explicitly selling selective top-k retrieval as the source of its token efficiency. Agent Workflow Memory (ICML 2025, arXiv:2409.07429) induces reusable workflows and "selectively provides" them per query. Retention/admission policies and consolidation methods (e.g., Auto-Dreamer, arXiv:2605.20616, which consolidates offline but keeps retriever and schema fixed; Structured Distillation, arXiv:2603.13017, which compresses "with retrieval preservation") are all downstream of the same premise. **None of them reports a control in which the same bank is delivered query-independently at equal token cost.** That missing control is the paper.

**(2) The mirror-image claim — that we need *more* conditioning.** "Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved" (arXiv:2606.06036) argues fixed-set passive retrieval is *insufficient* and replaces it with a stateful, query-specific reconstruction policy, reporting large prompt-token savings. Its premise is exactly the negation of ours: query-specificity is the payload and should be increased. Our decoy and fixed-prefix arms test that premise directly.

**(3) Compilation as a method — the nearest positive-result work.** "Atlas" (arXiv:2603.15666) states "memory is distillation, not storage; delivery is instruction rewriting, not context injection," and implements compilation of experience into the system prompt, reporting gains on CUAD. Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952, EACL 2026) maintains one persistent cheatsheet shared across queries rather than per-item retrieval. These build the replacement; **neither shows that the thing being replaced was contributing zero.** They are consistent with "retrieval carries real query-specific information that compilation delivers better." Our claim is stronger and discriminable: correct retrieval is worth no more than decoy retrieval at matched tokens. Atlas-style accounts predict a correct-vs-decoy gap; we predict none. That is a measurable disagreement, and it is prediction 2.

**(4) Simplicity results on the write path.** "Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience" (arXiv:2603.18272) finds elaborate memory pipelines barely beat a plain trajectory-retrieval baseline, echoing Wei et al. (2025). This deflates *write-path complexity* while leaving the *read channel* untouched — it makes plain retrieval the baseline to beat, and we ask whether even plain retrieval's conditioning does anything.

**(5) Experience-following.** "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (ACL 2026; arXiv:2505.16067) formalizes memory reading as top-K retrieval of query–execution pairs used as demonstrations and shows agents follow retrieved experience, sometimes harmfully. If following drives outcomes, decoys retrieved for the wrong query must change accuracy. We predict following without benefit. Same episodes, two measurements, opposite predictions.

**(6) Length effects.** "Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval" (Findings of EMNLP 2025, arXiv:2510.05381) establishes the *cost* side — length degrades performance even with masked distractors. Context Rot (Chroma, 2025) qualifies it: needle–haystack similarity modulates harm. We take the cost side as settled prior work and test the *value* side, which neither addresses.

**Positioning.** Not a memory method, not a length study. A negative identification result about a component that four distinct research programs treat as load-bearing, plus the token-matched control that would have caught it, plus a deployment consequence (a fixed prefix is prefix-cacheable; a per-query retrieval is not).
Abstract: Agentic memory systems store distilled experience and retrieve it per query at inference. Whole subfields now optimize what to store, how to organize it for retrieval, and how to make retrieval more query-specific. We test whether the query-conditioning is doing anything at all. Our claim: at matched token budget, an experience item retrieved *for this query* is worth no more than one retrieved for a different query, or one from a single fixed set prepended to every query — and no more than nothing at all, once the same bank has been compiled offline into one fixed instruction. Three named accounts disagree with us and with each other: reconstruction-style memory (arXiv:2606.06036) says conditioning should be *increased*; compilation-as-method (Atlas, arXiv:2603.15666) says conditioning carries real content that instruction rewriting merely delivers better; experience-following (arXiv:2505.16067) says agents imitate retrieved experience and therefore its identity must matter. All three predict a correct-vs-decoy accuracy gap. We predict none, together with a high following rate on decoys, so that "the agent ignored them" is refuted rather than assumed. The centerpiece is a paired, compute-matched grid on WebShop (n=500, graded reward): P1, a GEPA-compiled instruction distilled from the bank with **no inference-time retrieval**; P2, the same optimizer run jointly with live top-k retrieval, which is what agent frameworks deploy; P3, P2's instruction with token-matched decoys drawn for a different query; and, holding *format* fixed rather than only tokens, A1(7) correct top-k versus A2(7) decoys versus A3(7) a single fixed prefix identical across all test queries. A search-free naive compiler (single-pass summarization, no optimization) is included so that a null cannot be attributed to GEPA's search power. We then decompose ExpeL on ALFWorld, where it published and whose code separates a global insight list from retrieved trajectories, and predict that deleting the retrieved-trajectory channel costs nothing while removing ~70% of injected memory tokens. Everything is fully paired, with seed-pair null replicates fixing the noise floor, pre-registered MDEs, and TOST for every equivalence claim. A pre-registered slice search is our own serious attempt to break the strong claim; if a slice survives, we report routing instead of deletion.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT:** ReAct scaffold, tool stack, step limit, dense retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from the training split via an ExpeL-style write path — raw successful trajectories plus distilled insights — then frozen), decoding temperature and seed schedule, and for the P-conditions the offline optimization budget (identical iteration count, identical dev-set size, identical reflection model, identical instruction token cap). Only the inference-time memory channel and the instruction differ. Every test instance runs under every condition (fully paired).

**PRIMARY MODEL:** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. A frontier API model is the offline reflection/optimizer and write-path distiller, identically across arms, and is never in the inference loop.

---

**CENTERPIECE — E1, WebShop, n=500, graded reward + binary success.** Chosen as primary because it is genuinely sequential and agentic (so the result is not a restatement of static-QA length effects) and because graded reward buys power that ALFWorld's 134 unseen tasks cannot.

*Conditioning block — format held fixed, only conditioning varies (base, unoptimized instruction):*
- **A0** no memory.
- **A1(3), A1(7)** query-conditioned top-k. Canonical deployed read.
- **A2(7)** per-query decoys: items retrieved for a randomly drawn *different* test query from a disjoint task family, token-matched within 5%.
- **A3(7)** **fixed prefix**: one set of seven items chosen once from the bank (highest mean retrieval score across the dev split), identical for every test query, same format and token count as A1(7). *This is the cleanest conditioning ablation in the paper: identical format, identical tokens, only "was this chosen for you" varies. It is also the deployable alternative, because a fixed prefix is prefix-cacheable and a per-query retrieval is not.*
- **A2u(7)** decoys drawn from a structurally different environment's bank, token-matched — separates environment-generic procedure from query-specific content, and measures the similarity-modulation that Context Rot predicts.
- **A5** oracle: gold trajectory of the nearest training task. Upper bound on the value of conditioning.
- **A6** cross-encoder rerank of a 30-candidate pool to k=1. Best practical conditioning signal short of oracle.

*Compilation block — matched offline compute:*
- **P0** GEPA-optimized instruction, optimizer **blind to the bank**, no retrieval. Controls for "it's just prompt optimization."
- **P1** GEPA-optimized instruction, optimizer **reads the bank** as reflection material, no inference-time retrieval. Instruction capped at the median token count of one retrieved item.
- **P1n** **naive compiler**: single-pass LLM summarization of the bank into an instruction under the same token cap, **no search at all**, no dev-set feedback. Isolates "compilation as a strategy" from "GEPA's optimization power." A P1n ≈ P2 result is strictly stronger than P1 ≈ P2 and we will say so.
- **P2** GEPA-optimized instruction evolved **jointly with live top-3 retrieval**. What agent frameworks deploy.
- **P3** P2's instruction with token-matched decoys at test time.

13 conditions. Decisive set {A0, A1(7), A2(7), A3(7), P0, P1, P1n, P2, P3} × 2 decoding seeds; the seed pair doubles as the null replicate. Supporting {A1(3), A2u(7), A5, A6} × 1 seed. **11,000 episodes**, ~10 steps each ≈ 110k calls at ~2.5k prefill. ~1.5 node-days with vLLM tensor-parallel and continuous batching.

---

**PUBLISHED-RESULT RE-EXAMINATION — E2, ALFWorld, n≈234 (134 unseen + 100 held-out seen), binary success.** ALFWorld is where ExpeL published and its code is released, removing reimplementation-fidelity risk.
- **B1** ExpeL full: global insights + retrieved successful trajectories (published config).
- **B2** insights only, retrieved trajectories deleted.
- **B3** retrieved trajectories only, insights deleted.
- **B4** insights + **decoy** trajectories, token-matched to B1.
- **B5** insights + **fixed-prefix** trajectories (one set for all tasks), token-matched to B1.
Plus **A0, P1, P2** for directional replication. 8 conditions × 234 × 1 seed = **1,872 episodes** × ~25 steps ≈ 47k calls at ~4k prefill. ~1.1 node-days.
Clean contrasts: B1 vs B4 and B1 vs B5 (identical tokens and format, differ only in conditioning) and B1 vs B2 (does the channel earn its tokens at all).
**Fidelity gate:** B1 must reproduce ExpeL's published ordering over a no-memory ReAct baseline on ALFWorld unseen, at our model scale, on a dev split. If it does not, we report ExpeL as unreproduced at 14B and withdraw the re-examination rather than reinterpret a failed reproduction.

---

**TIGHT-BOUND ENVIRONMENT — E3, tool-augmented multi-hop QA (HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue), n=600, binary EM.** ~6 calls/episode, so this is where our narrowest equivalence intervals live. Conditions: A0, A1(7), A2(7), A3(7), P0, P1, P1n, P2. Decisive 5 × 2 seeds + 3 × 1 seed = **7,800 episodes** ≈ 47k short calls. ~0.6 node-day.

---

**MODEL REPLICATION.** Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on E1, six conditions {A0, A1(7), A2(7), A3(7), P1, P2}, 1 seed, with separately optimized instructions (prompts do not transfer): **3,000 episodes**, ~0.4 node-day.

**OFFLINE OPTIMIZATION COST.** Each GEPA-produced instruction: ~20 iterations against a 300-episode dev split disjoint from test. 3 GEPA variants (P0/P1/P2) × 3 environments + 2 variants × 1 environment (8B) = 11 runs ≈ **3,300 dev episodes**, ~0.5 node-day. P1n costs one API call. k* for A1 and the fixed-prefix selection for A3 are tuned on the same dev split, so the retrieval arm is not disadvantaged on tuning. **We report GEPA optimization curves for P2**, so that a null P2−P1 cannot be attributed to an under-converged optimizer that never learned to exploit the retrieval channel.

**TOTAL: ~27,000 episodes, ~4.5 node-days.** Frontier API: ~900 GEPA reflection + ~1,500 write-path distillation + ~500 ExpeL insight extraction + ~50 naive-compilation calls ≈ 3,000 calls, under $250.

---

**DROPPED, AND WHY.**
- *A-Mem and other curation reimplementations.* If the read channel is inert, every method that optimizes retrieval is downstream of a component we show does nothing. Reimplementing three of them from paper text was also the largest soundness threat in review. Replaced by ExpeL, which is released and already decomposes along exactly the axis we test.
- *Padded-single / truncated-seven and the random-token filler control.* These adjudicate the *cost* mechanism (attention load vs. exemplar interference), which arXiv:2510.05381 already settles better than we could and which changes no recommendation we make.
- *The mixed-effects token-coefficient regression as a headline.* Demoted to a supporting budget curve.
- *A1(1) and the full injection-budget sweep.* Cost-side, prior work.

---

**ANALYSIS.**
(a) **The conditioning table.** Paired deltas, 95% bootstrap CIs, and TOST equivalence tests for: A1(7)−A2(7), A1(7)−A3(7), A1(7)−A2u(7), P2−P3, P2−P1, P2−P1n, P1−P0, B1−B2, B1−B4, B1−B5. Each row prints the measured noise floor and median injected memory tokens beside the delta.
(b) **Experience-following, the discriminator.** For every memory-injecting condition: rate at which the agent's emitted actions reuse actions, entity strings, or phrasings from injected items (exact + fuzzy n-gram match on actions, plus LLM-judge paraphrase check on a 200-episode sample). Reported *jointly* with the accuracy delta on the same episodes. The predicted dissociation — following high on decoys and fixed prefixes, accuracy flat — is what separates us from arXiv:2505.16067, from Atlas, and from the reconstruction account.
(c) **Accuracy per injected memory token, plus a serving ledger.** Median prefill tokens, retrieval calls, and — for the fixed-prefix and compiled arms — the fraction of prompt eligible for prefix-cache reuse, with measured TTFT under vLLM prefix caching. The deployment claim is not just "fewer tokens" but "cacheable tokens."
(d) **Pre-registered slice search against ourselves.** Five slicings fixed in advance: retrieval-score quartile, task family, episode-length quartile, oracle-availability (does a near-identical training task exist), P1-failure set. Does any slice show A1(7) or P2 beating A3(7)/P1 by more than the noise floor after Holm correction? A survivor converts the recommendation from "delete retrieval" to "route to retrieval on slice X."
(e) **Subsumption check.** Semantic overlap between the compiled P1 instruction and the content of retrieved items, to report *what* got amortized (procedure? failure modes? tool syntax?), not merely that it did.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
- **A1(7) over A3(7)/A2(7).** The single most direct refutation: same format, same tokens, only conditioning varies. If correct retrieval beats a fixed prefix by more than the noise floor, conditioning carries information and the paper's central claim is dead.
- **P2 (coupled optimizer + retrieval).** The deployed design. Beating P1 by more than the noise floor at matched offline compute vindicates coupling; we report that as the headline if it happens.
- **A5 (oracle nearest-gold trajectory).** Upper bound on conditioning. If the oracle is also flat, conditioning has no headroom even with a perfect retriever. If the oracle wins big while A1/A6 do not, the finding becomes "retrievers are the bottleneck," a different and also publishable paper we would report as such.
- **A6 (cross-encoder rerank to k=1).** Wins if content *selection* is the lever.
- **B1 (ExpeL full).** Must clear the fidelity gate; if it then survives B2, B4, and B5 at matched tokens, its published ablation stands and we report a failed challenge.
- **P0 (bank-blind optimized instruction).** The uncomfortable baseline for us: P1 ≈ P0 means the bank contributes nothing even after compilation, and the conclusion becomes the bleaker "experience banks add nothing over prompt optimization at this scale." We commit to leading with that if it occurs.
- **P1n (search-free naive compiler).** Insurance against the compiler-adequacy confound in the direction that matters. If P1n ≈ P2, no one can attribute the null to GEPA's search power; if P1n ≪ P1 ≈ P2, the honest conclusion narrows to "compilation works but requires real optimization," and we report the narrower claim.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.** A1 vs A2 removes conditioning at fixed tokens; A1 vs A3 removes conditioning at fixed tokens *and* fixed format and fixed item identity across queries; A2u checks whether what survives is environment-generic procedure; P2 vs P3 repeats the swap under a learned instruction; B1–B5 replicate the entire logic inside a published method on its own benchmark.

**CONSTRUCTIVE PAYLOAD.** Two, both already conditions in the grid: A3(7) — keep the format, delete the retriever, cache the prefix — and P1 — compile the bank, delete the memory channel entirely. Per-query cost (tokens, retrieval calls, cache-hit fraction, TTFT) is reported alongside accuracy for both.

**MANIPULATION CHECKS.** (i) Experience-following rate in every injecting condition, so decoy and fixed-prefix arms cannot be dismissed as ignored text. (ii) Shuffled-bank sanity check confirming the retriever functions and A1's items are genuinely on-query. (iii) Per-instance token accounting, published, so budget matching is auditable. (iv) GEPA optimization curves for P2, so a null is not an under-convergence artifact.
Falsifiable Predictions:
1. **Conditioning is inert at fixed tokens and fixed format.** A1(7) − A2(7) and A1(7) − A3(7) both fall below the measured noise floor and pass TOST at ±3 points (WebShop reward ±0.03; QA ±4 points). Equivalently: ≥80% of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives replacement by decoys, and ≥80% survives replacement by a single fixed prefix. *Refuted if either gap exceeds the noise floor.*
2. **The same holds under a learned instruction.** P2 − P3 falls below the noise floor. *Refuted otherwise.* This is the arm that separates us from Atlas-style accounts, which hold that retrieval carries real content merely delivered badly.
3. **Dissociation from experience-following.** Following rate on decoys and on the fixed prefix is ≥70% of following rate on correctly retrieved items — the agent reads and imitates them — while the accuracy delta is within noise. *Refuted if following on decoys is near zero, which would make predictions 1–2 vacuous, and we say so in advance.*
4. **Compilation matches coupling.** P2 − P1 ≤ 3 points, passing TOST at ±3 (WebShop) / ±4 (QA), with P1 injecting ≥3× fewer memory tokens per query and requiring zero retrieval calls. *Refuted if P2 − P1 > 3 points.*
5. **Compilation does not depend on optimizer strength.** P1n (search-free) falls within noise of P1 in at least two of three environments. *If violated, we report the narrower claim "compilation works, but only with real offline search."*
6. **ExpeL's retrieval channel does not earn its tokens.** B1 − B2, B1 − B4, and B1 − B5 all fall below the noise floor while B2 injects ~70% fewer memory tokens than B1. *Refuted if removing or decoying retrieved trajectories costs more than the noise floor.*
7. **The bank does contribute, query-independently.** P1 − P0 exceeds the noise floor in at least two of three environments. *If violated, the stronger negative result stands and becomes the headline.*
8. **No rescue slice.** No pre-registered slicing yields A1(7) or P2 beating A3(7)/P1 by more than the noise floor after Holm correction. *Refuted by any survivor, which converts the recommendation from "delete retrieval" to "route to retrieval on slice X."*
9. **Serving dominance.** A3(7) and P1 lie on the accuracy-per-injected-token frontier with ≥60% of their memory tokens prefix-cacheable; all query-conditioned arms are interior and cache 0% of their memory tokens.

**REFUTATION SUMMARY.** The strong claim dies if any of: A1(7) beats A2(7) or A3(7) above noise; P2 beats P3 above noise; P2 > P1 + 3 pts; B1 beats B2/B4/B5 above noise; a pre-registered slice survives correction. Each failure localizes value somewhere specific — in conditioning, in retriever quality, in an identifiable slice — and yields a different, still-reportable paper. We commit in advance to the grid and to reporting whichever occurs.
Measurement and Noise Control:
**Paired design.** Every test instance runs under every condition on the same seed schedule; all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests: exact McNemar on fix/break counts for binary outcomes (ALFWorld success, QA EM, WebShop success); Wilcoxon signed-rank plus paired bootstrap for WebShop graded reward. Holm correction within each pre-registered comparison family (the conditioning table is one family; the slice search is another).

**Noise floor.** Each decisive condition in E1 (9) and E3 (5) carries a null replicate — identical condition, different decoding seed — and we report the full distribution of apparent deltas. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. Pilot work in this exact setting produced 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets, and a null replicate with no treatment once reproduced the apparent gain of the best real treatment. This protocol is load-bearing, not decorative.

**Minimum detectable effect, pre-registered.** WebShop, n=500 paired, graded reward with expected per-instance difference sd ≈ 0.25: MDE ≈ 0.031 reward (~3 points) at 80% power, α=0.05; binary success MDE ≈ 4–5 points. QA, n=600 paired, expected discordant rate 12–18%: MDE ≈ 4 points. ALFWorld, n≈234: MDE ≈ 7–8 points — we state plainly that **ALFWorld cannot support equivalence claims** and carries only the ExpeL contrast direction plus directional replication.

**Equivalence, not absence of significance.** Every "matches" claim (predictions 1, 2, 4, 5, 6) is tested with TOST at pre-registered margins: ±3 points WebShop, ±4 points QA. A non-significant McNemar is never reported as a null.

**Auditability.** Every reported delta ships with (a) its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding large symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention; (b) median and IQR of injected memory tokens per instance; (c) the measured following rate; (d) for the P-arms, the optimizer's dev-set curve.

**Compute parity and the asymmetry we do not hide.** P0, P1, P2 receive identical optimizer iterations, dev-set size, reflection model, and token cap; k* for A1 and the fixed-prefix choice for A3 are tuned on the same dev split. P1 spends offline search that A1 does not; A3 spends essentially none, which is why A3 rather than P1 carries the cleanest version of the conditioning claim. The full compute ledger for every arm is published.
Preprint Collision Check:
This round's search returned eight relevant items across nine queries. Two collide materially; I report both and how the claim was changed in response.

**Hard collision on the *method*, not the *claim*: "Atlas" (arXiv:2603.15666).** Its thesis — "memory is distillation, not storage; delivery is instruction rewriting, not context injection" — is functionally the mechanism our P1 condition instantiates, and it is already a working system with an ablation, reporting token-F1 gains on CUAD. **This preempts any framing of ours in which compiling-to-instruction is the contribution.** It does not preempt the claim we now make. Atlas shows compilation *works*; it does not show that the query-conditioned read it replaces contributes *zero*. Those are different statements and they make different predictions: Atlas's account is fully consistent with retrieval carrying real query-specific content that instruction rewriting merely delivers more cheaply, and therefore predicts that correct retrieval beats token-matched decoys. We predict it does not. Predictions 1–3 are the test, and Atlas has not run them. Honest exposure: if that group adds a decoy or fixed-prefix arm, predictions 1–2 are scooped and the paper narrows to the ExpeL decomposition plus the following/benefit dissociation. I could not independently verify Atlas's venue or authorship beyond the introduction section the search returned, and I flag that rather than paper over it.

**Direct counter-hypothesis: "Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved" (arXiv:2606.06036).** Argues passive fixed-set retrieval is *insufficient* and installs a stateful, query-specific reconstruction policy. This is the negation of our claim and a live threat to significance: if the field's momentum is toward more conditioning, our null must be robust. It also gives us a clean adversary — A3(7), a fixed set identical for every query, is precisely the object that paper says is inadequate. We report that contrast whichever way it lands.

**Adjacent but distinct: "Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience" (arXiv:2603.18272, March 2026).** Finds elaborate memory pipelines provide limited improvement over a simple experience-retrieval baseline, consistent with Wei et al. (2025). This deflates *write-path complexity* and leaves the read channel intact; it makes plain retrieval the baseline we must beat rather than a claim we duplicate. **Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952, EACL 2026)** maintains one persistent cross-query cheatsheet — closest in spirit to a compiled artifact, but presented as a method with its own gains, with no controlled removal of conditioning. **Auto-Dreamer (arXiv:2605.20616)** consolidates offline but keeps the retriever and schema fixed. **Structured Distillation (arXiv:2603.13017)** compresses "with retrieval preservation" — explicitly protecting the component we test.

**Targets, not collisions.** A-Mem (NeurIPS 2025) and AWM (ICML 2025, arXiv:2409.07429) are exemplars of the query-conditioned paradigm; ExpeL (arXiv:2308.10144) is re-examined directly from released code. "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (arXiv:2505.16067) is the closest empirical study and the account prediction 3 is designed to discriminate against. "Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance" (arXiv:2510.05381) supersedes the volume-not-content claim an earlier version of this proposal had as its headline — which is precisely why the headline moved to the value side.

**Correction carried forward.** An earlier round of this proposal cited MemHarness (2607.28272), MRAgent (2606.06036 under a different title), RecMem (2605.16045), AtomicRAG (2604.20844) and Distractor-Aware Truncation (2608.03297). None was re-verified in this round's search and all have been removed from the positioning, along with the reimplementation that a headline prediction depended on. Note also that arXiv:2604.04373 ("Decocted Experience"), flagged as the closest threat in the prior round, **was not returned by this round's search and I no longer rely on it.** I would rather lose a re-examination row than build one on a citation I cannot confirm.

**Gap statement, as a claim about this search and not proof of absence.** Across these nine queries, no paper runs a token-matched, format-matched control in which experience items retrieved for the current query are replaced by decoys or by a single fixed prefix inside an existing published memory system, and none pairs such a swap with a measured experience-following rate to dissociate imitation from benefit. The search's own gap statement independently identifies exactly this: "a controlled, token-matched ablation across multiple existing published agentic-memory systems that swaps their per-query retrieval step for a single fixed compiled instruction of equal token cost and shows the accuracy delta is statistically zero" does not appear to exist. Coverage is nine queries, not exhaustive. An appendix-level insights-only ablation inside a recent memory paper would shrink prediction 6 from a correction to a confirmation; predictions 1–3 would stand.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Compiler adequacy — partially, not fully, defused.** P1 ≈ P2 could mean GEPA is a good compiler rather than that conditioning is inert. P1n (search-free naive compilation) bounds this from below, P0 bounds it from above, and the A1/A2/A3 block sidesteps compilation entirely by holding format fixed. That block, not P1, is now the claim's load-bearing evidence, precisely because it involves no compiler at all. Residual risk: all our compilers are LLM-based single-instruction artifacts, and a different delivery format (e.g., a learned routing policy) might extract more.
2. **Optimizer under-exploitation of the retrieval channel.** If GEPA never learns to use retrieved trajectories well, P2 underperforms its ceiling and we mistake that for inertness. We publish P2's optimization curve and require it to have plateaued; P2 vs. P3 (fixed instruction, swapped content) is immune to this by construction.
3. **P1 could win for the wrong reason.** If P1 ≈ P2 ≈ P0, the finding is about prompt optimization, not memory. P0 is in the decisive set and prediction 7 states the condition explicitly; we commit to leading with "experience banks add nothing over bank-blind prompt optimization at 14B" if that is what we see.
4. **Decoy and fixed-prefix validity.** Off-query items might simply be more ignorable. The following-rate check bounds this, A2u gives a second reference point, and A3 (which uses genuinely high-quality, dev-selected items, just not query-selected) is the hardest version to dismiss. A near-zero following rate on decoys makes predictions 1–2 vacuous, and we say so up front.
5. **Bank quality.** If A5 (oracle) is also flat, the bank has no exploitable content and the claim is trivially true in a way that will not generalize to richer banks. The oracle is reported first in the table for this reason.
6. **Environment scope.** Three environments; only WebShop and QA carry point estimates. ALFWorld at n≈234 is under-powered by design (MDE 7–8 points) and can confirm or fail to confirm direction only. We chose depth over breadth because equivalence claims are the product and cannot survive being spread thin. A directional conflict between ALFWorld and WebShop will be reported, not dropped.
7. **Model scope.** Two open-weight models (8B, 14B). "Conditioning becomes useful at frontier scale" is a live possibility we cannot exclude and will not claim a trend from two points.
8. **Refusals, stated plainly.** We declined reviewer requests for (a) additional curation baselines (ReasoningBank, conflict-pruning, a third method) — coverage, not identification: if the read channel is inert, curating it is moot, and the right deliverable is the missing control that each of those papers can run against, not three shaky reimplementations; (b) a random-token filler control — it adjudicates whether token cost is attention load or exemplar interference, a question arXiv:2510.05381 answers better and whose answer changes no recommendation here; (c) a second full prompt-optimizer (MIPRO alongside GEPA) — we accepted the cheaper and more informative version of that request, the search-free naive compiler, and moved the claim's weight onto the compiler-free A1/A2/A3 contrast instead, which makes optimizer identity irrelevant to predictions 1–3; (d) promoting ALFWorld to full-power co-primary — n≈234 caps MDE at 7–8 points and no framing fixes that.
9. **The claim deliberately over-reaches.** "Query-conditioning buys nothing" is stronger than our pilot supports and stronger than the complementarity result this track previously reported. That is intentional. The pre-registered slice search (prediction 8) is a serious attempt to break it, and the modal honest outcome is a narrow surviving slice and a routing recommendation rather than a deletion recommendation. We would rather state the strong version and lose part of it on record than state the safe version and be unfalsifiable.
10. **What changes if we are right, and who has to check it.** ExpeL's ablation table credits retrieved trajectories; that row would have to be revised, and the retrieval channel deleted for ~70% fewer injected memory tokens at no accuracy cost. A-Mem, AWM, Auto-Dreamer, Structured Distillation, and retention/admission-policy work would each owe a fixed-prefix control at equal token cost — a baseline none currently runs. Reconstruction-style memory (arXiv:2606.06036), whose entire premise is that retrieval is not query-specific *enough*, would need to show its gains survive against a fixed prefix. Atlas's compilation gains would be reinterpreted: not better delivery of real content, but removal of a channel that was never delivering any. And frameworks that hand an optimizer and a memory the same inference context should move the bank offline. Serving-side, the fixed-prefix result is directly checkable by anyone: prefix-cache hit rate goes from 0% to ≥60% of memory tokens.

Name: counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise
Title: Does Counterfactual Screening of Agent Memory Survive Its Own Noise? Neighborhood-Conditional Utility, Winner's Curse, and Interference
Short Hypothesis: Self-editing agent memory harms accuracy because the write path assigns credit from episode outcome or reflective self-assessment, signals that are near-uninformative about whether injecting an item will help future queries. The right admission criterion is an item's *measured marginal utility inside the deployed injection context*, estimated by leave-one-out from the actual top-k bundle and averaged over the queries that actually retrieve the item (its retrieval neighborhood) rather than over a global validation sample. But — and this is the load-bearing half — per-item utility estimates at realistic probe budgets are so noisy that naive "keep if measured utility > 0" selection is selection-on-noise: its projected gain is substantially illusory (winner's curse), empirical-Bayes shrinkage recovers part of it, and the residual gap that shrinkage does *not* explain is non-additive interference among co-injected items. We measure the two components separately rather than assuming either.
Related Work:
**Write-time heuristics.** ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024) and Reflexion (Shinn et al., NeurIPS 2023) write insights and trajectories into a bank keyed on episode success and reflective self-assessment; ReasoningBank-style 2025 systems distill reasoning strategies from both successes and failures. In all of them an item is admitted because a reflector judged it insightful, never because injecting it was measured to help a future query.

**Content-side memory management.** Existing memory managers prune by recency, frequency, contradiction, or embedding redundancy. These are the cheapest possible competitors to any outcome-based screen and, following review, one is now an implemented end-to-end cell (embedding-redundancy + recency pruning at matched bank size), not a citation. If deduplication alone repairs the bank, our screen is not worth its probe cost and we say so.

**Global validation scoring of demonstrations.** MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024) scores demonstration *sets* by validation accuracy — globally, over bootstrapped training examples, with a fixed shot count and no retrieval gate. "In-context Example Selection with Influences" (Nguyen & Wong, 2023) computes per-example influence on a fixed validation set for classification-style ICL. Both estimate a single global utility per example. Our estimand differs: for a retrieval-gated agent memory, utility is a property of the (item, retrieval neighborhood) pair, so an item can be net-positive averaged over a validation set while being net-negative on exactly the queries that retrieve it. We test this against a global screen at matched probe budget. Neither line reports whether its selection survives its own estimation noise, which is the gap our decomposition targets.

**RL / bandit memory curation.** A 2025 line of work (Memory-R1-style memory managers) trains add/delete/no-op policies from downstream task reward — the closest existing mechanism to outcome-conditioned admission, and the most dangerous neighbour. We treat it as a competitor, not a citation: its reward is episode-level and shared across all co-injected items, so credit assignment to individual items is confounded, and there is no paired counterfactual. We implement a Thompson-sampling keep/drop curator at matched compute (3,200 online episodes) and predict the paired leave-one-out estimator dominates at equal episode budget precisely because it removes that confound.

**Retrieval-side gating.** Diagnostic and abstention-aware work gates memory injection on retrieval score. The pilot results motivating this proposal show the harmful bank retrieved topically *correct* items, so retrieval score should not be a sufficient gate — but following review this is now tested as a full end-to-end thresholded cell at matched bank size, not only as an AUC control.

**Selection on noisy estimates.** Winner's curse, empirical-Bayes shrinkage (Efron/Tweedie), and BH-FDR are standard in genomics and A/B testing but, to our recollection, have not been applied to memory-item admission, where per-item probe budgets are necessarily tiny (single-digit observations). Making that statistical structure explicit — and separating it from item–item interference — is the contribution we consider hardest to duplicate and now foreground in the title.
Abstract:
Agentic memory systems admit experience into a bank using signals that are never validated: the source episode succeeded, or a reflector declared the distilled insight useful. Pilot measurements motivating this work show the consequence — injecting a full retrieved bank fixed zero held-out items and broke six to seven (McNemar p<0.05, replicated), while content-side repairs and volume reduction only moved the effect to zero rather than converting it to gain. The obvious fix is to admit items on measured downstream utility. We ask whether that fix actually works, and give two results rather than one.

First, the estimand matters: we define an item's utility as the paired change in outcome when it is removed from the top-k bundle that would actually be injected, averaged over the queries that actually retrieve it. We predict this neighborhood-conditional quantity differs materially from a global validation screen at equal probe budget — large item×neighborhood interaction, frequent sign disagreement.

Second, and this is the load-bearing claim: because each item's utility is estimated from a handful of probe queries, keeping every item with positive measured utility is selection on noise. A split-half probe design decomposes the gap between projected and realized gain into a winner's-curse component and a non-additivity (interference) component at zero extra episode cost, so the mechanism is identified rather than asserted, and either outcome is publishable. Empirical-Bayes and FDR screens are tested as the corrections.

We evaluate on multi-hop QA with one 7B open agent under a fully item-paired design with measured null-replicate noise floors, against volume reduction, random size- and token-matched pruning, embedding-redundancy/recency pruning, retrieval-score threshold gating, reflector-confidence gating, global validation screening at matched compute, a learned utility classifier on the same probe data, and a matched-compute bandit curator. A three-cell instruction-shift arm tests whether a screened bank is co-adapted to the instruction it was probed under. Total: ~35k agent episodes on one 4×A100 node.
Experiments:
**Scope decisions made to fit the envelope and the review.** One agent model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) for all results; one primary task; no interactive benchmark; the GEPA coupling arm and the 14B portability arm were cut (reasons in Baselines/changes_made); the probe-budget sweep is analysis-only. Two reviewer-named baselines were added as full end-to-end cells.

**Setup.** Primary task: HotpotQA (distractor) with a ReAct agent and a retrieval tool, ~5 LLM calls/episode. Bank construction: 500 training episodes; a frontier model writes distilled insights + trajectory summaries with a self-reported usefulness score; the source episode's success label is recorded. Candidate bank: 240 items. Dense retrieval (bge-base) over items, top-k=7 injection by default. Held-out evaluation set: n=1,000 paired items, disjoint from all probe and training pools. Metric: exact-match/F1 (string-matched, no LLM judge — which is why the API budget stays under $100).

**Utility estimator.** For a probe query q we retrieve the bundle B(q) of top-7 items and run the agent (i) with the full bundle and (ii) with B(q)\{m} for each of the 7 items. The utility observation for item m on q is y_full(q) − y_{−m}(q): the marginal contribution of m *in the context it is actually deployed in*. Each probe query yields 7 observations for 8 runs. Item m's neighborhood N(m) is the set of probe queries whose top-7 retrieval contains m; by construction every observation for m comes from N(m).

**E1 — Is the write path blind? (no extra episodes; analysis of probe data.)** Split each item's probe observations into halves A and B. Compute AUC for predicting sign(û_i^{(B)}) from (a) source-episode success, (b) reflector self-reported usefulness, (c) mean retrieval score, (d) item length, (e) embedding-redundancy rank, and (f) û_i^{(A)}. Prediction: write-path and retrieval-side signals near 0.5–0.6; measured utility ≥0.65. Each of (a), (b), (c), (e) additionally has a matched-bank-size end-to-end cell (see cells 9, 10, 11 below), so the AUC result is confirmed at the level reviewers asked for.

**E2 — Is utility neighborhood-conditional?** Run a *matched-budget* global probe arm: 400 random validation queries, each with a random 7-item bundle from the bank, same leave-one-out protocol. Compare per-item global vs neighborhood estimates (correlation, sign-disagreement rate) and fit a mixed-effects model of paired outcome change with item and item×neighborhood random effects to decompose variance. End-to-end confirmation: the global-screened bank cell.

**E3 — Screening rules and decomposition of the transfer gap (the headline analysis).** Build banks by: (a) naive, keep if û_i>0; (b) empirical-Bayes, u_i ~ N(μ,τ²) fit across items, keep if posterior P(u_i>0)>0.7; (c) BH-FDR on one-sided paired tests at q=0.1. Evaluate each end-to-end at k=7, item-paired against no-memory and unscreened. Decompose using the split-half probe design:
 G_insample = Σ_{retained} û_i^{(A)} (the selection sample),
 G_unbiased = Σ_{retained} û_i^{(B)} (independent probes, same neighborhoods, same retained set),
 G_actual = measured held-out net gain.
Winner's curse = G_insample − G_unbiased. Non-additivity + distribution shift = G_unbiased − G_actual. G_unbiased is the "noiseless oracle screen" projection and costs zero extra episodes. If the second component dominates, the winner's-curse story is falsified and interference is implicated; we report that as the finding.

**E3b — In-context vs singleton utility (interaction ablation).** For 80 randomly chosen items, additionally measure singleton utility (item alone vs no memory) on 8 probe queries drawn from each item's neighborhood, plus 400 no-memory controls. Report correlation and sign-flip rate between singleton and leave-one-out utility. This quantifies directly how much the estimand changes when interference is admitted.

**E4 — Probe budget (analysis-only, no end-to-end cells).** Subsample probe observations to give effective m ∈ {2,4,7,12} per item and recompute the E3 decomposition at each point. Prediction: the winner's-curse component shrinks monotonically in m; the non-additivity component does not. The end-to-end confirmation cells at m=2 were cut — the decomposition is well powered at item level (240 items), whereas an m=2 end-to-end contrast would sit near our 3.5-point claim threshold and could not decide anything.

**E5 — Instruction-shift / co-adaptation (3 cells).** The screen is fit under instruction A. Obtain instruction B by a single frontier-model rewrite pass of A (~10 API calls, zero agent episodes; this is an instruction *shift*, not a prompt-optimizer run, and we label it as such). Evaluate {no memory, unscreened k=7, EB-screened k=7} under instruction B at n=1,000. Contrast of record: EB-B vs no-memory-B (a replication, estimable at our MDE), plus item-level rank correlation of per-item memory effects across instructions. This is the track's co-adaptation question at 3,000 episodes with an estimable contrast.

**E6 — Directional replication (MuSiQue, 3 cells, n=400).** Fresh 240-item bank (300 construction episodes), 300 probe queries × 8 = 2,400 probe episodes, evaluate {no memory, unscreened k=7, EB-screened k=7}. MDE ≈ 5 points; treated as direction-only.

**Episode arithmetic (all counts are agent episodes; ~5 LLM calls each).**
- Bank construction (HotpotQA): 500
- Neighborhood probes: 400 queries × 8 runs = 3,200 (≈11.7 observations/item over 240 items; ≈5.8 per split-half)
- Global probes, matched budget: 400 × 8 = 3,200
- Singleton ablation (E3b): 80 × 8 + 400 controls = 1,040
- End-to-end cells @ n=1,000, **12 cells = 12,000**: (1) no-memory; (2) unscreened k=7; (3) unscreened k=3; (4) EB-screened k=7; (5) random size+token-matched prune; (6) global-screened; (7) naive-screened; (8) learned-classifier-screened; (9) reflector-confidence gate at matched size; (10) **retrieval-score threshold gate at matched size** [added]; (11) **embedding-redundancy + recency prune at matched size** [added]; (12) top-3-most-harmful-items-removed
- Noise-floor replicates: no-memory ×2 extra, EB ×2 extra (independent probe draws) = 4,000
- Bandit curator baseline: 3,200 online + 1,000 eval = 4,200
- Instruction-shift arm (E5): 3 × 1,000 = 3,000
- MuSiQue replication (E6): 300 + 2,400 + 1,200 = 3,900
**Total ≈ 35,040 episodes ≈ 175k LLM calls.**

**Why this fits.** 35k episodes at ~12.5k prefill + ~750 decode tokens each = ~438M prefill and ~26M decode tokens. With 4 vLLM replicas of Qwen2.5-7B on 4×A100 80GB (batched prefill ~6–8k tok/s/GPU, aggregate decode ~1.5–2.5k tok/s under high concurrency), pure inference is ~8–10 hours. Applying a 3× overhead factor for retrieval-tool latency, orchestration, and failures gives ~1.5 days, leaving a full re-run allowance inside a 3–4 day wall-clock budget. Frontier API usage: 800 bank-writing calls + ~10 instruction-rewrite calls ≈ $40–80; scoring is string-match, not LLM-judged. Both fit the stated envelope with slack.
Baselines and Ablations:
**Baselines that could plausibly win (all end-to-end, item-paired, n=1,000).**
1. **Volume reduction (unscreened, k=3).** The pilot's neutralizer and the cheapest fix. Screening must beat it by producing gain, not merely absence of harm.
2. **Random size- and token-matched pruning.** Prune uniformly at random to the item count *and* injected-token count the EB screen retains. This is the decisive control, pre-registered as such: the total effect of screening over the unscreened bank decomposes into a **volume component** (random-matched − unscreened) and a **content component** (EB − random-matched). If the content component is within the noise floor, the core claim is refuted and the paper's headline becomes "content-blind size reduction fully explains memory repair."
3. **Embedding-redundancy + recency pruning at matched bank size** *(added, reviewer 2)*. The standard content-side memory-management heuristic. If simple deduplication matches the counterfactual screen, the probe cost is unjustified and we report that.
4. **Retrieval-score threshold gating at matched bank size** *(added, reviewer 1)*. Threshold chosen so the retained bank matches EB's item count; head-to-head against the screen rather than only an AUC check.
5. **Reflector-confidence gate at matched bank size.** The gate deployed in existing systems.
6. **Global validation screening at matched probe budget** (the MIPROv2 / influence-function analogue), isolating the conditionality claim from the screening claim.
7. **Learned utility classifier on the same probe data.** Logistic regression / gradient-boosted trees over item and query features (retrieval score, item type, length, reflector confidence, query–item embedding interactions), fit on the *same* probe observations. Tests whether the gain is specific to the counterfactual signal or obtainable from any reasonably-fit model on the same budget.
8. **Bandit/RL curator at matched compute.** Thompson-sampling keep/drop over items, reward = episode outcome credited to all co-injected items, 3,200 online episodes (equal to the screening probe budget), then frozen and evaluated. The natural competitor from the RL-memory-curation line.

**Ablations kept (each carries a prediction).**
(a) Selection rule: naive vs EB vs FDR on identical probe data (naive and EB are both end-to-end cells; FDR is analysis-level plus a bank composition report).
(b) In-context (leave-one-out) vs singleton utility on 80 items (E3b) — isolates the interaction confound.
(c) Probe budget m ∈ {2,4,7,12} via subsampling — decomposition only, no end-to-end cells.
(d) Pairing ablation: recompute utilities from unpaired accuracy differences on the same runs (free, analysis-only) to quantify how much power comes from pairing.
(e) Top-3-most-harmful-items-removed: tests whether the whole effect is a few poison items rather than a distributional property.
(f) Instruction shift (E5): does the screened bank's advantage survive a rewritten instruction?

**Cut, and why.**
- **GEPA coupling arm (−5,500 episodes).** Its prediction was a difference-in-differences on a base effect the pilot measured as approximately zero (prompt evolution fixed as many items as it broke), so P6-as-written was not estimable at n=1,000 regardless of budget. Spending 13% of the episode ledger on an unestimable contrast fails the "carries a claim" test. The co-adaptation question it was partly serving is preserved, estimably, by E5.
- **14B portability check (−4,000 7B-equivalents).** Marginal utility is model-conditional by construction, so "does a 7B-screened bank help a 14B agent" tests a strawman at 2 underpowered cells. We keep MuSiQue instead, which tests whether the *method* reproduces on a fresh task and fresh bank. Single-model is stated as the main limitation.
- **End-to-end m=2 cells (−2,000).** The probe-budget curve is free and well powered at item level; the end-to-end version would land near the claim threshold.
- **Neighborhood-definition sensitivity, per-stage injection restriction.** No distinct prediction / already answered by the pilot.
Falsifiable Predictions:
**P1 (write path is blind).** AUC of source-episode success and of reflector confidence for predicting held-out sign(u_i) is ≤0.60 with a 95% CI excluding 0.70 (n=240 items, AUC SE ≈ 0.035); retrieval score and embedding-redundancy rank likewise ≤0.62; split-half measured utility reaches AUC ≥0.65. *Refutation:* any cheap signal reaches ≥0.70, in which case the expensive screen is unjustified — we report that and stop. Confirmed end-to-end by cells 9–11 failing to beat cell 4.

**P2 (utility is neighborhood-conditional).** ≥25% of items flip sign between global and neighborhood estimates at equal probe budget, and the mixed-effects decomposition attributes ≥30% of explained variance to the item×neighborhood interaction. This item-level test (n=240) is the primary evidence. The end-to-end neighborhood-vs-global contrast is confirmatory: claimed only if it exceeds 3.5 points; a 2-point difference is reported as an underpowered estimate with a CI.

**P3 (screening converts harm to gain), stated at the detectable effect size.** EB-screened memory at k=7 beats no-memory by ≥3.5 points with fixes significantly exceeding breaks (McNemar p<0.05). *We claim nothing below 3.5 points.* A realized +1.5 to +3 is reported as "positive direction, not established at this sample size." *Refutation:* screened memory indistinguishable from no memory — a strong negative result about experience reuse that we would report as the paper's finding.

**P4 (winner's curse, and its separation from interference) — the load-bearing prediction.** At m≈6 observations/item (split-half), the winner's-curse component G_insample − G_unbiased accounts for ≥40% of the naive rule's projected gain and shrinks monotonically as m grows to 12; the non-additivity component G_unbiased − G_actual accounts for <25% and does *not* shrink with m. EB/FDR reduce the winner's-curse component to <15%. End-to-end, naive-screened underperforms EB-screened (reported with CI; claimed as a difference only above 3.5 points). *Refutation:* the non-additivity component dominates and is stable across m — then the transfer failure is interference among co-injected items, not selection noise, our mechanism claim is wrong, and the paper reports the interference finding, which is itself actionable (screen bundles, not items).

**P5 (content, not size).** The content component (EB − random size+token-matched) is at least half the total gain over the unscreened bank and exceeds the null-replicate floor; EB also beats embedding-redundancy/recency pruning at matched size. *Refutation:* parity with either matched-size control, which collapses the claim to "smaller or deduplicated banks are better" — reported as the headline, not buried.

**P6 (co-adaptation to the instruction).** Under the rewritten instruction B, EB-screened memory still beats no-memory-B by ≥3.5 points, and the item-level rank correlation of per-item memory effects between instructions A and B is ≥0.4. *Refutation:* the advantage vanishes under B — then screening is co-adapted to the prompt it was probed under and must be re-run whenever the instruction changes, a directly actionable result for anyone composing a memory with a prompt optimizer, and the one we would report.
Measurement and Noise Control:
**Pairing.** Every end-to-end comparison is item-paired: all conditions are evaluated on identical held-out items with identical decoding seeds; the unit of analysis is the per-item outcome change; contrasts use McNemar's exact test on discordant pairs with fixes and breaks reported separately (the pilot showed net deltas can be flat while composition shifts).

**Minimum detectable effect, and claims narrowed to fit it.** With n=1,000 paired items and a discordance rate between 10% and 20% (100–200 discordant pairs), McNemar has 80% power at α=0.05 for a net difference of roughly **2.8–4.0 accuracy points**. We pre-register a claim threshold of **3.5 points** on all primary end-to-end contrasts and will explicitly decline to claim effects below it. The MuSiQue replication (n=400) has MDE ≈5 points and is directional only. The item-level analyses (E1 AUC, E2 variance decomposition, E3/E4 transfer decomposition, E3b sign-flip rate) are powered at n=240 items with ~12 observations each and carry the mechanistic claims; end-to-end cells confirm rather than establish them. This asymmetry is deliberate: the paper's contribution does not depend on detecting a 2-point end-to-end delta.

**Noise floor.** Three cells (no-memory, unscreened k=7, EB-screened k=7) are run in triplicate with different decoding seeds; one no-memory replicate is relabelled as a null treatment and analysed blind through the full pipeline. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of the null-replicate distribution. The three EB replicates additionally use three *independent probe-query draws*, so the retained bank is treated as a random object and EB results are reported as mean ± SD over banks, not as a single number.

**Estimation discipline.** Per-item utility estimates are deliberately underpowered (m≈12) — that is the substantive point, and why utilities are pooled in a hierarchical model that borrows strength rather than tested one at a time. Screening is fit on training-split probe queries; every reported gain is measured on a disjoint held-out set; the split-half decomposition (G_insample, G_unbiased, G_actual) is the pre-registered overfitting diagnostic, fixed before any end-to-end run.

**Multiplicity.** Three primary contrasts, reported uncorrected: EB-screened vs no-memory; EB-screened vs random size+token-matched; neighborhood screen vs global screen. All other cells (volume, redundancy/recency, retrieval-score gate, reflector gate, learned classifier, bandit, top-3-harmful, naive) are secondary and Holm-corrected within family. Predictions P1–P6 and the 3.5-point threshold are registered before data collection.
Preprint Collision Check:
**The literature search failed again.** Every query in this round returned a server-side "tool use limit exceeded" error, including a bare single-query test; no titles, venues, or dates were retrieved. This is the second consecutive failed attempt. **Silence here is a tooling failure, not evidence of novelty**, and this proposal has *not* been cleared against the last twelve months of arXiv. I will not fabricate a CLOSEST/GAP table from memory.

What I can state, explicitly flagged as unverified recollection with unverified dates: the nearest work I am aware of is (i) ExpeL (AAAI 2024) and Reflexion (NeurIPS 2023) for write-time heuristic admission; (ii) MIPROv2 (EMNLP 2024) for global validation scoring of demonstration sets; (iii) Nguyen & Wong (2023) for influence-based ICL example selection; (iv) a 2025 line of RL-trained memory managers (Memory-R1-style) learning add/delete policies from episode reward; (v) ReasoningBank-style 2025 experience-distillation systems; (vi) 2025–2026 diagnostic/abstention work gating memory injection on retrieval score. Item (iv) is the most dangerous neighbour and is now an implemented, compute-matched baseline rather than a citation. I cannot confirm any date or rule out a closer 2025–2026 preprint.

**How the proposal was restructured to be robust to a collision, rather than merely disclosing the risk.** Both reviewers advised retargeting the headline to the selection-noise decomposition if a close preprint exists. I have done that pre-emptively: the title, abstract, and P4 now foreground the winner's-curse-vs-non-additivity decomposition, and the neighborhood-conditional estimand is presented as the estimator that makes that decomposition well posed. The consequence is that a preprint proposing counterfactual memory screening would *not* subsume this paper: our result would then read "the published screen's projected gain is X% winner's curse at realistic probe budgets, and here is the shrinkage correction and the interference residual," which qualifies rather than duplicates it — the methods contribution the track explicitly invites. Only a preprint that both (a) estimates per-item counterfactual utility conditioned on the retrieval neighborhood *and* (b) reports a split-sample transfer/overfitting analysis would be a genuine collision; in that case we would retarget again, to the interference measurement (E3b + the non-additivity component), and say so explicitly in the paper.

**Committed pre-submission search protocol, executed manually since the tool is unavailable** (results reported with dates in the paper): arXiv listing sweeps of cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.LG from 2024-09 onward and Semantic Scholar forward-citation sweeps of ExpeL, MIPROv2, ReasoningBank, and Memory-R1, with queries — "memory utility estimation LLM agent"; "counterfactual memory pruning agent"; "leave-one-out demonstration utility retrieval"; "shrinkage demonstration selection in-context"; "winner's curse example/prompt selection"; "negative transfer agent memory"; "RL memory management LLM agent"; "abstention retrieval memory injection agent".
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Unverified novelty.** Two failed searches. This is an open risk at submission time; the mitigation is the structural retargeting described above, not reassurance.
2. **The bank may contain no positive-utility items** for a 7B agent, making P3 unreachable. Pre-check on probe data before committing to the end-to-end grid: require posterior P(u_i>0)>0.7 for ≥15% of items. If not, we pivot to the negative result plus E1/E2/E3 mechanism analysis, which stands on probe data alone.
3. **Power.** MDE ≈3–4 points; a real 2-point screening effect cannot be decided here, and we will say so rather than claim a win. Budget was deliberately spent on item-level mechanism analyses, which are well powered.
4. **Non-additivity may dominate.** If G_unbiased − G_actual is large and stable in m, the winner's-curse mechanism is wrong. The design detects this rather than hiding it, but the paper's framing would then change to interference-aware bundle screening — a different, smaller contribution.
5. **The gain may be a few poison items.** Ablation (e) tests it; if so we reframe as "find and delete the few catastrophic items," weaker but actionable.
6. **Screening cost is real** (~3,200 probe episodes, ~3× the held-out eval). We report accuracy per screening episode alongside accuracy; the k=3 and redundancy-pruning baselines may dominate on that axis even if they lose on accuracy. We report that honestly.
7. **Single agent model, single task family, single instruction pair.** All primary results use Qwen2.5-7B on multi-hop QA; MuSiQue is 3 cells at n=400 and the cross-model check was cut. We do not claim generality to interactive, web, or code agents; this is the main external-validity limitation.
8. **No prompt-optimizer coupling result.** E5 is an instruction *shift*, not a GEPA run, and we do not claim to have measured optimizer–memory coupling. We release the screened banks and probe data so that arm can be run by us or others as a follow-up.
9. **Probe-query distribution shift.** Neighborhoods estimated on training queries may not match test-time retrieval; probe queries are drawn from the same pool as test items and we report train/test neighborhood overlap.
10. **EB normality.** A heavy left tail would violate the Gaussian prior; we report the nonparametric BH-FDR variant so no conclusion hinges on it.

Name: coverage_currency_coupling
Title: Concentration Is the Common Currency: Self-Editing Memory and Prompt Optimization Both Buy pass@1 by Spending Solve-Set Coverage, and Stacking Them Pays Twice
Short Hypothesis: Both halves of the memory+prompt-optimizer stack act on the *same* axis: they are distribution-concentration devices, not information-addition devices. Concretely: (i) retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions each raise pass@1 while shrinking the set of tasks solvable with any of k samples, so each advantage decays or reverses by moderate k; (ii) the concentration is a mode *shift*, not mere sharpening — matching decoding diversity by temperature does not restore coverage; (iii) they concentrate onto *different* modes, which is why they look complementary at k=1, but composing them in one prompt (naively or co-adapted) compounds the coverage loss while the pass@1 gains sub-add — coupling pays twice and gets less than double. The constructive corollary, and the reason the track's "division of labour" intuition is right but misplaced: the labour must be divided *across the rollout portfolio*, not across prompt slots. A heterogeneous portfolio (some rollouts plain, some memory-conditioned, some optimizer-conditioned) beats any homogeneous conditioning at matched total budget.
Related Work:
Five clusters.

(1) **Prompt optimization.** MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695) and GEPA (arXiv 2507.19457) treat a prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over it with Bayesian or reflective-evolutionary updates, reporting single-sample validation accuracy at every step. Neither the search objective nor the reported result is sampling-aware: a candidate that concentrates mass onto an already-reachable solution is indistinguishable, under their metric, from one that makes a new solution reachable. Our claim is that this distinction is exactly what the optimizer is silently trading away, and it is the reason the prior track finding "the optimizer's gain was redistribution, not accuracy" recurs.

(2) **Agentic experience memory.** ExpeL, Reflexion, A-Mem (2502.12110), AgentFly/Memento (2508.16153), MemGen (2509.24704), ReasoningBank and the 2026 wave all report pass@1 with a bank versus without, at fixed decoding budget. None reports a pass@k or solve-set coverage curve, so none separates "memory supplied a solution otherwise unreachable" from "memory made a reachable solution more likely."

(3) **Concurrent work on memory and multi-sample inference — the live collision.** "When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?" (arXiv 2605.28224) argues that injected positive prior facts bias tool-use agents toward consistency, producing a diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff no retrieval policy escapes. This is the closest existing statement of our memory-side phenomenon and we treat it as prior work, not as a gap. It is qualitative about the tradeoff (diversity and efficiency), it does not measure whether the *set of solvable instances* shrinks, it does not distinguish sharpening from mode shift (no diversity-matched decoding control), it contains no prompt optimizer, and its "any positive prior triggers it" account makes a prediction we can falsify with a length-matched decoy arm. "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (arXiv 2505.16067, ACL 2026) documents *experience-following*: high input-memory similarity yields highly similar outputs, with error propagation over time — a mechanism-level precedent for homogenization, framed as long-horizon degradation rather than coverage accounting.

(4) **Diversity collapse from training.** Outcome-based Exploration for LLM Reasoning (2509.06941) and Post-training LLMs for Diverse High-Quality Outputs (2509.04784) establish pass@1-up / pass@k-down for gradient updates; R-Diverse (2602.13103) and DyJR (2603.16157) attack the same collapse inside self-play and RLVR training loops; "Exploratory Memory-Augmented LLM Agent" (2602.23008) asserts that static memory cannot capture the diversity needed for continued improvement and fixes it with joint RL. All of these are weight-space interventions or propose fixes; none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue, and none asks whether *prompt optimization* — the other half of the stack — carries the same signature.

(5) **Retrieval × aggregation.** Inference Scaling for Bridging Retrieval and Augmented Generation (2412.10684) notes retrieval quality interacting negatively with self-consistency in single-turn RAG QA and proposes passage permutation; "Self-Consistency Is Losing Its Edge" (2511.00751) attributes diminishing sampling returns to model capability, a competing explanation we control for by measuring the unconditioned curve on the same models; ICL-diversity work (2404.16807) shows in-context examples reduce *lexical* diversity in single-turn generation.

Our contribution is not "memory reduces diversity" — 2605.28224 is concurrent on that. It is the coverage accounting (what is actually lost, and whether it is lost or merely made rarer), the sharpening-vs-shifting adjudication, and the claim that concentration is the *common currency* of both halves of the memory+optimizer stack, which turns the track's division-of-labour question upside down: complementarity is real, but only harvestable across rollouts.
Abstract: Agent frameworks now bolt a self-editing memory onto a prompt optimizer and report a higher single-sample success rate. That number cannot tell you whether either component supplied a solution the agent could not otherwise find, or merely made one it could already find more probable. We hypothesize that both components are concentration devices operating on the same axis, and that this explains why they appear complementary at k=1 and yet compose badly. We test it by estimating, for every held-out task, the agent's per-instance solve probability from many independent rollouts under seven conditions: unconditioned, retrieved-experience memory, length-matched decoy memory, diversity-matched-by-temperature memory, GEPA-optimized instructions alone, GEPA instructions plus memory (the naive composition practitioners ship), and GEPA co-evolved with memory in the loop. From these pools we read off pass@k curves and their crossovers, a per-instance coverage decomposition into instances made newly solvable, made unsolvable, made more reliable, or made less reliable, and strategy-level solution diversity. Two controls decide the mechanism: raising temperature under memory until strategy diversity matches the unconditioned agent (if memory only sharpens, coverage returns; if it shifts the mode, it does not), and length-matched decoy memory (separating experience-specific narrowing from generic context load). The coupling test is the paper's centre: we ask whether the optimizer's gain carries the same coverage signature as memory's, whether the two concentrate onto the same or different strategy modes, and whether stacking them compounds coverage loss while sub-adding pass@1. Finally we test the fix the account implies and that the prompt-slot framing cannot express: a heterogeneous rollout portfolio that spends part of its budget unconditioned, part on memory, part on optimized instructions, constructed at zero extra compute by resampling the collected pools.
