All comparisons are instance-paired with unbiased pass@k estimators, two-level bootstrap intervals, null replicates, and matched-token as well as matched-k budgets.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED.** ReAct scaffold, tool stack, step limit, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from a training split with an ExpeL-style write path, then frozen for all test rollouts), prompt boilerplate, held-out split. Only the conditioning variant, decoding temperature (in one designated arm), and rollout-allocation policy vary.

**ENVIRONMENTS.** E1 (primary, carries every quantitative claim): tool-augmented multi-hop QA over HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue; the agent issues search calls, 4–8 model calls per episode. E2 (directional replication only): ALFWorld, step cap 20, where "strategy" is a concrete action sequence. **WebShop is cut** — it carried no claim the other two do not.

**MODELS.** Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (primary, full E1 grid), Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (secondary, decisive E1 arms). **Qwen3-32B is cut**; the claim is about conditioning, not scale, and two model families at two sizes is what the budget buys. A frontier API model performs offline bank distillation, GEPA reflection, and strategy annotation, identically across arms.

**PRECHECKS (gate the study, reported either way).** On a 150-instance dev split: (P-a) the memory bank must give a paired pass@1 gain ≥5 points over unconditioned at deployment temperature; (P-b) GEPA-optimized instructions must give a paired pass@1 gain ≥3 points. If a component does not help at k=1 there is no concentration to explain for that component; we enrich the bank / extend the GEPA budget until it passes, and report the precheck numbers rather than proceeding quietly.

**ARMS (E1, Llama-3.1-8B).**
- A0 Unconditioned.
- A1 Memory, top-7 retrieval (standard deployment).
- A3 Decoy memory: 7 items retrieved for a different query from a disjoint task family, token-matched to A1 within 5%. Adjudicates the generic-long-context account and the concurrent "any positive prior" account of 2605.28224.
- A4 Diversity-matched memory: A1 with temperature raised until mean distinct strategies per instance matches A0 within 5%, calibrated on dev only and frozen. **The decisive mechanism arm.**
- O1 GEPA-optimized instructions, no memory.
- O2 GEPA instructions (evolved memory-free) + memory at test — the naive composition.
- O3 GEPA co-evolved with memory in the loop + memory at test — the co-adaptation condition.

(The top-3 volume arm is **cut**: prior work already established injection volume as the pass@1 lever, and A3/A4 are what adjudicate mechanism.)

**ARMS (E2, 8B):** A0, A1, O1, O3.
**ARMS (E1, Qwen2.5-14B):** A0, A1, O1, O3.

**PORTFOLIO ARMS (zero additional rollouts, constructed by resampling collected pools).**
- P1 Heterogeneous portfolio: allocate k rollouts across {A0, A1, O1} on a simplex grid in steps of 0.25; report pass@k of the mixture. Endpoints reduce exactly to the homogeneous arms, so any interior peak cannot be a compute artifact.
- P2 Memory-as-reranker: k A0 rollouts, then one selection call in which retrieved memory items are shown alongside the k candidate trajectories. Costs one extra model call per draw (~5k calls total). Compared at matched total calls against A1 with self-consistency selection.

**CORE MEASUREMENT.** E1: 250 held-out instances × n=16 independent rollouts per arm at deployment temperature. E2: 100 instances × n=8. Unbiased combinatorial pass@k for k ∈ {1,2,4,8,16} (E1), {1,2,4,8} (E2).

**PRIMARY ENDPOINTS.**
1. **pass@k curves and crossovers** for each arm against A0, with bootstrap intervals on the crossover k*. Also reported on a matched-token axis, where shorter-prompt arms get proportionally more rollouts — the deployment-relevant comparison, since conditioning costs tokens on every rollout.
2. **Coverage decomposition.** Classify each instance by estimated solve probability under A0 versus the treatment arm: NEW (A0 never solves in n, treatment sometimes does), LOST (reverse), CONCENTRATED, DILUTED, NEITHER. Reported at the raw threshold, under a Jeffreys-prior posterior, and under two disjoint n=8 subsamples for split-half stability.
3. **Strategy diversity.** Each rollout reduced to a pre-registered canonical signature (E1: normalized sequence of search queries with entity/relation types; E2: sequence of primitive action types and target object classes), clustered per instance. Report distinct strategies per instance, first-tool-call entropy, and token-level self-BLEU on reasoning traces as a definition-free companion statistic. Signature extraction validated against 100 human-clustered instances (report adjusted Rand index).

**MECHANISM ANALYSES.**
(a) *Sharpening vs shifting.* Per instance, the fraction of A0's distinct strategies present in the treatment pool and vice versa. Pure sharpening predicts the treatment's strategies are a subset of A0's high-probability ones; shifting predicts strategies absent from A0's entire pool, plus elimination of strategies A0 used successfully. A4 is the causal version of the same test at the outcome level.
(b) *Mode identity across components — the coupling mechanism.* Jensen–Shannon divergence between per-instance strategy distributions of A1 and O1 (do memory and the optimizer concentrate onto the *same* mode?), and of O3 against A1 (does co-adaptation collapse the optimizer onto memory's mode?). This is the quantitative form of the track's "disjoint slices" observation.
(c) *LOST forensics.* On 60 LOST instances per component, annotate whether the conditioning recommended a strategy incompatible with the successful unconditioned strategy and whether the agent attempted it.
(d) *Bank-similarity moderator.* Per-instance max similarity to any bank item as a predictor of NEW vs LOST — if NEW concentrates on near-duplicates, memory's genuine coverage contribution is limited to task recurrence, which is the honest scope statement.

**RE-EXAMINATION TABLE.** For each component alone and for the naive composition, report the gain as it is normally reported (single sample, deployment temperature), then the same comparison at k=4 and at matched token budget. This is the direct statement of how much of a published-style memory / optimizer / memory+optimizer gain survives a sampling-aware protocol.

**RESOURCE ARITHMETIC.** E1-8B: 7 arms × 250 × 16 = 28,000 episodes, plus a 4,000-episode null replicate of A0 at a fresh seed set = 32,000. E1-14B: 4 × 250 × 16 = 16,000. E2-8B: 4 × 100 × 8 = 3,200. GEPA runs: 6 total (memory-free and memory-in-loop × {E1-8B, E1-14B, E2-8B}), each 40 candidates × 20 train instances × 2 rollouts = 1,600 episodes → 9,600. Total ≈ 61,000 episodes ≈ 352,000 model calls (E1 ~5 calls/episode, E2 ~20). At vLLM throughput on 4×A100 for 8B/14B this is ~3–4 days wall clock, within "days not weeks," and each configuration sits in the few-thousand-episode band the constraints assume. Portfolio arms add ~5k selection calls and no rollouts. API spend: GEPA reflection (~2M tokens), one-time bank distillation, and annotation/judging ≈ $180 total.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
(i) *A1 or O1 retaining its full advantage at k=8 and k=16* — the component adds genuine coverage, the concentration account is wrong for it, and we report that as vindication of the corresponding literature.
(ii) *A4 (diversity-matched memory)* — if decoding hotter under memory restores the unconditioned pass@k curve while keeping the pass@1 gain, memory is a pure sharpener, the fix is a hyperparameter, and the mode-shift claim dies while the measurement reframing survives. Single most important control.
(iii) *A3 (length-matched decoy)* — if irrelevant experience collapses coverage as much as A1, the phenomenon is generic context load, not experience. This also tests the concurrent 2605.28224 account, which predicts decoys (no positive priors about the query) should *not* collapse coverage.
(iv) *O1 as the missing baseline the reviewers named* — prompt-optimizer-only, run through the identical coverage pipeline. If O1 adds coverage while A1 destroys it, the "common currency" claim fails and the classical division-of-labour story stands.
(v) *O2/O3 beating both single components at k=8* — coupling works, our compounding prediction is wrong.
(vi) *Self-consistency over A1 rollouts at matched calls beating P1 and P2* — aggregation over memory-conditioned samples is already the best use of budget and the portfolio fix is unnecessary.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.** A4 discriminates sharpening from shifting at the outcome level; the strategy-overlap analysis does it at the trajectory level; the two must agree for the mechanism claim to stand. A3 removes content while holding tokens. O2 vs O3 isolates naive composition from co-adaptation (the drift question): O3 tells us whether letting the optimizer evolve *against* the memory absorbs the coverage loss or deepens it. P1's endpoints reduce exactly to A0/A1/O1, so the portfolio curve is an interpolation with all endpoints measured. A matched-token axis is reported for every arm so no conditioning is credited for spending more context. A shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check confirms retrieval functions.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Single-component (memory and optimizer alike):
1. On E1, each of A1 and O1 shows ≥5 points advantage over A0 at k=1 and ≤2 points by k=8, with crossover k* ≤ 8 for both models; on the matched-token axis, k* is smaller. (Stated as an equivalence claim at a 4-point margin at k=8; anything inside the band is reported inconclusive, not as support.)
2. Coverage: for each of A1 and O1, NEW instances are <4% of the test set and LOST/NEW ≥ 2 with exact binomial p<0.05 on discordant instances. Below that ratio we report the decomposition as inconclusive rather than as nesting.
3. Strategy diversity per instance falls ≥30% under A1 and ≥20% under O1 relative to A0, with matching drops in first-tool-call entropy.
4. **Mode shift, not sharpening:** under A4, with strategy diversity matched to A0, memory recovers less than half the pass@8 coverage gap, and ≥20% of A1's strategies are absent from A0's entire rollout pool.
5. A3 decoy memory reproduces less than half of A1's coverage loss.

Coupling (the track claim):
6. **Different modes:** per-instance strategy distributions of A1 and O1 are far apart (mean JSD ≥ 0.4, and ≥0.25 above the within-arm split-half JSD floor), while both are far from A0 — the quantitative form of "optimizer strong where memory weak."
7. **Stacking pays twice:** the naive composition O2 loses at least as much coverage at k=8 as the worse of A1 and O1 (LOST(O2) ≥ max(LOST(A1), LOST(O1)) within noise), while its pass@1 gain is strictly sub-additive: gain(O2) < gain(A1) + gain(O1) − 2 points.
8. **Co-adaptation is co-concentration:** O3 raises pass@1 over O2 by ≥2 points while its strategy distribution moves toward A1's (JSD(O3, A1) < JSD(O2, A1) by ≥0.1) and its pass@8 coverage is no better than O2's.
9. **The portfolio fix:** P1's optimum lies strictly in the interior of the simplex and beats the best homogeneous arm at matched k=8 by ≥3 points; equivalently, the union of solve sets from {A0, A1, O1} at k=4 each exceeds the best single arm at k=12 by ≥3 points.

**REFUTATION.** Advantages flat or growing in k, or NEW >8% with NEW exceeding LOST, kill the concentration claim for that component. If A4 restores the pass@8 gap to within 1 point, memory is a sharpener and the mode-shift claim is dead. If A3 reproduces A1's loss in full, the paper is about injected context volume, not experience, and we reframe explicitly. If O1 shows no coverage loss, the common-currency claim fails and we report that memory and prompt optimization are genuinely different animals — a clean negative for our central thesis. If P1's optimum is at a vertex, the constructive corollary is empty.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Many rollouts per instance are collected by construction, so estimates and their uncertainty come from the same data.
(a) **pass@k estimation:** standard unbiased combinatorial estimator per instance from n rollouts, averaged over instances; intervals from a two-level bootstrap resampling instances (10k resamples) and, within instance, rollouts, so instance heterogeneity and finite-rollout noise both propagate. All arms share instances, so every comparison is instance-paired.
(b) **Primary tests:** exact McNemar on paired fix/break counts at k=1 with the full decomposition always shown; paired bootstrap on per-instance pass@k differences for k>1; Holm correction across the arm family within each endpoint. Crossover k* reported with a bootstrap interval, never as a point.
(c) **Null replicates:** A0 is re-run on E1 with a disjoint seed set (4,000 episodes); the distribution of apparent pass@k deltas between the two identical arms defines the noise floor at every k, and no effect is claimed unless it exceeds that distribution's 95th percentile. Load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.
(d) **Coverage-decomposition noise:** NEW/LOST are thresholds on noisy rates, so they are reported at n=16, on two disjoint n=8 subsamples (split-half stability), and under a Jeffreys posterior giving the probability an instance is truly zero-rate. No NEW-vs-LOST difference smaller than the split-half instability is interpreted; the pre-registered claim threshold is LOST/NEW ≥ 2 with exact binomial p<0.05.
(e) **Minimum detectable effect:** with 250 paired E1 instances at n=16, the two-level bootstrap gives SE ≈ 1.7 points on a paired pass@k difference for k ≤ 8, so the design detects ~4.5 points at 80% power. Every quantitative prediction above is stated at or beyond that threshold, and the k=8 equivalence claim uses a 4-point margin. E2 at 100 instances × n=8 has roughly double the SE and is explicitly directional replication, not evidence for a numeric threshold.
(f) **Frozen calibration:** the A4 temperature and all GEPA optimization use dev/train splits only and are frozen before test rollouts. GEPA candidate selection uses its own validation split, never the test instances.
(g) **Portfolio estimator validity:** rollouts are independent given (instance, arm), so mixture pass@k estimated by resampling across arm pools is unbiased for a deployed heterogeneous portfolio; intervals come from the same two-level bootstrap.
Preprint Collision Check:
The search returned one genuine collision and several near misses; I treat the collision as prior work rather than arguing it away.

**COLLIDES, PARTIALLY: "When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?" (arXiv 2605.28224).** This paper already places retrieved fact/experience memory inside multi-trajectory tool-use inference and argues for a diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff that no retrieval policy escapes, with the mechanism "any positive prior facts in the prompt bias the model toward consistency." That is the same causal story as our memory-side hypothesis in the same experimental regime. I therefore drop any claim to having discovered that memory reduces trajectory diversity, and cite it as concurrent prior work. What survives, and what this proposal is now organized around: (i) it does not measure whether the *solve set* shrinks — diversity loss with intact coverage is a different and benign outcome, and our NEW/LOST decomposition is the test that separates them; (ii) it has no diversity-matched-temperature control, so it cannot distinguish sharpening from mode shift, which is the difference between "raise the temperature" and "restructure the deployment"; (iii) its "any positive prior" account makes a prediction our length-matched decoy arm can falsify; (iv) it contains no prompt optimizer, so it says nothing about whether instruction search carries the same signature, whether the two components concentrate onto the same mode, or what happens when they are stacked or co-adapted — which is the assigned coupling question and now the centre of this proposal.

**"How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents" (arXiv 2505.16067, ACL 2026)** — experience-following: high input-memory similarity produces highly similar outputs, causing error propagation. Mechanistic support for our account, framed as long-horizon degradation; no pass@k, no coverage, no optimizer. Does not collide; strengthens our bank-similarity moderator analysis, which we now frame as a direct test of experience-following at the coverage level.

**Training-time diversity collapse: 2509.06941, 2509.04784, R-Diverse (2602.13103), DyJR (2603.16157), Exploratory Memory-Augmented LLM Agent (2602.23008).** All are weight-space or RL-loop interventions; 2602.23008 asserts static memory limits diversity but proposes a joint-RL fix rather than measuring the trade. None collides; together they establish the phenomenon for gradients, which is precisely why the training-free analogue and the optimizer-side extension are worth nailing down.

**Retrieval × aggregation: 2412.10684** (single-turn RAG, retrieval interacting with self-consistency, passage-permutation fix) and **2511.00751** (capability, not context, explains diminishing sampling returns — a competing explanation we control for by measuring A0's own curve). **2404.16807** measures lexical, not strategy-level, diversity. **"Leveraging LLM Inconsistency to Boost Pass@k" (2505.12938)** runs the opposite direction and is a useful counterpoint for the portfolio arm.

**HONEST CAVEATS.** The search budget was exhausted before I could characterize three borderline titles (MemCollab, ParamMem, Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory) or sweep 2026 OpenReview submissions. Given 2605.28224 exists, I now assume a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure exists somewhere in the 2026 memory literature; the proposal is written so that its contribution does not depend on that figure being absent. What no retrieved work does is measure solve-set coverage loss, adjudicate sharpening versus mode shift, or ask whether prompt optimization is the same kind of device as memory.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Concurrent-work risk is real, not hypothetical.** 2605.28224 already owns "memory costs diversity in multi-trajectory tool-use inference." If a follow-up adds coverage curves before we publish, our remaining contribution is the optimizer-coupling half (common currency, mode divergence, compounding under stacking, portfolio fix). We have deliberately made that half the paper's spine rather than an appendix, so the contribution degrades gracefully.
2. **pass@k saturation** could compress the crossover into an uninterpretable region; mitigated by selecting instance pools with unconditioned pass@1 in the 30–60% band on dev and reporting full curves.
3. **NEW/LOST is a threshold on noisy rates.** n=16 cannot certify an instance is truly unsolvable without conditioning; the nesting claim is stated as "nested at n=16" with split-half stability and a pre-registered LOST/NEW ≥ 2 evidentiary bar, not as a claim about policy support.
4. **Strategy signatures are a design surface** that could manufacture the diversity result; the definition is fixed in advance, published verbatim, validated against human clustering (ARI reported), and accompanied by definition-free self-BLEU.
5. **A4 may not be achievable** — temperature might not reach A0's diversity without destroying coherence. We then report the achieved diversity level and treat A4 as partial rather than clean, and lean on the trajectory-level overlap analysis for the sharpening/shifting call.
6. **GEPA may not clear its precheck** on a 8B agent for these tasks. If P-b fails after an extended search budget, we report that and reinterpret O1 as "best hand-plus-search instruction found," which weakens the optimizer-specific claim to a claim about optimized instructions generally; we say so rather than quietly relabeling.
7. **Single bank, single optimizer.** Results may depend on bank composition (general heuristics may narrow more than episodic near-duplicates) and on GEPA's particular reflective operator; the bank-similarity moderator is our only within-study handle, and MIPRO is not run — a scope limit we state rather than paper over.
8. **Compute forced real cuts:** WebShop, the 32B model, and the injection-volume arm are gone; long-horizon evidence is E2-only and directional, at roughly double the E1 standard error.
9. **The portfolio payload presupposes k>1 deployments.** For strictly single-sample deployments the paper's message is a measurement warning and a caution about stacking conditioners, not a method.
10. **A refusal, stated plainly:** reviewers asked for a smaller, safer design. We cut breadth (environments, models, arms) but did not soften the claim into "we measure the interaction." The prediction that coupling *compounds coverage loss while sub-adding pass@1* is the risky part, and it is preserved with numeric thresholds and explicit refutation conditions.

Name: coverage_selection_division_of_labour
Title: Coverage Failures Are the Only Thing Memory Can Sell: A Stratified Division of Labour Between Self-Editing Memory and Prompt Optimization, Judged Against a Compute-Matched Sampling Control
Short Hypothesis: Given n memory-free samples, an agent's failure on an item is either a *coverage* failure (the gold answer never appears in any sample) or a *selection* failure (it appears but loses the vote). This partition predicts a division of labour: injected experience is the only mechanism that can convert coverage failures, prompt/instruction optimization acts on selection failures, and injection's damage falls almost entirely on high-agreement already-solved items. Three consequences are testable and sharp: (a) always-on memory injection is dominated at matched token budget by plain self-consistency; (b) the decisive test of memory's value is not memory vs. sampling but agreement-gated memory vs. *agreement-gated extra sampling on the same hard items* at matched compute; (c) memory and an instruction optimizer should fix approximately disjoint item sets, which is the mechanistic reason to couple them rather than to pick one. We are powered to decide (b) and (c), and pre-commit to reporting the bounded null ("spend the tokens on samples") if (b) ties.
Related Work:
Two collisions have to be conceded up front, because an earlier search found them and they remove claims this proposal originally made.

*Compute-matched evaluation of agent memory is no longer a novel protocol contribution.* MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) evaluates episodic-memory agents against Pass@k sampling under a unified frozen-backbone protocol precisely to separate memory from raw sampling capability. MemDelta (arXiv:2606.29914) argues that agent-memory gains must be budget-matched against simpler baselines and shows Mem0 matching cloud RAG at 50× cost. "Reusing Pre-Training Data at Test Time is a Compute Multiplier" (arXiv:2511.04234) runs a compute-comparable self-consistency-vs-retrieval ablation for document RAG. Evo-Memory (arXiv:2511.20857) finds a trivial ExpRAG baseline beating more elaborate self-evolving memory designs. We do **not** claim "match the compute" as a contribution; we adopt it as the required setting and cite these as establishing it.

*Agreement as a free gate on further computation is also not novel.* Adaptive-Consistency (Aggarwal et al., EMNLP 2023) and Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency (2025) already use inter-sample agreement to decide whether to keep sampling; Self-RAG (Asai et al., ICLR 2024), FLARE (Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023) and Adaptive-RAG (Jeong et al., NAACL 2024) gate *document* retrieval on self-assessed confidence or query-complexity classifiers. We withdraw "the gate is free" as a novelty claim. Difficulty-Adaptive SC is the nearest hybrid (it conditions low-agreement generation on related solved queries), and following review we now **implement and run it as a baseline** rather than distinguishing it by citation.

*Prompt optimization.* MIPRO and GEPA treat a prompt as instructions + demonstrations and search over it reflectively/evolutionarily. Our pilot found that GEPA-style evolution on this task family fixed as many held-out items as it broke and moved only the class-balanced metric — a *redistribution* signature. The coverage/selection partition explains why: instruction edits reweight which of the already-sampled candidates wins, i.e. they act on the selection side and cannot manufacture a candidate the model never produces. This is the concrete, falsifiable form of the "division of labour" question, and it is what the coupling literature (ExpeL, Reflexion, ReasoningBank and their 2026 successors bolted onto optimizers) reports end-to-end without isolating.

*What survives as ours.* The item-level coverage/selection stratification; the measured *recoverable-coverage ceiling* it implies for any memory bank; the agreement-gated-memory vs. agreement-gated-plain-sampling control that the stratification demands; and the stratum-decomposed test of whether an instruction optimizer and a self-editing memory fix disjoint items. None of MemRL, MemDelta, Evo-Memory, 2511.04234, the adaptive-consistency line, or the GEPA line performs this decomposition or runs that control. Our pilot supplies the motivating anomaly: a topically correct retrieved bank fixed **zero** held-out items and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031, p=0.016, replicated), harm scaled with injection volume rather than content, and a null replicate with no treatment reproduced the best treatment's apparent gain.

Test-time-augmentation work (arXiv:2608.09351) shows input-side diversity can Pareto-dominate self-consistency at matched cost; a reminder that the memory-free frontier is stronger than agent-memory papers assume, which is why we take the strongest cheap memory-free configuration as the thing to beat.
Abstract: Agentic memory systems distill past episodes and inject them at inference; recent preprints (MemRL, MemDelta) have begun to hold their compute accounting honest. We take compute-matching as given and ask the next question: is there any regime where injected experience buys something extra sampling cannot, and if so, does that regime also tell us what a prompt optimizer should be doing instead? We answer with a stratification. Given n memory-free samples an item is a *coverage* failure (gold never sampled), a *selection* failure (gold sampled but outvoted), or solved. Sampling and instruction edits can only convert selection failures; injected experience is the only mechanism that can convert coverage failures; and injection's damage falls on high-agreement solved items — which explains our pilot finding that a topically correct bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven. This gives three decidable claims: always-on memory is off the compute-matched Pareto frontier; agreement-gated memory beats *agreement-gated extra sampling* at matched tokens if and only if a non-trivial share of low-agreement items are repairable coverage failures; and an instruction optimizer and a memory fix near-disjoint item sets, which is the mechanistic case for coupling them. We test this on one task (ReAct multi-hop QA with a local search index) with one model (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) on 800 paired held-out items, using a pre-drawn sample-pool design in which every routing policy, budget point, seed replicate and null replicate is simulated post hoc over recorded rollouts at zero marginal inference cost. Following review we add three arms that cost real compute because they carry claims the pooled reads cannot: an **online self-editing memory** (written during evaluation, not a static bank), a **GEPA-style instruction-optimization** arm for the division-of-labour test, and a single-purpose **14B stratum probe** testing whether the coverage stratum — and hence memory's ceiling — shrinks with model capability. Total ≈82k episode-equivalents, ≈34 GPU-hours on 4×A100. We pre-commit to publishing the bounded null with the measured ceiling as its headline if the decisive contrast ties.
Experiments:
**Fixed setup.** Task: multi-hop QA with a search tool over a local Wikipedia index (BM25 + bge-large rerank; no network latency), ReAct agent, HotpotQA-distractor + HoVer. Splits: 800 paired held-out items, 200 validation items (all thresholds/hyperparameters), 500 training items (bank construction and prompt optimization). Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, vLLM, T=0.7, decoding seed fixed per (item, sample-index) so all conditions are literally paired. Static bank: ExpeL/ReasoningBank-style, distilled by a frontier API model from 4 rollouts on each of 500 training items (insights + successful/failed trajectory summaries); dense retrieval; top-k injected into the system prompt. Compute unit: total tokens (prefill + decode) logged per item; headline contrasts also reported under LLM-call count and measured wall-clock.

**Design principle: sample pools, not per-policy runs.** We draw fixed pools of rollouts once and *simulate* every gate, budget, aggregation rule, seed replicate and null replicate over them post hoc at zero further inference cost. This is why a 20-arm comparison fits in under two days. Three arms cannot be simulated (online memory, optimized instructions, second model) and are budgeted explicitly below.

**E0 — Stratification and ceiling (runs first; go/no-go).** From a designated 8-sample subset of pool A, label each held-out item SOLVED-HIGH (maj@8 correct, top-1 vote share ≥0.75), SOLVED-LOW (maj@8 correct, share <0.75), SELECTION-FAIL (gold present, majority wrong), COVERAGE-FAIL (gold absent from all 8). Compute the **recoverable-coverage ceiling**: fraction of COVERAGE-FAIL items where the memory pool contains the gold answer, minus the reverse loss on other strata. *Gate:* if the ceiling is below ~4 accuracy points we stop the routing arm and publish a bounded null whose headline number is the ceiling, rather than chase an effect below our 3.1-point MDE. E7 (optimizer) and E6 (self-editing) still run, since their claims are about *where* fixes land, not about beating sampling.

**E1 — Compute-matched frontier (primary claim 1).** Accuracy vs. tokens/item for SC(n), n ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,24} from pool A; always-on MEM(k), k ∈ {2,4} at n ∈ {1,2,4,8} and k=8 at n ∈ {1,2,4}; mixed cells placed on the same iso-token contours. Headline: best always-on-memory cell vs. best memory-free cell at ≈1×, 2×, 4× single-sample cost, item-paired, McNemar.

**E2 — Where fixes and breaks live (mechanism).** Paired fixes/breaks by E0 stratum for every memory condition vs. its memory-free counterpart at equal sample count; logistic regression of break (and of fix) on pre-injection agreement, controlling for retrieval score, injected token count, hop count. Stratum labels come from a sample subset disjoint from the outcome being explained.

**E3 — Routing (primary claim 2).** AGM: draw n0=3 memory-free samples; if top-1 vote share ≥ τ answer by majority and never inject; else inject top-k and draw n1 memory-injected samples. τ, k, n1 fitted on validation only. Compared at matched or lower tokens against, in order of threat: (i) **AGS — agreement-gated extra plain sampling** (same n0, same τ, matched tokens spent on n1′ ≥ n1 additional memory-free samples); (ii) **Difficulty-Adaptive-SC-style routing** (same gate, but low-agreement items are conditioned on retrieved *solved training exemplars* rather than distilled insights — pool D); (iii) plain SC at matched tokens; (iv) always-on MEM at matched tokens; (v) injection-rate-matched random gating; (vi) oracle gating (held-out labels) for headroom. (i),(iii)–(vi) are free pool reads; (ii) needs pool D.

**E4 — Is the agreement signal replaceable? (secondary, not a novelty claim).** At matched injection rate: single-sample self-reported confidence (Self-RAG-style, 3 short calls/item), mean/max retrieval score (free), sequence log-prob margin (free). Report AUC for predicting the *sign* of injection's effect plus end-to-end accuracy.

**E5 — Verifier-reranked self-consistency (baseline against "it's just better aggregation").** Log-prob-weighted voting (free from pool A) and self-verification rerank of the top-3 distinct answers (3 short calls/item). If this absorbs AGM's advantage we say so.

**E6 — Self-editing memory, online (added; reviewer-named).** The bank is *empty at test time* and written during a single sequential pass over the 800 held-out items: after each item the frontier reflector distills an entry from that item's rollouts and appends it; retrieval at item i sees only entries from items 1..i−1. Two independent stream orders. Contrasts: (a) online self-editing vs. static bank at matched k and matched tokens, both against the memory-free frontier; (b) does self-editing raise the recoverable-coverage ceiling (it sees test-distribution items) *and* does it raise SOLVED-HIGH breakage; (c) is AGM-style routing still what makes it viable. This converts the study from "static RAG-flavoured injection" to the self-editing memory the track is about, and it is the strongest available test of "your conclusion is an artifact of a weak bank" — stronger than the contradiction-pruning check it replaces.

**E7 — Division of labour with prompt optimization (added; the track's open question 1).** GEPA-style reflective instruction evolution of the ReAct prompt on the 500 training items with a frontier reflector, budget 30 candidates × 100-item minibatches, selection on the 200 validation items. Evaluate three held-out conditions against the base memory-free agent at matched sample count: INSTR (optimized instructions, no memory), MEM (base instructions, static bank at fitted k), INSTR+MEM. Decompose fixes and breaks by E0 stratum (strata defined by the *base* memory-free agent, so all three share a reference frame). The prediction is a disjointness structure: INSTR's fixes concentrate in SELECTION-FAIL, MEM's in COVERAGE-FAIL, their fixed-item sets overlap little, and INSTR+MEM's gain approximates the sum of the two — except inside SOLVED-HIGH, where injection's breakage interferes with whatever the instructions bought.

**E8 — Model-invariance probe (added; single-purpose).** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, 400 held-out items, 8 memory-free + 8 memory-injected (k=4) rollouts. Measures **only** stratum proportions and the recoverable-coverage ceiling — not a replication of the grid. Claim: memory's ceiling shrinks as the coverage stratum shrinks with capability. Directional (n=400).

**Cut from the previous version and why.** Tier-2 code-agent replication (a second task at half power carried no claim the 800-item primary does not); the T=0.3 sweep; the contradiction-pruned-bank check (subsumed by E6, a stronger bank test); k ∈ {1} and the full four-point k sweep at held-out (k=1 kept on validation only); the Adaptive-RAG classifier baseline (redundant with the confidence gate); pool A reduced only where it did not cost the three disjoint 8-draws needed for the noise floor.

**Compute arithmetic (episodes = full ReAct rollouts; short calls counted separately).**
- Pool A (memory-free, base prompt): 24 × 800 = 19,200
- Pool B (static bank): k∈{2,4} at 8 rollouts = 12,800; k=8 at 4 = 3,200 → 16,000
- Pool D (solved-exemplar bank, DASC baseline, k=4): 4 × 800 = 3,200
- Pool S (E6 online self-editing): 2 orders × 4 × 800 = 6,400
- Pool P (E7 optimized instructions, no memory): 8 × 800 = 6,400
- Pool PB (E7 optimized instructions + bank): 4 × 800 = 3,200
- Optimizer search rollouts: 30 candidates × 100 items = 3,000
- Validation pools: 200 × (16 memory-free + 8 each at k∈{2,4,8}) = 8,000
- Static bank construction: 500 × 4 = 2,000
**7B subtotal: 67,400 episodes.** Short calls: 4,800 (confidence gate + verifier rerank) ≈ 1,500 episode-equivalents.
- E8 (14B): 400 × 16 = 6,400 episodes ≈ 12,800 7B-equivalents.
**Total ≈ 82,000 7B-episode-equivalents.** At ~2,500 generated + ~15,000 prefill tokens per episode with batched vLLM on 4×A100 and a local retrieval index, ~1.5 s/episode amortized (conservative) → **≈ 34 GPU-hours, under two days on the node.** Frontier API: 2,000 static-bank distillations + 1,600 online writes (E6) + ~60 optimizer reflections + 300-item judge audit ≈ **$250**. Every gate, budget point, aggregation rule, seed replicate and the 200-split null replicate in E1/E3/E4/E5 is a post-hoc read of the pools and costs zero further inference.
Baselines and Ablations:
Baselines that could plausibly win, in order of threat:
1. **AGS — agreement-gated extra plain sampling** (same trigger τ, same n0, matched tokens, no memory). Pre-registered primary competitor. If AGM ties AGS, adaptive compute allocation explains everything and memory contributes nothing.
2. **Difficulty-Adaptive-SC-style routing** — same gate, low-agreement items conditioned on retrieved solved exemplars instead of distilled insights. Now implemented and run (reviewer-named), doubling as a bank-content ablation.
3. **Plain self-consistency at matched tokens** — the SC(n) frontier. If AGM cannot beat this the method claim dies even if the stratification survives.
4. **Verifier / log-prob-reranked self-consistency at matched tokens** — controls for "AGM is just better aggregation".
5. **Always-on memory at matched tokens with sample count reduced accordingly** — what current agent-memory papers effectively report once budgets are equalized.
6. **Online self-editing memory (E6)** — the form of memory the track is about; also the strongest-bank control.
7. **Optimized instructions without memory (E7 INSTR)** — the competing mechanism, and the other half of the division-of-labour claim.
8. **Volume reduction (always-on k=2)** — the pilot's cheap neutralizer of memory harm.
9. **Self-reported-confidence gating (Self-RAG-style)** — an existing gate needing no extra samples.
10. **Injection-rate-matched random gating** — isolates the gate's information content from the mere fact of injecting less.
11. **Oracle gate** — upper bound on any routing policy over this bank.

Ablations (free pool reads unless noted): (a) n0 ∈ {1,2,3,5}, pricing the gate; (b) gate statistic: top-1 vote share vs. answer entropy vs. pairwise agreement; (c) reuse vs. discard the n0 gate samples in the final vote; (d) **unmatched-budget arm** — inject memory while holding sample count fixed, quantifying how many points of published memory "gains" are budget rather than memory; (e) k ∈ {2,4,8} injection-volume sweep, replicating the pilot's causal lever under the stratification; (f) E6 stream-order replicate; (g) E7 INSTR+MEM stratum interference decomposition.
Falsifiable Predictions:
**P1 (primary; compute-matched dominance of sampling over always-on memory).** At the 2× and 4× token budgets the best always-on-memory cell loses to the best memory-free cell by ≥3 points, and no MEM cell lies on the Pareto frontier. *Refutation:* some MEM(k)+SC(n) cell beats every SC(n′) at matched tokens beyond the noise floor — current evaluations were compute-fair after all and our premise fails.

**P2 (confirmatory; stratified mechanism).** ≥60% of memory's fixes fall in COVERAGE-FAIL, a stratum we expect to be 10–20% of items; break odds rise with pre-injection agreement, OR ≥1.4 per SD of vote share, 95% CI excluding 1.0. *Refutation:* fixes and breaks uniform across strata — agreement carries no routing information and the entire mechanism collapses.

**P3 (confirmatory).** AGM beats always-on memory at equal tokens by ≥3 points while injecting on ≤40% of items.

**P4 (primary; the decisive claim).** AGM beats **AGS** — agreement-gated extra plain sampling at the same trigger and matched tokens — by ≥3 points, with the advantage concentrated in COVERAGE-FAIL. *Refutation:* parity within the noise floor. Pre-committed headline in that case: "for this class of agent memory on this task family, the compute is better spent on samples; the recoverable-coverage ceiling is X points and the realized gain is 0" — the E0 ceiling makes the null quantitative rather than merely underpowered.

**P5 (confirmatory).** AGM beats injection-rate-matched random gating by ≥3 points. *Refutation:* parity — the benefit is injecting less, consistent with the pilot's volume finding, fatal to routing but leaving P1 intact.

**P6 (confirmatory; division of labour — the coupling claim).** Instruction optimization's fixes are ≥60% in SELECTION-FAIL and ≤15% in COVERAGE-FAIL; memory's fixes show the mirror pattern; the Jaccard overlap of the two fixed-item sets is <0.25; and INSTR+MEM's net gain is within 1.5 points of INSTR-alone + MEM-alone outside SOLVED-HIGH, while inside SOLVED-HIGH it is strictly below additive (injection breaks items instructions had fixed). *Refutation:* both mechanisms act on the same stratum and their fixes overlap heavily — the coupling is redundant rather than complementary, and the field's "combine A and B" results are double-counting one effect.

**P7 (confirmatory; self-editing).** Online self-editing memory raises the recoverable-coverage ceiling over the static bank by ≥2 points (it sees test-distribution items) *and* raises SOLVED-HIGH break rate by ≥1.5×, so that unrouted it still fails to beat the memory-free frontier at matched tokens, while routed (AGM over the self-editing bank) it is the best memory configuration in the study. *Refutation:* self-editing beats the memory-free frontier unrouted — the harm is a static-bank artifact and our mechanism is a property of stale banks only, which we would report as such.

**P8 (directional, n=400).** At 14B the COVERAGE-FAIL stratum is proportionally smaller than at 7B and the recoverable-coverage ceiling is correspondingly lower. *Refutation:* stratum proportions are flat or coverage grows with scale — memory's headroom does not shrink with capability, which materially strengthens the case for agent memory and we say so.
Measurement and Noise Control:
**Pairing.** Every simulated condition is read off the same recorded rollouts on the same 800 items with the same per-(item, sample-index) decoding seeds, so AGM and its gate-matched controls share the identical n0 gate samples and differ only in what is spent on gated items. Unit of analysis is the per-item outcome change; contrasts use McNemar's exact test with fixes and breaks reported separately, since the pilot showed net deltas can be flat while composition shifts.

**Power/MDE.** With 800 paired items and ~10% discordance (80 discordant pairs), 80% power at α=0.05 needs |fixes − breaks| ≈ 25, i.e. **MDE ≈ 3.1 accuracy points**; at 15% discordance, ≈3.8. All primary and confirmatory thresholds are stated at ≥3 points and we make no claim below that. E8 (n=400, MDE ≈4.5) is labelled directional and never carries a claim on its own.

**Variance without extra compute.** Pool A's 24 rollouts give three disjoint 8-sample draws and pools B/D/S/PB give disjoint 4-sample draws, so every SC/AGM/AGS/MEM cell is reported as mean ± SD over ≥2–3 independent draws at zero extra inference cost. A condition beats another only if the paired test is significant *and* the gap exceeds twice the between-draw SD.

**Null-treatment floor.** Split pool A into two disjoint halves, relabel one "treatment", compute the apparent paired effect; over 200 random splits this yields the null distribution of an effect produced by nothing at all. Nothing is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile — directly answering the pilot finding that a null replicate matched the best real treatment.

**Compute matching is realized, not nominal.** Prefill and decode tokens are logged per item; headline contrasts are subsampled/padded so mean realized token counts differ by <5%. Results are shown as full accuracy-vs-budget curves with item-bootstrap CIs, and additionally under LLM-call and measured-wall-clock accounting, so no single matched point carries the argument.

**Arms that break the pool design, handled explicitly.** E6 (online self-editing) is sequential: the bank state at item *i* depends on items 1..*i*−1, so items are not exchangeable and policies cannot be simulated post hoc. Mitigations: (i) item-paired contrasts against pool A on the identical 800 items; (ii) two independent stream orders, with order treated as a nuisance factor and both reported; a claim requires the same sign in both orders and is otherwise labelled directional; (iii) no thresholds fitted on the E6 stream. E7 (optimizer) fits instructions on training items and selects on validation only; strata are defined by the base memory-free agent so INSTR, MEM and INSTR+MEM share one reference frame; the additivity test in P6 is a pre-registered contrast of observed vs. predicted-additive fix counts with bootstrap CIs.

**Leakage and multiplicity.** Stratum labels come from sample subsets disjoint from the evaluated outcome. τ, k, n0, n1 and all gate thresholds are fit on the 200 validation items only. Two families: **primary** (P1: best-MEM vs. best memory-free at matched budget; P4: AGM vs. AGS) reported uncorrected, since these are the two claims the title makes; **confirmatory** (P2, P3, P5, P6, P7) Holm-corrected within family; everything else (E4, ablations) Holm-corrected and labelled exploratory. Exact-match scoring audited against a frontier judge on a 300-item subsample. A 100-item audit compares simulated-over-pools policy execution against fresh live execution to verify the pool design's fidelity.
Preprint Collision Check:
**This round's literature search returned nothing.** The search tool hit a hard session-wide usage limit and produced no results at all — not an empty result set for our queries, but a tool failure. We therefore have **no new evidence** about collisions from this round, and we explicitly refuse to treat that silence as evidence of novelty. The positioning below is carried over from an earlier successful search and is **unverified as of now**.

Carried-over collisions, restated with their consequences:
- **MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192)** — direct collision with any "compute-matched evaluation of agent memory" protocol claim; it already places Pass@k sampling beside memory systems under a unified frozen-backbone protocol. Consequence: that claim remains withdrawn. Residual distinctions (Pass@k with a verifier is an oracle-flavoured bound, not a deployable single-answer policy; sampling is one baseline there rather than the object of study) are stated but not leaned on.
- **MemDelta (arXiv:2606.29914)** — direct collision, same consequence; cited as establishing budget-matched agent-memory evaluation. Its focus is confound control across LM/embedder/pipeline, not an item-level decomposition.
- **arXiv:2511.04234 (compute multiplier)** — partial collision; compute-comparable self-consistency vs. retrieval, but for document RAG (knowledge the model lacks), no procedural agent memory, no fix/break stratification.
- **Evo-Memory (arXiv:2511.20857)** — adjacent and supportive; a trivial ExpRAG baseline beats fancier self-evolving memory. Strengthens our premise; does not pre-empt the mechanism.
- **Adaptive-Consistency (EMNLP 2023) and Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency (2025)** — direct collision with "the gate is free", which remains withdrawn. Difficulty-Adaptive SC is the nearest hybrid and both reviewers flagged its proximity; **we now implement and run it as a baseline (E3-ii)**, converting a novelty risk into a head-to-head. It does not stratify by coverage vs. selection failure and does not run the agreement-gated-plain-sampling control.
- **arXiv:2608.09351 (test-time augmentation at matched compute)** — adjacent; motivates including verifier-reranked SC in the memory-free frontier.
- **MIPRO / GEPA and the ExpeL / Reflexion / ReasoningBank line** — the two halves of E7. They are the object of study, not competitors; the specific gap is that combinations of the two are reported end-to-end without a stratum-level decomposition of which component fixed what.

**What we believe survives, stated as a belief rather than a verified fact:** the item-level coverage/selection stratification, the measured recoverable-coverage ceiling, the AGM-vs-AGS control, and the stratum-decomposed disjointness test between an instruction optimizer and a self-editing memory. **Commitment:** before submission we will run a structured search over arXiv, ACL Anthology, OpenReview, and NeurIPS/ICML proceedings with the queries "compute-matched agent memory", "self-consistency vs experience retrieval", "when does retrieved experience hurt", "coverage vs selection failure sampling", "prompt optimization and memory division of labour", and update positioning — including, if a collision appears, demoting the affected claim as we did twice already.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **The ceiling may be too small to detect.** If COVERAGE-FAIL is small or the bank recovers little of it, memory's maximum achievable gain sits below the 3.1-point MDE. E0 runs first and cheaply as a go/no-go; below ~4 points of recoverable coverage we publish a bounded null with the ceiling as the number. E6 and E7 still run, since their claims concern *where* fixes land.
2. **The paper now stands on two legs, and both can break.** If P2 fails (fixes/breaks uniform across strata) the mechanism collapses and what remains is one more compute-matched replication. If P6 fails (optimizer and memory fix the same items) the coupling claim collapses — though that result is itself informative, since the coupling literature assumes complementarity without testing it. We state this rather than hedge it.
3. **Token accounting favours sampling.** Prefill is cheaper in wall-clock than decode on modern serving stacks, so iso-token may under-credit memory. Mitigation: report iso-call and measured-latency curves alongside iso-token, and state under which basis each conclusion holds.
4. **E6 is statistically weaker than the rest of the study.** Online writing forbids pool simulation; with two stream orders and 800 items we can detect ~3-point effects per order but cannot separate order variance finely. Any E6 conclusion requires sign agreement across orders and is otherwise reported as directional.
5. **E7's optimizer is one optimizer at one budget.** A stronger search (larger GEPA budget, demonstration slot included) could relocate fixes across strata. We fit the instruction slot only — deliberately, since letting the optimizer own demonstrations would confound the division-of-labour test — and flag that as the scope limit.
6. **Scope is deliberately narrow: one task family, one primary model, answer-aggregation tasks.** Self-consistency is ill-defined for open-ended long-horizon web agents and we make no claim there. E8 is a single-purpose probe of stratum proportions at 14B, not a replication; a two-model probe cannot distinguish "memory loses to sampling in general" from "small models have unusually large selection strata", and we present P8 as directional evidence about a trend, not as a scaling law.
7. **Pool-design assumptions.** Simulating policies over pre-drawn pools requires memory-injected rollouts to be drawn independently of gate decisions (they are; pools are drawn for all items) and τ selection not to leak (it cannot; validation is disjoint). Policies are evaluated on i.i.d. resampled rollouts rather than fresh online execution; a 100-item live-execution audit verifies agreement.
8. **Frontier-model dependence in the write path.** Both the static bank and E6's online writes are distilled by an API model; a weaker self-hosted reflector would change bank quality. We report reflector identity and cost, and note that this makes our memory arms, if anything, *stronger* than a fully self-hosted pipeline — which cuts against, not for, our predicted null.

Name: decorative_retriever
Title: When Is a Retriever Decorative? Retrieval-Set Overlap Predicts Whether Procedural Agent Memory Must Be Retrieved or Can Be Frozen
Short Hypothesis: Per-instance retrieval in procedural agent memory (ExpeL/ReasoningBank/Memp-style) is decorative in exactly the regimes the field evaluates in, and there is a cheap, pre-deployment statistic that says when. Concretely: (a) **the frozen-subset swap** — replacing top-k retrieval with the *same k items, fixed for every query, verbatim, no LLM rewriting* — costs <2 accuracy points in every cell whose measured top-k retrieval-set Jaccard overlap exceeds 0.5; (b) that same overlap statistic, computable from the retriever alone in seconds with zero agent rollouts, predicts the retrieval premium **out of sample** across ~20 cells spanning overlap 0.05–1.0, with all overlap<0.25 cells showing a premium ≥8 points; and (c) the sign of the injection-volume effect is the *same* function of overlap — more retrieved items hurt at high overlap and help at low overlap, which reinterprets ReasoningBank's own "retrieving more memories hurts" ablation (49.7%@k=1 → 44.4%@k=4) as a redundancy artifact of a low-diversity retrieval set rather than a general "quality over quantity" law. One measured quantity, two phenomena, no agent runs required to predict either.
Related Work:
**(1) The systems under test.** ExpeL (arXiv:2308.10144, AAAI 2024) "autonomously gathers experiences and extracts knowledge using natural language from a collection of training tasks" and at inference "recalls its extracted insights and past experiences." ReasoningBank (arXiv:2509.25140, Sept 2025) "stores high-level strategies and reasoning hints rather than reusing successful trajectories, procedural workflows, or instance-level concepts," distilling items from self-judged successes and failures. Memp (arXiv:2508.06433, Aug 2025) formalizes procedural memory as "Build, Retrieve, and Update." All three are architected as retrieval systems and all three are evaluated against *no memory* at a fixed scaffold. None reports what happens when the retriever is replaced by a fixed subset of its own bank.

**(2) The published result we intend to reinterpret.** ReasoningBank's own ablation reports that "retrieving more memories actually hurts performance: success rate drops from 49.7% at k=1 to 44.4% at k=4," concluding that "quality and relevance of retrieved memory matter far more than quantity." *Neural Procedural Memory* (arXiv:2606.29824, June 2026) reports the same shape from a different angle: "minimal pools fail to separate the core procedural signal from instance-level noise, overly large pools introduce cross-task interference." Both read the k-curve as a signal/noise or interference property of the *pool*. Our account says it is a property of the *retrieval set's diversity*: when top-k sets are near-identical across queries, additional items are redundant, so k buys interference without information; when they are not, k buys coverage. These accounts differ in sign on a cell we run (Falsifiable Prediction 6): diversifying the retriever (MMR) at fixed pool size and fixed k should remove the large-k harm on our account and leave it intact on theirs.

**(3) The closest recent work, and the reason our contribution is a law rather than a direction.** *A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents* (arXiv:2511.21730, Nov 2025) is the single strongest threat and also our best mechanistic ally. It builds ALFWorld corpora of expert and LLM-generated trajectories, evaluates six retrieval methods, finds a "generalization cliff" where embedding methods degrade on novel contexts while "LLM-generated procedural abstractions demonstrate reliable cross-context transfer," and shows via controlled ablations that "embeddings fundamentally treat procedures as unordered bags of words, discarding temporal structure." That is precisely the mechanism that would make procedural top-k sets collapse to near-identical across queries — it predicts our mediator. But it evaluates *retrieval in isolation from task execution* (does the retriever return a functionally equivalent procedure), not end-to-end agent accuracy; it never freezes a subset and re-runs the agent; it does not token-match; and it offers no statistic that predicts, before deployment, whether the read path will pay. We take the direction as partly established by them and stake the paper on the predictive law and the end-to-end swap.

**(4) Converging evidence that the premise holds, which we concede rather than rediscover.** *Scaling Small Agents Through Strategy Auctions* (arXiv:2602.02751, 2026) reports exactly the saturation we predicted: "the critical transition is from M=0 to M>0 … beyond this point, increasing memory size yields only small further improvements within seed-level noise." *Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents* / SkillsBench (arXiv:2606.23127, 2026) notes that "end-to-end agent benchmarks score full pipelines without separating the skill artifact from planning, retrieval, or tool use" and that "retrieval from large noisy corpora collapses much of the gain." *Procedural Memory Distillation* (arXiv:2607.01480, July 2026) documents bank growth plateauing at fixed per-problem capacity. Our bank-size sweep is therefore **not** a novelty claim; it is one knob on the diversity dial, and we say so.

**(5) Counter-evidence we must confront.** *Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents* (arXiv:2511.22074, Nov 2025) reports procedural memory raising reliability 74.5% → 79.0%, attributing it to memory "suppress[ing] unwanted stochastic variance by biasing decisions toward previously successful trajectories under similar states." That mechanism is fully compatible with our claim — a *frozen* bias would suppress variance identically — and we state the check: their gain should survive a frozen-subset swap. If in our hands a comparable gain does *not* survive, we are wrong.

**(6) Offline consolidation is prior art for the write path, not the read path.** *Auto-Dreamer* (arXiv:2605.20616, 2026) summarizes AWM as inducing "reusable workflows abstracted from successful trajectories, with memory growth tied to the diversity of induced workflows rather than the number of trajectories, leading to compact stores," with Memp in between. AWM already compiles; it still *retrieves* the compiled workflow per instance. Our object is the read path that every one of these systems keeps.

**(7) The RAG-vs-long-context parallel, which a reviewer correctly raised.** Comparing per-query retrieval against stuffing the corpus into context is a familiar question in factual RAG. We do not claim the question is new in general; we claim the answer is *regime-dependent* and that the regime is measurable. Factual corpora sit at low overlap — different questions genuinely need different documents — which is why retrieval wins there. Procedural banks sit at high overlap because their items are strategy-level and near-universal. Our law is stated over the same axis and predicts the RAG finding as its low-overlap limit; if it does not, the law is falsified.

**(8) Instruction/demonstration containers.** GEPA (arXiv:2507.19457) and the reflective-optimizer family treat the instruction as the learned container. We deliberately do **not** run an optimizer (see Experiments); the compiled-static arm is a *lower bound* on that container, which makes a tie conservative for us and makes the optimizer question moot in the regimes where the tie holds.
Abstract:
Procedural agent memory is built as a retrieval system — distil training episodes into a bank, retrieve top-k per instance, inject — and every evaluation we can find compares it against *no memory*. Nobody re-runs the agent with the retriever replaced by a fixed subset of its own bank.

We do, and we do it across a designed sweep of retrieval-set diversity. The centerpiece is the **frozen-subset swap**: hold the agent, tools, decoding, bank, item count and injected tokens fixed, and replace per-instance top-k retrieval with the *k most frequently retrieved items on a dev split, verbatim, identical for every query*. No frontier model touches this arm, so a null cannot be attributed to a clever compiler. We run this swap in ~20 cells spanning measured top-k Jaccard overlap from ~0.05 to 1.0, moving overlap by four independent knobs — task-family breadth (single ALFWorld task type vs. all six vs. a mixed ALFWorld+multi-hop-QA bank), bank size (N=100→1000), retriever (dense vs. BM25 vs. MMR-diversified), and injection budget (k∈{1,3,7}) — plus a non-compilable near-duplicate bank as the low-overlap anchor.

Three claims, in order of how much of the paper they carry. **(i)** Wherever overlap > 0.5, the frozen-subset swap costs < 2 points (TOST equivalence at a 4-point margin; random-effects meta-estimate CI excluding 4). **(ii)** Overlap, computed from the retriever alone with zero agent rollouts, predicts the retrieval premium *out of sample* (leave-one-cell-out, permutation-tested against a grand-mean predictor), with a fitted crossing threshold — this is a deployable diagnostic, not a benchmark number. **(iii)** The sign of the injection-volume effect is the same function of overlap, which reinterprets ReasoningBank's published k-ablation (49.7%@k=1 → 44.4%@k=4, read as "quality over quantity") as a redundancy artifact, and makes an opposite-sign prediction to the interference account of Neural Procedural Memory (2606.29824) in an MMR-retriever cell we run.

We implement both ExpeL-style and ReasoningBank-style bank construction, token-match every static arm to the retrieval arm per instance, include an off-domain compiled control to rule out "any well-written static block of this length helps," and pre-register gates under which the study is reported as uninterpretable. ~23k evaluation episodes, three base models (8B/14B/32B), instance-paired McNemar and TOST, null replicates, stated MDE. No prompt optimizer is run; that arm was cut on purpose.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT.** ReAct scaffold, tool stack, step limit, similarity function, decoding temperature and seed schedule, the training split from which every bank derives, and the held-out test split. Only the *memory-injection arm* varies. The instruction is the same hand-written scaffold in every cell of the centerpiece — there is no optimizer in this proposal.

**MODELS.** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is the load-bearing agent (vLLM, two TP=2 replicas). Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (TP=4) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct replicate the core cells; because no arm requires optimizer rollouts, cross-model breadth is cheap and is spent on the claim that carries the paper. A frontier API model performs bank distillation (both ExpeL-style and ReasoningBank-style) and offline compilation, used identically across conditions. Scoring is programmatic (normalized EM/F1; ALFWorld task success) — no LLM judge on the critical path.

**ENVIRONMENTS AND THE DIVERSITY DIAL.** The dial is the experiment; environments are how we build it.
- *E1:* tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a Wikipedia search tool, 600 held-out instances (360 HotpotQA-distractor, 240 MuSiQue), ~6 LLM calls/episode.
- *E2:* ALFWorld, whose six task types give an *internal* heterogeneity knob. **E2-narrow:** bank and test restricted to a single task type (pick-and-place), n=100 — maximum overlap. **E2-broad:** bank and test span all six types, n=140.
- *E-mix:* a single bank built from ALFWorld items *and* E1 QA items, evaluated on each test set separately. Retrieval must route across procedurally disjoint families; a single static block must hold both. This is the reviewer-requested heterogeneous condition, built inside budget by mixing what we already have rather than importing AFTER.
- *B-dup:* the low-overlap anchor — distilled items for training instances that are deliberate paraphrase near-duplicates of specific held-out test instances. Instance-specific by construction, cannot fit in a bounded static block.

Overlap is *measured*, not assumed, in every cell.

**BANK CONSTRUCTIONS.**
- **B_expel(N)**: ExpeL-style distilled insights + condensed trajectories, N ∈ {100, 250, 500, 1000} on E1; N ∈ {100, 200} on E2.
- **B_rbank(500)**: ReasoningBank-style construction as described in 2509.25140 — self-judged success/failure items, strategy-and-reasoning-hint granularity, consolidation. Added because the paper names ReasoningBank; a claim about it must be backed by an implementation of it.
- **B_raw(500)**: undistilled trajectories (separates "value of distillation" from "value of any exposure").
- **B_offdomain(500)**: distilled bank from an unrelated task family, used only for the content control.

**ARMS (all token-matched per instance to the retrieval arm at the same cell).**
- **A0** — no memory (floor).
- **A_ret** — per-instance top-k dense retrieval. k is chosen per (env, bank) on a 150-instance dev split to *maximize A_ret accuracy*, so retrieval is evaluated at its own best setting; ReasoningBank reports k=1 as optimal in their setup and we will not handicap them by fixing k=7.
- **A_fix** — **the frozen-subset swap, primary arm.** The k items with the highest dev-split retrieval frequency, injected verbatim, identical for every test instance. No LLM rewriting, no summarization, same item count, same tokens.
- **A_rand** — random fixed subset of k items, 3 independent draws, on a 300-instance subsample. Lower bound on A_fix; distinguishes "the popular items are the useful ones" from "any k items work."
- **A_comp** — one static instruction compiled offline by the frontier model from the *entire* bank (hierarchical two-pass for large N), token-matched, retriever deleted. This is the deployment arm and the pigeonhole probe.
- **A_scram** — A_comp built from B_offdomain, token-matched. Rules out "any structured static block of this length helps."
- **A_mmr** — retrieval with MMR diversification at the same bank and k. The knob that separates our redundancy account from the interference account.

**PRIMARY AND SECONDARY ENDPOINTS.**
- **R_fix = acc(A_ret) − acc(A_fix)**, instance-paired. *Primary.* Does query-conditioning do anything, with no frontier model anywhere in the comparison?
- **R = acc(A_ret) − acc(A_comp)**, instance-paired. *Secondary/deployment.* Can you delete the retriever in practice?
- **V = acc(k=7) − acc(k=1)** at fixed bank. *Volume-sign endpoint.*
- **Overlap O** = mean pairwise Jaccard of top-k sets across test instances (primary diagnostic), with bank coverage and item-usage entropy as pre-registered secondaries. Computed from the retriever alone, no agent calls.

**CENTERPIECE — the frozen-subset swap across the diversity dial.**

E1, Qwen2.5-14B, n=600 unless noted:

| Cell | Arms | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| A0 × 2 decoding seeds | — | floor + null replicate |
| B_expel N∈{100,250,500,1000}, k* | A_ret, A_comp | R vs bank size (pigeonhole probe) |
| B_expel N∈{500,1000}, k* | A_fix | R_fix at two bank sizes |
| B_expel N=500 | A_ret@k=1, A_ret@k=7, A_fix@k=7 | volume-sign endpoint V |
| B_expel N=500, k=7 | A_mmr | redundancy vs interference |
| B_raw N=500, k* | A_ret | distillation contribution |
| B_offdomain N=500 | A_scram | static-content control |
| B_rbank N=500, k* | A_ret, A_comp, A_fix | claim about ReasoningBank, backed by ReasoningBank |
| E-mix bank (500), k*, tested on E1 | A_ret, A_comp, A_fix | low-overlap cell |
| B-dup, n=300 | A_ret, A_comp, A_fix | low-overlap anchor / positive control |
| B_expel N=500, n=300 | A_rand × 3 draws | frozen-subset lower bound |

E2, Qwen2.5-14B:
- E2-narrow (n=100): A0, A_ret, A_comp, A_fix — the maximum-overlap end of the dial.
- E2-broad (n=140): A0 × 2 seeds, A_ret, A_comp, A_fix, plus A_ret@k=1 and A_ret@k=7.
- E-mix tested on ALFWorld (n=140): A_ret, A_comp, A_fix.

Cross-model (E1, n=300 subsample, no optimizer needed): Qwen2.5-32B and Llama-3.1-8B × {A0, A_ret(N=500,k*), A_comp, A_fix, A_ret-dup, A_fix-dup}. The 8B and 32B arms probe opposite failure modes: a small model may fail to exploit a long static block while still using concrete exemplars; a large model may make the read path redundant for capability rather than information reasons. We report per model and never pool.

**THE LAW (the result the paper stands on).** Every cell yields a measured O and a paired R_fix (and, where run, R). We fit R_fix ~ O with cell-level random effects and the A_ret−A0 memory gain as a covariate (so "cells where memory does nothing" cannot masquerade as "cells where retrieval is decorative"). The decisive test is **leave-one-cell-out prediction**: predict each held-out cell's R_fix from O alone and compare prediction error against a grand-mean predictor, with a permutation null that shuffles O across cells. We report the fit with and without B-dup, and require it to survive on non-synthetic cells alone (Spearman ρ ≤ −0.6). Deliverable: the overlap statistic and threshold, shipped as a pre-deployment diagnostic with reference code, computable in seconds before a single episode is run.

**PRECHECK GATES (reported either way).** On a 150-instance dev split: (G1) each bank must beat A0 by ≥8 points at k*, or that cell's premium comparison is vacuous and is reported as "memory inert here"; (G2) B-dup must yield R_fix ≥ 10, or the instrument cannot detect instance-specific value and the study is reported as uninterpretable rather than confirmatory; (G3) the dial must actually span overlap — if all cells land in [0.4, 0.7], the regression is unidentified and we report the sweep as a failed manipulation.

**WHAT IS NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE.** No prompt optimizer (no GEPA, no MIPROv2, no substitution ratio, no coupled-optimization arm). Removing it freed ~9,000 episodes and all optimizer-seed variance — the largest and least-reported noise source in this literature — and bought the diversity dial, the ReasoningBank implementation, and the frozen-subset arm. See changes_made for why this was the right trade and what we give up.

**COMPUTE ARITHMETIC.**
E1, Qwen-14B: 2 (A0) + 8 (bank sweep ×2 arms) + 2 (A_fix) + 3 (k sweep) + 1 (MMR) + 1 (raw) + 1 (scram) + 3 (B_rbank) + 3 (E-mix) = 24 full cells × 600 = 14,400 episodes; plus B-dup 3×300 = 900 and A_rand 3×300 = 900. **E1 ≈ 16,200 episodes ≈ 97k calls.**
E2: narrow 4×100 = 400; broad 5×140 + 2×140 (k sweep) = 980; E-mix 3×140 = 420. **≈ 1,800 episodes ≈ 45k calls.**
Cross-model: 2 × 6 × 300 = 3,600 episodes ≈ 22k calls.
Bank-construction rollouts: ≈ 1,500 episodes ≈ 12k calls.
**Total ≈ 23,100 episodes / ~176k LLM calls**, ≤ 600 episodes per reported cell, ~3–4 days wall clock at vLLM throughput on 4×A100.
**API:** distillation of ~1,500 training episodes under two pipelines ≈ $25; ~10 hierarchical whole-bank compilations ≈ $20; B-dup paraphrase generation ≈ $5. **Total ≈ $50.**
**Ordered contingency cuts:** A_rand → B_rbank arm → Llama-8B → bank sizes {250} → E-mix on ALFWorld. **Never cut:** the frozen-subset swap across the E1 diversity dial, the E2-narrow vs. E2-broad contrast, B-dup, the 32B replication. Those four are the law.
Baselines and Ablations:
**OUTCOMES THAT WOULD REFUTE US AND WHICH WE REPORT AS THE PRIMARY RESULT IF THEY OCCUR.**
(i) **R_fix ≥ 4 points with CI excluding 2 in high-overlap cells.** Per-instance conditioning carries real information even where retrieval sets barely differ. The paper's central claim is dead and the field's architecture is vindicated.
(ii) **Overlap fails the leave-one-out prediction test** (no better than grand mean under permutation). Even if R_fix ≈ 0 everywhere, we then have a null without a mechanism — a weaker and much less interesting paper, and we say so in the abstract rather than burying it.
(iii) **V > 0 in high-overlap cells** (more retrieved items help where sets are near-identical). The redundancy account is wrong and ReasoningBank's k-curve needs a different explanation.
(iv) **A_mmr does not remove the large-k harm.** The interference account of 2606.29824 wins over ours on its own turf.
(v) **A_scram ≈ A_comp.** Then the static arms are riding on generic well-written text, not bank content, and both our null and the memory literature's positive results are about prompt length and style. This is a threat to our framing as much as to theirs.
(vi) **A_rand ≈ A_fix ≈ A_ret.** Any k items work; the bank contains nothing task-specific and the object we are studying is emptier than either we or the memory papers claim.

**ABLATIONS THAT ISOLATE THE MECHANISM.**
- **A_fix (frozen verbatim subset)** — the primary arm, and the direct answer to the "your compiler is doing the work" confound: no frontier model appears in the R_fix comparison at all.
- **A_rand × 3 draws** — separates "the popular items are the right items" from "any items."
- **A_scram (off-domain compiled, token-matched)** — separates bank content from generic static text of that length.
- **{ExpeL-style, ReasoningBank-style, raw} bank constructions** — the claim names three systems; three constructions are implemented.
- **Four independent overlap knobs** (task-family breadth, bank size, retriever, k) — a mediator that only moves under one manipulation is an artifact; requiring the law to hold across all four is the strongest version of the test we can afford.
- **k chosen on dev to maximize retrieval accuracy** — retrieval is evaluated at its own best budget, so a tie cannot be dismissed as a handicapped k.
- **Per-instance token matching, audited** — reported as measured distributions and as accuracy-vs-token-residual, not as an intention.
- **E2-narrow vs. E2-broad** — the same environment, same agent, same bank pipeline, differing only in task-family breadth. If overlap is the mediator, R_fix must differ between these two cells; nothing else does.
- **B-dup** — converts a null into a finding, and anchors the low-overlap end of the regression.
- **Shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check** — confirms the retriever functions in A_ret.
- **A0 null replicates in both environments** — no effect claimed below the 95th percentile of the treatment-free delta distribution.
Falsifiable Predictions:
1. **Frozen-subset swap (primary).** In every cell with measured overlap O > 0.5, R_fix = acc(A_ret) − acc(A_fix) < 2 points; per-cell TOST equivalence at a 4-point margin passes in ≥8 of the ~11 such cells; the random-effects meta-estimate over those cells has a 95% CI excluding 4 points.
2. **The law, tested out of sample.** Across all ~20 cells, leave-one-cell-out prediction of R_fix from O alone beats a grand-mean predictor with permutation p < 0.05. Every cell with O < 0.25 has R_fix ≥ 8; every cell with O > 0.5 has R_fix < 2. The fitted crossing threshold is reported with a bootstrap CI. Excluding the synthetic B-dup cells, Spearman ρ(O, R_fix) ≤ −0.6.
3. **Retriever deletion in practice.** R = acc(A_ret) − acc(A_comp) < 2 in all O > 0.5 cells, and does not increase with bank size: the slope of R on log N has a CI containing zero up to N = 1000 on E1.
4. **Heterogeneity, not just synthetic duplicates.** The E-mix cell (bank spanning ALFWorld + multi-hop QA) has O < 0.3 and R_fix ≥ 5; E2-narrow (single ALFWorld task type) has O > 0.7 and R_fix < 2. The narrow-vs-broad contrast within ALFWorld shows R_fix increasing by ≥3 points as task-family breadth rises. This is the prediction that decides whether our claim is about procedural memory or only about template-repeating benchmarks.
5. **Positive control.** On B-dup, R_fix ≥ 10 with CI excluding 0, in ≥2 of the 3 models. Without this, predictions 1–4 are reported as uninterpretable.
6. **Volume-sign flip, and a discriminating test against the interference account.** V = acc(k=7) − acc(k=1) is negative in O > 0.5 cells and positive in the E-mix and B-dup cells, with the sign predicted by O. Further, in the O > 0.5 cell at k=7, MMR-diversified retrieval recovers ≥3 points over dense retrieval at the *same* bank size and k. The interference account (2606.29824) predicts the harm is pool-size-driven and survives diversification; we predict it is redundancy-driven and does not. Opposite outcomes on a cell we run.
7. **Compiler skill is not the explanation.** |acc(A_comp) − acc(A_fix)| < 3 points at matched tokens in O > 0.5 cells, and acc(A_scram) sits ≥6 points below both. A_rand falls ≥3 points below A_fix (the popular items are not arbitrary) while still landing within 3 points of A_ret in the highest-overlap cell.
8. **Construction is not load-bearing.** B_rbank and B_expel agree within 3 points on all three arms at N=500, and |acc(A_ret over B_raw) − acc(A_ret over B_expel)| < 3 at matched tokens. If so, ReasoningBank's reported superiority over raw-trajectory memory does not survive token matching in our setup — stated as a qualification of a published claim, with our own scaffold differences disclosed.
9. **Reconciliation with reported positives.** In cells where memory beats A0 by ≥8 points (the regime 2511.22074 reports), the *entire* gain survives the frozen-subset swap: acc(A_fix) − acc(A0) ≥ 0.8 × [acc(A_ret) − acc(A0)].

**REFUTATION CONDITIONS.** (a) R_fix ≥ 4 with CI excluding 2 in any two independent O > 0.5 cells → the read path carries per-instance information; central claim dead. (b) Failure of prediction 2's out-of-sample test → the diagnostic, which is the paper's deliverable, does not exist; we report a null without a mechanism and say the contribution is reduced to a replication of the direction already indicated by 2511.21730 and 2602.02751. (c) R_fix ≈ 0 on B-dup → instrument broken, study reported as uninterpretable. (d) Failure of G3 (dial does not span overlap) → the manipulation failed and the regression is unidentified; reported as such. Predictions 1 and 2 are reported separately and neither is allowed to carry the other: a flat null with no overlap dependence is a *different, weaker* result than a predictive law, and we will not present the former as the latter.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Four variance sources, handled separately.

**(a) Evaluation variance.** Every held-out instance runs under every arm within a cell with the same seed schedule; all endpoints are within-instance. Primary tests: exact McNemar on fix/break counts with Holm correction across the cell family. Every reported delta carries its fix/break decomposition — a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention, and the prior program in this track observed exactly that pattern.

**(b) Equivalence, not just null-hypothesis, testing.** The per-cell claim is a claim of *no* difference, so significance tests are the wrong instrument. TOST at a pre-registered 4-point equivalence margin (the smallest gap the memory literature treats as meaningful, and our single-cell MDE). At n=600 with an expected 15% discordant rate, the SE of the paired difference is ≈1.6 points, so a 90% CI has half-width ≈2.6 and equivalence at margin 4 requires an observed gap ≤1.4. Declared in advance: observed gaps in (1.4, 4) are **inconclusive between equivalence and a small retrieval advantage**, not support. The random-effects meta-estimate over the high-overlap cells (effective n > 5,000 paired observations) is the properly powered version and is the headline for prediction 1.

**(c) The law's own statistics.** The regression of R_fix on O has ~20 cells, which is small. We therefore (i) pre-register O = mean pairwise top-k Jaccard as the single primary diagnostic, with coverage and usage entropy reported as secondaries and never substituted post hoc; (ii) include acc(A_ret) − acc(A0) as a covariate so cells with inert memory cannot drive the fit; (iii) weight cells by the inverse variance of their R_fix estimate; (iv) test by leave-one-cell-out prediction error against a grand-mean predictor with a permutation null over O labels (10k permutations); (v) report the fit with and without the synthetic B-dup cells and require survival on non-synthetic cells alone. Cell-level bootstrap resamples both instances within cells and cells.
