**(d) Null replicates.** In each environment we re-run A0 under a different decoding seed and report the distribution of apparent deltas; on E1 we additionally re-run one full A_ret cell under a second seed. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of the matching null distribution. Load-bearing given prior observations in this track of 5–14 point re-scoring drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment. Note that **no arm in this proposal involves an optimizer**, so the largest and least-reported variance source in this literature is absent by construction — this was a design goal, not an accident.

**Minimum detectable effects.** E1, n=600: paired McNemar MDE ≈ 4 points at 80% power. E1 subsamples (B-dup, A_rand, cross-model), n=300: MDE ≈ 6 — which is why prediction 5 is stated at ≥10, not ≥5. E2-broad, n=140: MDE ≈ 8; E2-narrow, n=100: MDE ≈ 9. The E2 cells are explicitly directional; their role is to populate the overlap axis at its high end and to widen the meta-estimate, not to carry standalone tests. We say this before running rather than after.

**Token-matching audit.** For A_fix, A_rand, A_comp and A_scram we report the measured per-instance injected-token distribution against A_ret's, plus accuracy as a function of the token residual, so a reader can verify a tie was not bought with extra context. Item counts are matched exactly for A_fix and A_rand (same k), which is a stronger match than tokens alone.

**Diagnostic reproducibility.** O is computed from retriever outputs only and requires no agent execution; we release the script and the per-cell O values so any reader can compute it on their own bank in seconds and check whether our threshold transfers.
Preprint Collision Check:
**Grounding.** This check uses only work returned by the literature search run for this revision, plus ExpeL and GEPA, which are named in the calling track. **I explicitly withdraw the previous draft's reliance on MemAPO (2603.21520), EvoClinician (2601.22964), Meta-learning Agentic Memory Designs (2602.07755), Contrastive Reflection (2606.30840) and RePrompt: none were returned by the current search.** An earlier draft of this line of work was caught citing arXiv IDs I could not see in a search result (MemDelta, Memory-R2, A-Mem, and others); reviewers rightly flagged that. My standing rule now: nothing enters the novelty argument unless it appears in a search result I can quote. Every claim of difference below is anchored to quoted text from this search. Note that Memp (2508.06433), previously withdrawn, *was* returned this time and is reinstated.

**CLOSEST WORK — a real partial collision. *A Benchmark for Procedural Memory Retrieval in Language Agents*, arXiv:2511.21730 (Nov 2025).** It "isolates procedural memory retrieval from task execution, evaluating whether agents can recognize functionally equivalent procedures that span different object instantiations," on ALFWorld, across six retrieval methods, and finds that "LLM-generated procedural abstractions demonstrate reliable cross-context transfer" while "embeddings fundamentally treat procedures as unordered bags of words." **This collides with the *direction* of our finding and I concede it.** It does not collide with the contribution: it measures retrieval quality in isolation, never re-runs the agent with a frozen subset, does not token-match, does not compare against a compiled whole-bank instruction, and offers no statistic that predicts before deployment whether the read path will pay. It is also, on our reading, evidence *for* our mediator — bag-of-words retrieval over strategy-level items is exactly what produces near-identical top-k sets. We cite it as mechanistic support and stake novelty on the predictive law, the end-to-end frozen-subset swap, and the volume-sign reinterpretation, none of which it contains.

**SECOND CLOSEST — *Scaling Small Agents Through Strategy Auctions*, arXiv:2602.02751 (2026).** Reports that "the critical transition is from M=0 to M>0 … beyond this point, increasing memory size yields only small further improvements within seed-level noise." **This scoops the bank-size saturation claim outright.** In the previous draft the bank-size sweep was the spine of the paper; it now appears only as one knob on the diversity dial, and I state in Related Work that saturation is established rather than discovered here.

**Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents / SkillsBench, arXiv:2606.23127 (2026).** Notes that benchmarks "score full pipelines without separating the skill artifact from planning, retrieval, or tool use" and that "retrieval from large noisy corpora collapses much of the gain." Same suspicion, adjacent mechanism: they compare no-skill / curated-skill / self-generated-skill *contents* and attribute collapse to corpus noise. They do not freeze the read path, do not token-match, and offer no pre-deployment predictor. Their finding is compatible with both our redundancy account and the interference account; ours is the one that makes a sign prediction under MMR.

**Neural Procedural Memory, arXiv:2606.29824 (June 2026).** The sharpest *mechanistic rival*: "minimal pools fail to separate the core procedural signal from instance-level noise, overly large pools introduce cross-task interference." Same phenomenon, different cause. We give it its own cell and an opposite-sign prediction (Falsifiable Prediction 6). This is a better opponent than the complementarity papers I cited last round, because it is verified in this search and because the disagreement is settled by measurement.

**ReasoningBank, arXiv:2509.25140 (Sept 2025).** A target, not a competitor — and now also a source of the specific published result we intend to qualify: "retrieving more memories actually hurts performance: success rate drops from 49.7% at k=1 to 44.4% at k=4, indicating quality and relevance of retrieved memory matter far more than quantity." Our account says this generalizes only at high overlap. We implement ReasoningBank-style construction rather than proxying it with ExpeL-style distillation, because the previous draft was correctly criticized for naming it without implementing it.

**Real-Time Procedural Learning, arXiv:2511.22074 (Nov 2025).** Direct counter-evidence: procedural memory raised reliability 74.5% → 79.0%, attributed to memory "suppress[ing] unwanted stochastic variance." We treat it as a target of Falsifiable Prediction 9 rather than as a rival framing.

**Auto-Dreamer / AWM, arXiv:2605.20616 (2026).** Reports AWM inducing "reusable workflows abstracted from successful trajectories, with memory growth tied to the diversity of induced workflows rather than the number of trajectories." Prior art for offline abstraction on the *write* path — and note that it independently identifies *diversity* as the quantity that governs memory growth, which is suggestive support for our axis. AWM still retrieves per instance; the read path remains untested.

**ExpeL (2308.10144), Memp (2508.06433), Procedural Memory Distillation (2607.01480).** Canonical targets and bank-dynamics evidence respectively; none removes the retriever.

**RAG-vs-long-context.** Not returned by this search but raised by a reviewer, and I engage it in Related Work rather than distinguishing it in a footnote: the question is not new in general, but the answer is regime-dependent, and our law predicts the RAG result as its low-overlap limit. If procedural cells and factual-RAG cells did not sit at opposite ends of the overlap axis, the law would be falsified.

**The search's verdict, which I adopt:** "No paper found runs the specific controlled design implied by the proposal … The *direction* of the finding (abstraction/static content ≈ or > per-instance retrieval) is converging across several 2025–2026 papers, but the precise mechanism-isolating ablation … appears unaddressed." I accept the first half of that sentence as a genuine constraint on my novelty and have restructured the proposal around it: the direction is not the contribution, the predictive diagnostic and the volume-sign reinterpretation are.

**Residual risk.** I could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions. A "freeze the retrieved subset" ablation could exist in an appendix of a combined-system preprint. Even so, the overlap-based out-of-sample predictor, the four-knob diversity dial, the MMR discriminating test against 2606.29824, and the ReasoningBank k-curve reinterpretation would remain new.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **The law could fail even if the null holds.** If overlap does not predict R_fix out of sample, I am left with a flat null whose direction is already converging in the 2025–26 literature (2511.21730, 2602.02751, 2606.23127). That is a substantially weaker paper and I have written the refutation condition so it cannot be quietly upgraded. This is the single largest risk and it is deliberate: I chose to stake the paper on the explanation rather than the observation.
2. **Twenty cells is a small regression.** The fit is inverse-variance weighted, covariate-adjusted, permutation-tested, and reported with and without the synthetic anchor — but it is still ~20 points. A skeptic can reasonably want 50. I state the effective sample size and do not claim a precise threshold value, only a crossing region with a bootstrap CI.
3. **The overlap statistic may be the wrong summary.** Mean pairwise top-k Jaccard is pre-registered as primary; coverage and usage entropy are reported but cannot be promoted post hoc. If a different statistic fits better, that is a hypothesis for future work, reported as such.
4. **Heterogeneity is manufactured, not naturally occurring.** The low-overlap cells come from mixing two environments and from near-duplicate seeding. Reviewers asked for a genuinely heterogeneous suite (AFTER, arXiv:2606.23127); that is out of budget and I decline to claim its domain. The E2-narrow vs. E2-broad contrast is the closest thing to a naturally occurring diversity manipulation I can afford, and it is a *within-environment* contrast, which is its main virtue.
5. **Precheck failure.** If a bank cannot clear the 8-point gate against no-memory, its premium comparison is vacuous. Reported regardless; a bank that cannot beat no memory is itself an observation about the literature. If the dial fails to span overlap (G3), the regression is unidentified and the manipulation is reported as failed.
6. **Compilation is lossy and bounded.** A_comp depends on a compiler prompt fixed in advance on a 100-instance dev split, reported verbatim, never iterated after seeing test results. It is a lower bound: a tie is conservative evidence for us; a loss is weaker evidence against us than a tie is for us. Compilation must eventually fail as N → ∞; our claim is bounded to N ≤ 1000 on E1 and N ≤ 200 on E2, which brackets the bank sizes ExpeL and ReasoningBank use, and we report the fitted trend so a reader can extrapolate at their own risk. Note that the *primary* endpoint R_fix involves no compilation at all, so this limitation does not touch the main claim.
7. **No prompt optimizer.** The track is framed around coupling memory with prompt optimization and this proposal runs no optimizer. I do not test whether a reflective optimizer beats my compiler, and I cannot report a substitution ratio. My defense: the compiled arm is a lower bound on the instruction container, so in regimes where even the lower bound ties with retrieval, the coupling question is moot — and the law says where those regimes are. If R_fix > 0 somewhere, that is where coupling research should be conducted, and naming that regime is the service I offer the track instead of an underpowered coupling arm.
8. **Model and environment scope.** Three open-weight models up to 32B; two task families plus their mixture. Nothing here speaks to episodic personal memory, long-conversation memory, or factual corpus retrieval — the diagnostic itself is offered as the boundary marker, and it says those regimes sit at low overlap where retrieval should and probably does pay.
9. **Comparisons to published numbers are qualifications, not refutations.** Our scaffold, models and prompts differ from ReasoningBank's. When we say their k-curve reflects a low-diversity regime, we mean it as a testable reinterpretation with our own conditions disclosed, and we will state explicitly that we have not reproduced their setup.

Name: failure_signature_routing
Title: Transfer Is Predicted by How Tasks Fail, Not by What Tasks Are About: A Routing Study for Textual Prompt Transfer
Short Hypothesis: When an optimized prompt from a source task is used to warm-start reflective prompt optimization on a new task, the realized transfer gain is predicted by the similarity of the two tasks' *failure-mode signatures* (a cheap, 10-dimensional profile of how a baseline prompt fails), and only weakly by semantic/task-embedding similarity of the SPoT kind. If true, a router built on failure signatures can select a source (or abstain to cold start) and thereby capture most of the small-budget transfer gain while avoiding negative transfer; if the transfer matrix is dominated by a single universally-good source, or if the matrix has too little seed-to-seed reliability to be predictable at all, the hypothesis is refuted — and we measure that reliability explicitly rather than assuming it.
Related Work: SPoT (Vu et al., 2021) and ATTEMPT establish that soft-prompt transferability is substantial and can be predicted by task embeddings derived from the learned prompt parameters; but soft prompts are model-bound continuous parameters, the study is over classification tasks with full fine-tuning-scale budgets, and the predictor is semantic/parametric task similarity with no notion of failure modes, no budget axis, and no abstention option. 'Exploring and predicting transferability across NLP tasks' (Vu et al., 2020) likewise predicts transfer from TaskEmb/TextEmb similarity for fine-tuning. On the text-prompt side, GEPA (2025), MIPROv2 (2024), OPRO and APE all run cold-start per task and never study which source to transfer from; PromptBreeder evolves operators within a single run. Cross-model prompt transfer work varies the model with the task fixed — the orthogonal axis. What is missing everywhere is (i) a measured, reliability-quantified source×target transfer matrix for *textual* optimized prompts under a matched rollout budget, and (ii) the head-to-head test of failure-signature similarity against semantic similarity as the predictor of that matrix, with a router that can abstain. Our claim is not 'text instead of soft prompts' (a domain swap) but a specific, falsifiable claim about *what feature space transfer lives in* for reflective prompt optimization.
Abstract: Reflective prompt optimizers are re-run from scratch on every task, and the obvious cheap fix — warm-starting from a prompt optimized elsewhere — is unreliable: sometimes it saves a hundred rollouts, sometimes it is worse than starting cold. We ask whether that variability is predictable before paying for it. We measure a full source×target transfer matrix for textual optimized prompts: eight tasks spanning multi-hop QA, symbolic reasoning, code, and instruction following are each optimized with a reimplemented GEPA, and every domain-scrubbed source prompt is then used to seed a budget-capped optimization run on every other task. We first quantify the matrix's split-half reliability across seeds, which upper-bounds any predictor's achievable correlation and which prior transfer studies do not report. We then test two predictors of the matrix: SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, and failure-signature similarity — a 10-dimensional distribution over domain-general failure modes obtained by having a judge model label ~50 baseline rollouts per task, at a cost of well under one percent of an optimization run. Our hypothesis is that transfer in this setting is governed by shared failure structure rather than shared subject matter, so failure signatures should predict the matrix substantially better. We close the loop with a leave-one-target-out router that picks a source or abstains to cold start, evaluated against random-source, best-fixed-source, always-cold-start, and oracle-source baselines on small-budget test accuracy, with paired seeds, bootstrap intervals, and a treatment-free null replicate defining the noise floor.
Experiments:
(1) Noise floor and null replicate. Re-score 20 fixed candidate prompts on each task's held-out set 5 times; estimate per-task metric SD. Run two cold-start GEPA runs per task differing only in seed to bound the apparent 'gain' obtainable from nothing.
(2) Source optimization. Reimplement GEPA (executor: Qwen2.5-7B and 32B served locally; reflector: frontier API model). Optimize 8 tasks (2 BBH clusters, 2 Super-NaturalInstructions clusters, HotpotQA, GSM8K, MBPP, an instruction-following set), 300 rollouts × 3 seeds. Domain-scrub the winning prompt with an LLM (remove task-specific nouns/examples) and verify scrubbing with a source-identification leakage test.
(3) Transfer matrix. For each of 8×7=56 ordered pairs, seed GEPA on the target with the scrubbed source prompt and run to a 50-rollout cap; record test accuracy of the validation-argmax candidate and the AUC of the budget-accuracy curve at checkpoints 0/10/25/50. Transfer gain Δ(s→t) = warm-start metric − paired cold-start metric on the same seed/splits. Run 3 seeds per cell (168 short runs, each ~50 rollouts — the deliberate reason the cap is 50). Also record zero-shot transfer (checkpoint 0), which is nearly free.
(4) Reliability. Split seeds into halves; report split-half Spearman reliability of the 56-cell Δ matrix and its bootstrap CI. This is the ceiling for any predictor and is reported before any predictor is fit.
(5) Failure signatures. For each task, run a fixed seed prompt on 50 dev examples, have a judge model label each failing trace with one of 10 pre-registered domain-general failure modes (format/contract violation, missing decomposition, arithmetic/bookkeeping slip, unsupported claim, instruction omission, premature termination, over-generation, ambiguity mis-resolution, tool/context misuse, spurious refusal); signature = normalized 10-vector. Report inter-judge agreement on 100 double-labeled traces.
(6) Predictor comparison. Predict Δ(s→t) from: (a) failure-signature similarity (cosine / 1−JS), (b) SPoT-style task-embedding similarity of task descriptions and of dev-set inputs, (c) edit-direction similarity (embedding of the seed→optimized prompt diff on the source vs. target's own first-10-rollout diff), (d) source-prompt zero-shot score on the target (checkpoint-0 transfer, the strongest cheap baseline predictor), (e) source main-effect only. Compare Spearman correlations with attenuation correction by the step-4 reliability; significance by paired bootstrap over cells with target-clustered resampling.
(7) Router evaluation. Leave-one-target-out: fit the predictor on 7 targets' rows, on the held-out target choose argmax predicted Δ or abstain (predicted Δ ≤ 0) to cold start. Metric: realized test accuracy at 50 rollouts, and rate of negative-transfer incidents (Δ below −noise floor).
(8) Mechanism separation. Decompose warm-start gain into (i) starting-point quality (checkpoint-0 score), (ii) search direction (fraction of proposed edits with positive validated delta), (iii) output-format compliance measured separately from task accuracy.
Baselines and Ablations:
Baselines for the router: always cold start (wins if transfer is on average useless); random source; best-fixed-source chosen on the 7 training targets (the strong, boring baseline most likely to beat a learned router if one source is universally good — we report it prominently); oracle source (upper bound); zero-shot-score-based routing, which needs no failure taxonomy at all and is the cheapest competitor; SPoT-style semantic-similarity routing. Baselines for the predictor comparison: source main effect + target main effect only (an additive model with no pairwise term — if this explains the matrix, 'similarity' is irrelevant).
Ablations: failure signature computed from 10 vs 50 traces (how cheap can the probe be?); taxonomy coarsened to 3 modes; signature computed on successes as well as failures; scrubbed vs unscrubbed source prompts; warm start as seed candidate vs as an extra Pareto-pool member; second executor model (Llama-3.1-8B) on a 4×3 sub-matrix to test whether the matrix and the predictor are executor-specific.
Falsifiable Predictions: If the hypothesis holds: (a) the Δ matrix has split-half reliability ≥ 0.5, with a spread of at least 6 test points between best and worst source for a typical target and at least 15% of cells showing negative transfer beyond the noise floor; (b) failure-signature similarity attains Spearman ≈ 0.45–0.65 with Δ (attenuation-corrected), exceeding semantic/task-embedding similarity (predicted ≈ 0.0–0.25) by ≥ 0.2 with a bootstrap CI excluding zero; (c) the leave-one-target-out router recovers ≥ 60% of the oracle-minus-cold-start gain at 50 rollouts and reduces negative-transfer incidents to ≤ 5% versus ≈ 25% for random-source; (d) mechanism: warm-start gain is only partly explained by checkpoint-0 score (partial correlation of failure-signature similarity with Δ remains ≥ 0.3 after controlling for it). Refutation: reliability below ~0.3 (matrix is noise, and we report that as the finding, with the implication that published warm-start results are not reproducible); or semantic similarity matching failure signatures; or best-fixed-source matching the router; or zero-shot score alone explaining Δ entirely, making the failure taxonomy superfluous.
Measurement and Noise Control: Per task, four disjoint splits: reflection-feedback, validation (candidate selection inside the optimizer), failure-signature probe, and a never-touched test set. Every transfer cell is paired with a cold-start run sharing seed, splits, executor, decode settings, and reflector temperature/seed, so Δ is a within-seed difference; where feasible the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness. 56 cells × 3 seeds = 168 paired Δ observations; analysis by bootstrap clustered on target task (the unit of generalization) and a mixed model with source and target random effects plus the similarity predictor as a fixed effect. With per-run test SD ≈ 3 points (measured in step 1) and 3 paired seeds per cell, a single cell detects only ≈ 5-point effects, so all cell-level claims are made only in aggregate; the matrix-level correlation analysis with 56 cells detects a Spearman of ≈ 0.27 at 80% power, and predictor differences are tested by paired bootstrap on cell-wise residuals. Any Δ below the treatment-free null-replicate floor is coded as null regardless of p-value, and all reported gains are test scores of validation-argmax candidates in both arms so the winner's curse is shared; we additionally report the validation-to-test selection gap per arm.
Risk Factors and Limitations: (1) The central risk is a low-reliability matrix; we measure reliability first and, if it is low, the paper becomes a negative result about the reproducibility of warm-start transfer — informative but less attractive. (2) Eight tasks give only 56 cells and 8 clusters for generalization; conclusions are stated at the level of these task clusters. (3) The failure taxonomy is hand-specified and judge-labeled; judge noise and taxonomy misfit are mitigated by inter-judge agreement reporting and a coarsened-taxonomy ablation, but a poor taxonomy could sink the predictor for uninteresting reasons. (4) Zero-shot transfer score is a strong and nearly free competitor predictor; if it wins, the contribution reduces to 'probe cheaply before transferring', which we would report honestly. (5) The 50-rollout cap defines a specific small-budget regime; rankings may differ at larger budgets, so we report checkpoint curves rather than a single number. (6) Domain scrubbing is imperfect; a source-identification leakage test bounds but does not eliminate residual leakage. (7) Frontier-model reflection is rate-limited and nondeterministic; reflection calls are capped (~15 per 50-rollout run, ~3k total) to stay within budget.

Name: instruction_conditioned_complementarity
Title: What Does the Prompt Already Say? Instruction-Conditioned Complementarity Decides When Retrieved Experience Helps, Hurts, or Just Costs Tokens
Short Hypothesis: The marginal value of an injected memory item is relational: it is determined by the item's content relative to what the agent's *instruction* already states, not by the item's similarity to the query nor by its similarity to other retrieved items. Labeling each unit of guidance in a retrieved item against the instruction as REDUNDANT (already asserted), NOVEL (instruction silent) or CONFLICTING (instruction asserts something incompatible) yields a three-way decomposition that predicts per-instance outcomes: fixes track novel units, breaks track conflicting units, redundant units are pure token cost. Consequences we test: (a) the *same* memory bank flips from helpful to inert when the instruction is optimized, because its units become redundant; (b) surgically deleting only the redundant units preserves accuracy at ~half the injected tokens while a token-matched random deletion does not; (c) deleting novel units destroys the fixes; (d) a retrieval rule that scores candidates by instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token beats similarity top-k and item-diversity MMR at matched budget.
Related Work:
The literature has established the *phenomenon* — retrieved experience sometimes helps, sometimes propagates errors, and always costs tokens — without a mechanism that says which will happen for a given item.

(1) Agent-memory harm, empirical. *How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior* (ACL 2026) is the closest empirical work: it shows agents follow retrieved experience by input similarity, and isolates two failure modes, error propagation and "misaligned experience replay", where seemingly correct past executions provide limited or misleading value. It documents helps/hurts/low-value under similarity retrieval; it does not condition value on the instruction's content, and its unit of analysis is the whole retrieved record. *The Trap of Trajectory* (arXiv 2605.09330) plots accuracy against token cost and shows high-cost memory pipelines do not convert budget into accuracy, attributing this to spurious correlations in trajectories. *Learning How to Remember* (arXiv 2601.07470) argues retrieval-based memory "overfits to surface-level similarity" and can be negative under task shift, and proposes meta-cognitive management rather than a content-level account. All three treat an item's value as a property of the item (or of the trajectory that produced it). Ours is a property of the *pair* (item, instruction): the identical item is redundant under one instruction and novel under another.

(2) Relevance is the wrong axis. *Sufficient Context* (ICLR 2025) makes the nearest conceptual move — relevance to the query is not what we want to measure; whether the context adds what is missing is. But "what is missing" there is defined relative to the question and the model's parametric knowledge in factual QA. We define it relative to the *task instruction*, which is (i) the only text guaranteed present on every episode, and (ii) the text a prompt optimizer is actively rewriting, which makes complementarity a moving target and couples memory to prompt optimization.

(3) Atomic decomposition. *AtomMem* (arXiv 2606.19847) decomposes conversations into atomic facts for storage and deduplication; A-Mem/AtomRAG-style work decomposes queries or the memory store. The machinery exists; nobody points it at instruction-vs-item pairs to score marginal value.

(4) Diversity retrieval and dedup. MMR/DPP selection penalizes similarity *among selected items*; skill-library dedup work (item-against-item, library-against-library) does the same at a different granularity. This is the exact structural analogue of our rule with the wrong reference set, and it is our decisive baseline.

(5) Token cost independent of relevance. *Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval* (EMNLP 2025 Findings) shows degradation with input length even under perfect retrieval, which motivates why redundant units are not free — but says nothing about which content is redundant.

Our contribution is the relational reframing plus the instrument that makes it falsifiable: a unit-level three-way taxonomy anchored on the instruction, a token-matched surgical ablation with a decoy-instruction placebo, and a selection rule conditioned on the current prompt state.
Abstract: Agentic memory retrieves past experience by similarity to the query and injects it alongside a task instruction that a prompt optimizer is separately rewriting. Both texts carry guidance; nothing in either pipeline checks whether they carry the *same* guidance. We propose that an item's marginal value is relational — it depends on what the instruction already says — and that this single variable explains the fix/break/token-cost structure of memory injection that recent empirical work documents but does not predict. We decompose the instruction and each retrieved item into atomic guidance units and label every item unit against the instruction as redundant, novel, or conflicting, using an off-the-shelf NLI model as the primary instrument (LLM and human labels used for validation only). We test three things on one environment with one primary model. First, relationality: holding the bank, retriever and retrievals fixed, we run under a short hand-written instruction and under an optimizer-produced long instruction, and predict that the same items flip from mostly novel to substantially redundant and that memory's paired gain collapses accordingly. Second, causality: unit-level surgery at matched token budget — delete only the redundant units, delete a token-matched random subset, delete the novel units, or delete a subset chosen against a *decoy* instruction — so the taxonomy can be falsified without touching the retriever. Third, exploitation: a complementarity retrieval rule scoring candidates by instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token, against similarity top-k, MMR item-diversity, and a cheap embedding-overlap proxy at matched injected-token budgets. All comparisons are instance-paired with McNemar tests, null replicates, and a stated 5-point minimum detectable effect at n=500. The whole program is ~27k agent episodes on one 4×A100 node and under $100 of API.
Experiments:
COMPUTE ENVELOPE (stated up front so it can be checked). One node, 4×A100 80GB, vLLM. Primary agent Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct served tensor-parallel-2 × 2 replicas; measured pilot throughput on this scaffold is ~1,000 completed episodes/hour at high concurrency (an episode is ~6 model calls, ~2.5k prompt tokens each). Total planned episodes: 27,300 → ~28 hours of node time, ~2–3 days wall clock with restarts and analysis. Frontier API is used only for (a) atomic decomposition of ~400 bank items + 2 instructions, (b) the reflective optimizer's reflection calls (~150), (c) validation labeling of 400 unit pairs: total well under $100. Task correctness is exact-match/F1 on public gold answers — no LLM judge, no judging cost.

HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: ReAct scaffold, tool stack (BM25+dense search over the corpus), step limit, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once with an ExpeL-style write path over the training split, then frozen for the entire study), decoding temperature and seed schedule, held-out test split. Only the instruction, the set of memory *units* placed in context, and the selection rule vary.

ENVIRONMENT. E1 only: tool-augmented multi-hop QA, a 50/50 mix of HotpotQA-distractor and MuSiQue dev questions (500 held-out instances, 300 train instances for bank construction and optimization, 150 dev instances for instrument fixing and the precheck). This environment carries every quantitative claim in the paper. (ALFWorld and WebShop are cut from the core program; see the contingent extension at the end.)

MODELS. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is the primary agent and carries all claims. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct runs the decisive arms only, as a cross-model directional check.

THE INSTRUMENT. Both the instruction and each memory item are split into atomic guidance units — single imperative or descriptive statements about how to act ("search the entity page before the relation page"; "if the first search returns a disambiguation page, refine with the year"). Decomposition is done once, offline, by the frontier model, with the prompt fixed on the 150-instance dev split before any test evaluation and published verbatim. Labeling of each item unit against the full set of instruction units is done by an off-the-shelf NLI model (DeBERTa-v3-large-MNLI): entailment of the item unit by some instruction unit → REDUNDANT; contradiction → CONFLICTING; else NOVEL. Thresholds fixed on dev. NLI is the *primary* instrument because it is free, deterministic, and reruns at zero marginal cost. Validation: 400 unit–instruction pairs double-annotated by two humans, plus a frontier-LLM labeling of the same 400; we report inter-human, NLI–human, and LLM–human Cohen's kappa, and require NLI–human kappa > 0.6 before the taxonomy is used as an explanatory variable. Every taxonomy-dependent analysis is re-run with the LLM labels on the subset where they exist.

THE TWO INSTRUCTIONS (the manipulation that makes value relational). I_short: a minimal hand-written ReAct scaffold. I_long: produced by a GEPA-style reflective optimizer run on the 300 training instances *without memory in context* (2,400 episodes, ~150 reflection calls). By construction I_long absorbs guidance that the bank also contains, so the same retrieved items should be mostly novel under I_short and substantially redundant under I_long. This is a two-point version of the co-adaptation dynamics question — round 0 versus round N of an optimizer that never saw the memory — obtained for the cost of one optimizer run instead of a 3-seed × 3-round sweep.

PRECHECK (gates the study, 150 dev instances, ~900 episodes). Proceed only if (i) the bank moves ≥6% of dev instances in either direction versus no-memory under at least one instruction, and (ii) the taxonomy is non-degenerate: each of the three labels covers ≥10% of injected units under at least one instruction condition. If either fails we report the precheck and stop, rather than proceeding quietly.

PART 1 — PREDICTIVE (uses the Part 2 arms; no extra episodes). For each of 500 held-out instances × 2 instruction conditions, record the fix/break outcome of S1 (full top-k=7 memory) against S0 (no memory). Fit mixed-effects logistic models of fix and of break on counts of novel, redundant and conflicting units, with these competing regressors in the same model: total injected tokens, mean retrieval score, instance difficulty (no-memory accuracy across seeds), and a **cheap embedding-overlap proxy** (max cosine between item embedding and instruction embedding, plus token-level Jaccard). The claim requires that novel-unit count predicts fixes and conflicting-unit count predicts breaks with 95% intervals excluding zero *after* those competitors are in the model, and that redundant-unit count has no positive fix coefficient. If the cheap proxy absorbs the unit counts, we say so — and note explicitly that this would *confirm* the reference-set claim (instruction, not query, not other items) while refuting only the need for the expensive decomposition machinery.

PART 2 — UNIT-LEVEL SURGERY (the causal test). Retrieved item set held fixed at top-k=7; only what is injected changes. Six arms, each fully paired on the same 500 instances, run under both instructions, 2 decoding seeds:
- S0 no memory
- S1 full top-k=7, unedited
- S2 drop-redundant: delete exactly the units labeled REDUNDANT
- S3 drop-random: delete a random unit subset token-matched to S2 within 5% *per instance*
- S4 drop-novel: delete NOVEL units, token-matched to S2 — the anti-ablation that must hurt
- S7 decoy placebo: delete a subset chosen by applying the taxonomy against a *decoy instruction* of matched length and register but different content, token-matched to S2
Cost: 6 × 2 × 500 × 2 = 12,000 episodes. S5 (drop-conflicting) and S6 (keep-novel-only) are cut; the conflicting channel is instead read off the Part 1 break regression and off S2-vs-S1 break counts, which is weaker but free.
S3 and S7 are the load-bearing controls: S3 removes the taxonomy's information while holding the token budget, S7 removes the *identity* of the conditioning instruction while holding the deletion machinery, the token count and the LLM/NLI-in-the-loop. All deletions use the identical delete-and-restitch procedure; we report a fluency check on the edited item text.

PART 3 — THE METHOD. Complementarity retrieval: from the retriever's top-m=20 candidates, greedily select items maximizing instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per injected token, given the current instruction and the units already selected, until a token budget is spent. Compared at *matched injected-token budget* against three selection rules: similarity top-k, MMR item-diversity selection, and the cheap embedding-overlap-with-instruction proxy (select items minimizing instruction overlap per token). Two budgets (token cost of k≈2 and k≈4), under I_long only — the regime where redundancy exists and the method can matter. Cost: 4 rules × 2 budgets × 500 × 2 seeds = 8,000 episodes. S1 (k=7) from Part 2 is the unmatched-budget reference. All (item, instruction) labels are precomputed and cached offline, so inference-time overhead is a table lookup; the offline labeling cost is reported in full, not hidden in setup.

NULL REPLICATES. 1,000 extra episodes: two arms re-run under a different decoding seed with no treatment change, to measure the apparent-delta distribution directly.

CROSS-MODEL CHECK. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, I_long only, arms S1/S2/S3/S7 plus complementarity vs top-k at the k≈2 budget: 6 arms × 500 × 1 seed = 3,000 episodes (~2h on the smaller model). Directional only; n=500 single-seed MDE ≈ 6 points.

EPISODE ARITHMETIC. Optimizer run 2,400 + precheck 900 + Part 2 (which supplies Part 1) 12,000 + Part 3 8,000 + null replicates 1,000 + cross-model 3,000 = 27,300 episodes ≈ 28 node-hours. Fits the envelope with roughly 2× headroom for reruns.

CONTINGENT EXTENSION (not counted in the budget, not a claim in the paper unless run). If Part 2 yields a decisive S2-vs-S3 result, we run a 150-instance, 4-arm (S0/S1/S2/S3) ALFWorld replication as a directional generality check where guidance units are procedural rather than search heuristics. It is reported as such, with its ~9-point MDE stated, or omitted.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) **MMR/DPP item-diversity selection at matched token budget.** If deduplicating items against each other captures the same savings as deduplicating against the instruction, the instruction-conditioning claim is unnecessary. This is the most likely way the method claim dies and it is run at both budgets.
(ii) **Cheap embedding/lexical instruction-overlap proxy** (added in response to review), both as a competing regressor in Part 1 and as a selection rule in Part 3. This is the strongest test of whether the atomic decomposition machinery earns its cost. Note the asymmetry we will report honestly: if the proxy wins, the *reference set* claim (instruction, not query, not other items) stands and the *instrument* claim falls — the paper then recommends a two-line change to any retriever.
(iii) **S3 drop-random at per-instance matched tokens.** If deleting an arbitrary equal-token subset works as well as deleting exactly the redundant units, the taxonomy carries no information and the whole effect is injection volume. Prior pilot work in this track makes this a live possibility, which is why S3 is matched per instance rather than on average.
(iv) **I_long with no memory at all (S0 under I_long).** Wins if the optimized instruction already contains everything worth having — which is itself our prediction (2) and would be reported as confirming relationality while nullifying the method.
(v) **Full top-k=7 unedited (S1).** The standard deployment; the equivalence target for S2 at ~half the tokens.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.
- **S7 decoy-instruction placebo** — the single most important control. Holds deletion machinery, deleted token count and labeler-in-the-loop fixed; removes only the identity of the conditioning instruction. Any S2−S7 gap is attributable to conditioning on the *real* instruction.
- **S4 drop-novel**, the anti-ablation: a taxonomy under which deleting novel units is harmless is not measuring guidance content, and no downstream result rescues it. We refused to cut this despite scope pressure because it is what makes prediction (1) falsifiable rather than merely correlational.
- **The two-instruction manipulation (I_short vs I_long)** establishes relationality: the same items must switch label distribution *and* switch measured value. Also refused as a cut — without it the proposal degenerates into a dedup engineering paper.
- **NLI labeler as primary with LLM and human validation** checks that results are not artifacts of one judge.
- All arms reported on matched injected-token, matched agent-call, and wall-clock axes.

CUT FROM THE PREVIOUS VERSION, with reasons: S5/S6 (conflicting/novel-only isolation) — mechanism read off regression instead; cross-encoder reranker and LLM-compressor baselines — neither could distinguish the instruction-reference-set claim from item-level curation, which MMR already tests more cleanly; Qwen3-32B, WebShop, and the 3-seed × 3-round optimizer dynamics sweep — the dynamics question is retained in its two-point I_short/I_long form.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Stated against the actual power of the design: n=500 paired instances, expected 12–18% discordant pairs, McNemar MDE ≈ **5 points** for a single-instruction-condition contrast and ≈ **3.5 points** pooled across the two instruction conditions (1,000 clustered paired observations). Effects smaller than these are reported as inconclusive, not as nulls and not as wins.

1. **Relationality (the core claim).** The identical retrieved items shift from ≤15% REDUNDANT units under I_short to ≥40% REDUNDANT under I_long, and memory's paired gain (S1−S0) falls by ≥5 points from I_short to I_long. If the label distribution shifts but the gain does not, the taxonomy is semantically valid but behaviourally inert and the paper says so.
2. **Prediction.** Novel-unit count predicts fixes and conflicting-unit count predicts breaks with 95% intervals excluding zero and standardized log-odds |β| ≥ 0.25, *after* injected tokens, retrieval score, instance difficulty and the cheap embedding-overlap proxy are in the model. Redundant-unit count has a fix coefficient indistinguishable from zero. Removing the three unit counts drops explained deviance by ≥25% relative.
3. **Surgery.** S2 (drop-redundant) is equivalent to S1 within a 4-point margin *pooled across instruction conditions* while cutting injected tokens by ≥40%; S3 (drop-random, token-matched) loses ≥5 points relative to S2 under I_long; S4 (drop-novel, token-matched) loses ≥5 points of fixes relative to S2.
4. **Placebo.** S7 (decoy instruction) recovers less than half of the S2−S3 gap.
5. **Method.** Complementarity retrieval beats similarity top-k by ≥5 points at the k≈2-equivalent budget, and beats MMR by ≥4 points pooled across the two budgets and two seeds. A 2-point MMR gap is reported as inconclusive, not as a win.

REFUTATION CONDITIONS.
- If S2, S3 and S7 are mutually indistinguishable within the noise floor, the taxonomy is inert and the entire effect is injection volume — a clean negative supporting the budget account, which we report as the primary result of the paper.
- If MMR matches complementarity retrieval at both budgets, item-item diversity suffices and instruction conditioning is unnecessary.
- If the cheap embedding proxy matches the unit taxonomy in both Part 1 and Part 3, the mechanism claim (instruction as reference set) survives and the instrument claim dies; we report the proxy as the recommended method.
- If S4 (drop-novel) is harmless, the novel/redundant distinction has no behavioural content and no downstream result can rescue prediction 2.
- If NLI–human kappa on unit labels falls below 0.6, we report the study as instrument-limited rather than reinterpreting the results.
Measurement and Noise Control:
(a) EVALUATION VARIANCE. Every held-out instance is run under every arm with the same seed schedule, so all arm comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar tests on paired fix/break tables, Holm-corrected across the arm family within each instruction condition. Every reported delta carries its full fix/break decomposition: a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention, and prior work in this track has confused the two.

(b) NULL REPLICATES. 1,000 dedicated episodes re-running identical arms under a different decoding seed, reporting the distribution of apparent deltas. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. This is load-bearing given prior observations in this track of 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.

(c) MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECT, computed rather than asserted. With N=500 paired instances and 15% discordance (D≈75), detecting a net swing requires |b−c| ≈ 2.8·√D ≈ 24 discordant-pair imbalance at 80% power, α=0.05 two-sided → **δ ≈ 4.8 points**. Pooled across the two instruction conditions with instance-clustered bootstrap, δ ≈ 3.5 points. All predictions above are set at or above these thresholds; the S2-vs-S1 equivalence claim uses a 4-point margin on the pooled comparison and anything inside it is reported as inconclusive, never as equivalence. Cross-model (Llama-8B, single seed) MDE ≈ 6 points, directional only.

(d) REGRESSION POWER. 1,000 instance-observations (500 × 2 conditions) with instance random effects detects a standardized log-odds coefficient of ≈0.22 at 80% power; we do not interpret smaller coefficients. VIF among the three unit-count regressors and the embedding proxy is reported; if any VIF > 5 we report the orthogonalized decomposition instead.

(e) INSTRUMENT RELIABILITY. Inter-human, NLI–human and LLM–human Cohen's kappa on 400 double-annotated unit–instruction pairs. Decomposition granularity fixed on dev before any test run, published verbatim, and all Part 2 results repeated at a second coarser granularity as a sensitivity check (analysis-only re-labeling; the coarser granularity changes which units are deleted, so this costs a re-run of S2/S3 only: +2,000 episodes, within the stated headroom).
Preprint Collision Check:
Grounded in the literature search run for this revision. The search returned seven relevant items; I treat these as the authoritative set and flag that the skill-library dedup cluster cited in my earlier draft (SkillZip / SkillRAE / SkillOps) was *not* re-confirmed by this search, so I do not lean on those citations here.

**Closest and most threatening: *How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior*, ACL 2026.** It demonstrates, at the agent-memory level, exactly the phenomenon we set out to explain — similarity-retrieved experience produces experience-following, error propagation (hurts) and "misaligned experience replay" where correct past executions carry limited or misleading value. Verdict: **does not collide, but it removes our right to claim the phenomenon.** It measures value as a function of input–input similarity between the query and the retrieved record; our unit of analysis is the pair (item unit, instruction unit) and our claim is that value is relational to the *instruction*, which that paper never varies. We will cite it as establishing the target phenomenon and position our contribution strictly as the mechanism and the intervention. If our Part 2 surgery is null, this paper is what we are unable to add to.

***Sufficient Context* (ICLR 2025)** is the nearest conceptual predecessor: relevance to the query is the wrong axis; what matters is whether the context supplies what is missing. Verdict: **does not collide.** "Missing" there is relative to the question and parametric knowledge in single-turn factual QA. Ours is relative to a task instruction that a prompt optimizer is rewriting, which is what makes complementarity time-varying and couples memory to prompt optimization. We adopt their framing as an intellectual ancestor and say so.

***AtomMem* (arXiv 2606.19847)** supplies atomic-fact decomposition for memory storage and dedup. Verdict: **does not collide** — same machinery, different reference set (memory store vs. memory store; never instruction vs. item), and no marginal-value or fix/break analysis. It does weaken any claim of novelty for "atomic decomposition", which we do not make.

***The Trap of Trajectory* (arXiv 2605.09330)** shows memory pipelines fail to convert token budget into accuracy. Verdict: **does not collide**; it is the strongest external support for our "just costs tokens" branch and we cite it as such rather than re-deriving it.

***Learning How to Remember* (arXiv 2601.07470)** critiques surface-similarity retrieval as producing negative transfer. Verdict: **does not collide** — same diagnosis, different remedy (meta-cognitive management, not instruction-conditioned content scoring). It is a competing account and we will note that our Part 3 method is a cheaper, testable alternative.

***Mitigating Errors in LLM-Generated Web API Invocations* (arXiv 2607.05936)** is a domain-specific instance of retrieved context conflicting with what the task already specifies (models over-include retrieved parameters). Verdict: **does not collide**, and it is arguably a single-domain confirmation of our CONFLICTING channel.

***Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance* (EMNLP 2025 Findings)** establishes that added context costs accuracy independent of relevance. Verdict: **does not collide**; it is why deleting redundant units should be a free win rather than a wash.

**What the search did not find, stated plainly.** No located work decomposes both the agent instruction and each retrieved memory item into guidance units and scores marginal value by instruction-relative redundancy/novelty/conflict. The three-way outcome taxonomy exists piecemeal across separate papers but is not unified under an instruction-conditioned mechanism. **Honest caveat:** I could not sweep unindexed OpenReview 2026 submissions, and given how crowded the agent-memory-harm niche is right now, I assign a nontrivial chance that instruction-aware dedup appears as an appendix ablation in a contemporaneous context-compilation preprint. The contribution would remain distinct in three respects that no located work has: the two-instruction relationality manipulation, the per-instance token-matched surgical ablation, and the decoy-instruction placebo.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Single environment.** All quantitative claims rest on tool-augmented multi-hop QA with one primary model. This is a deliberate consequence of the resource envelope: we chose n=500 paired instances in one environment (MDE ≈ 5 points) over n=150 in three environments (MDE ≈ 9 points each), because the second design cannot detect the effects we predict. Generality is a stated limitation, not a claim; the ALFWorld replication is contingent and labeled directional.
2. **Degenerate taxonomy.** If nearly all units are novel under I_short and nearly all redundant under I_long, the three-way decomposition adds nothing beyond the aggregate substitution effect. The precheck detects this and we report it rather than proceeding.
3. **The decomposition is a design surface that could manufacture the result.** Granularity changes unit counts and therefore token accounting. Mitigations: prompt fixed on dev before any test run, published verbatim, and S2/S3 re-run at a coarser granularity.
4. **Behavioural irrelevance of semantic redundancy.** A model may need a rule restated in concrete episodic form to actually follow it. If so, S2 loses fixes and S4 is harmless — a real finding that would overturn the recommendation to delete redundant units, and one we would report as the paper's result.
5. **Coherence confound in deletion.** Removing scattered units can produce disfluent item text. S3, S4 and S7 use the identical delete-and-restitch procedure as S2, and we report a fluency check; this controls the confound but does not eliminate it.
6. **The cheap proxy may win.** If embedding overlap with the instruction matches the unit taxonomy, the expensive instrument is unnecessary. We regard this as a partial win for the central claim (right reference set) and a loss for the instrument, and will report it that way rather than burying it.
7. **Dynamics are only two points.** Replacing the 3-seed × 3-round optimizer sweep with the I_short/I_long contrast means we observe co-adaptation at round 0 and round N but not its trajectory; we cannot claim monotonicity or a rate. We say this rather than implying a dynamics result we did not measure.
8. **Cacheability scopes the method.** Complementarity retrieval requires (item, instruction) labels; these are cached offline, so the practical claim is scoped to settings where the instruction is stable between optimizer rounds. Offline labeling cost is reported explicitly.
9. **Model specificity.** A model that ignores long instructions will show little redundancy effect regardless of the text. Per-model results are reported separately; no pooled headline across Qwen-14B and Llama-8B.
10. **A fully null Part 2** leaves a qualifying negative about instruction-aware curation, whose worth depends entirely on the placebo, the null replicates and the stated MDE — which is why those are load-bearing rather than decorative.

Name: memory_budget_confound
Title: One Item Is the Budget: Token Volume, Not Memory Content, Explains Both the Harm and the Apparent Gains of Agentic Memory Curation
Short Hypothesis: In experience-memory agents, the value of injected retrieved experience saturates after roughly one item, while its cost grows with injected tokens regardless of relevance. Two consequences follow, both falsifiable: (i) length-matched decoy experience — same environment, wrong task — reproduces most of the harm of correctly retrieved experience at the same injection volume; (ii) published curation methods (reconstruction, self-organizing memory) lose most or all of their advantage over raw top-k retrieval once the raw baseline is given the same per-instance injected-token budget the curated output happens to consume. The practical corollary is that k=1 raw retrieval, tuned once, is competitive with curation at a fraction of the cost.
Related Work:
Three clusters.

(1) **Curation-as-the-fix agent memory.** A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.12110) argues existing memory "lack[s] sophisticated memory organization" and proposes note-based self-organizing memory. MemHarness (arXiv 2607.28272, 2026) argues verbatim "replay" of retrieved experience causes negative transfer because of the abstraction gap between stored experience and the current state, and proposes situation-conditioned reconstruction. MRAgent (arXiv:2606.06036, 2026) proposes a Cue–Tag–Content graph with active reconstruction. RecMem (arXiv:2605.16045) consolidates memory recurrently. Every one of these attributes harm to *what* is in memory and proposes a content-side fix; in each case the fix also shortens or restructures the injected text, and none of the retrieved papers reports a comparison in which the uncurated baseline is matched to the curated system on injected tokens.

(2) **Length-vs-content disentangling, outside agent memory.** Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297, 2026) shows that naive and distractor-aware truncation give "sometimes opposite" answers to "does less context help?" and quantifies signal loss vs. distractor reduction, but for static long-context QA benchmarks. Context Rot (Chroma) documents degradation with raw input length independent of relevance. AtomicRAG (arXiv:2604.20844) reports a fixed-context-budget robustness analysis in general RAG. These establish the methodological move and the premise; none of them is about experience memory, procedural (non-answer-bearing) injected content, or the evaluation of curation methods.

(3) **RAG distractor work.** Lost in the Middle; "LLMs Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context"; The Power of Noise. These show irrelevant *documents* hurt. Our setting differs in two ways that make the claim non-obvious: the harmful items are topically correct, procedurally on-task experience selected by a retriever working as designed; and the injected content is not answer-bearing, so unlike long-context QA there is no "signal loss" term to trade off — which is exactly why we predict saturation at one item rather than a monotone accuracy/length tradeoff.

Positioning: this is not a new memory method. It is a causal decomposition (content value vs. token load) plus one specific missing control applied to published curation methods. The contribution is the re-examination table it produces.
Abstract: Agentic memory systems retrieve distilled past experience and inject it into an LLM agent's context. A 2026 wave of papers documents that this often hurts, attributes the harm to memory content — staleness, conflict, the abstraction gap between stored experience and the current state — and proposes a content-side remedy: reconstruction, reorganization, pruning. Each remedy also changes how many tokens get injected, and none of the papers we could find matches its raw-retrieval baseline on that budget. We ask whether the harm, and the reported cure, are about content at all. A pilot observation motivates the doubt: for a fixed memory bank, cutting injection from seven retrieved items to three eliminated a significant harm (McNemar p<0.05, replicated) without changing a single item. We propose a decomposition that separates the *content* value of retrieved experience from the *load* cost of the tokens carrying it. Holding bank, retriever, scaffold, tools and decoding fixed, we vary relevance (correct retrieval vs. length-matched decoys drawn from the same environment but the wrong task, and from an unrelated environment), item count, and total injected tokens (equalized by padding and truncation), with a gold-trajectory oracle bounding content value from above and a cross-encoder reranker instantiating the content-selection alternative. We then apply the missing control to two reimplemented curation methods: give raw top-k the same per-instance injected-token budget the curated output consumes, and add a compression-only rewrite that strips situational grounding from reconstruction. The sharp prediction is that content value saturates after about one item while load cost is roughly linear in tokens and largely relevance-independent, so that tuned k=1 raw retrieval lands within 2 points of the best curation method. Analysis is fully paired, with null replicates that fix the noise floor and a pre-registered minimum detectable effect.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED ACROSS ALL CONDITIONS:** ReAct scaffold, dense retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from the training split with an ExpeL-style write path producing raw trajectories plus distilled insights, then frozen), decoding temperature and seed schedule, tool stack, step limit. Only memory *injection* differs. Every test instance is run under every condition (fully paired).

**PRIMARY ENVIRONMENT (carries all quantitative claims):** E1, tool-augmented multi-hop QA over HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue, agent issues search calls, ~5–8 LLM calls per episode. n=600 test instances.

**PRIMARY MODEL:** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. A frontier API model is used only for offline write-path distillation and for the reconstruction/compression conditions, identically across conditions.

**CONDITION GRID (E1, 16 conditions):**

*Decomposition block (identification):*
- C0 No memory.
- C1(1), C1(3), C1(7) Top-k correctly retrieved experience — the standard deployment; C1(3) also makes BudgetFirst realizable.
- C2(7) Same-environment decoys: 7 items retrieved for a randomly drawn *different* query from a disjoint task family, token-matched to C1(7) within 5%.
- C2u(7) Unrelated-environment decoys: 7 items from a structurally different agent environment's bank, token-matched. Rules out generic scaffolding transfer contaminating the "irrelevant" arm.
- C3(7) Dilution: 1 correct item + 6 same-environment decoys, token-matched to C1(7).
- C4 Padded-single: top-1 relevant item padded with neutral task-generic boilerplate to C1(7)'s token count.
- C5 Truncated-seven: 7 top-k items each truncated so the total equals C1(1)'s token count. Mirror of C4; C4/C5 separate item multiplicity from token count.
- C6 Oracle: gold trajectory of the nearest training task. Upper-bounds achievable content value so a null on content cannot be dismissed as "the bank was worthless".
- C10 Reranker-7: cross-encoder reranking of a 30-item candidate pool down to 7, token-matched to C1(7). This is the content-selection alternative given a labeled condition; if content selection is the lever, C10 beats C1(7) and the load account weakens.

*Curation re-examination block (the contribution):*
- C7a MemHarness-style situation-conditioned reconstruction of retrieved items at its natural output length.
- C8a Raw top-k selected/truncated to match, **per instance**, C7a's injected-token count within 5%.
- C7b A-MEM-style linked/organized memory retrieval at its natural output length.
- C8b Per-instance token-matched raw retrieval for C7b.
- C9 Compression-only rewrite: raw retrieved items passed through the *same* reconstruction model with an instruction to compress but not to condition on current state. Separates "reconstruction as situational grounding" from "reconstruction as compression".

**BudgetFirst** (the practical payload) is not an extra run: it is C1(k*) with k* chosen once per model on a 100-instance dev split disjoint from the test set.

**SEEDS AND ARITHMETIC.** Eight conditions carry the decisive comparisons (C0, C1(7), C2(7), C4, C5, C7a, C8a, C9) and are run with 2 decoding seeds; the seed pair doubles as the null replicate that measures the noise floor. The remaining eight are run with 1 seed. E1 primary = 8×600×2 + 8×600×1 = **14,400 episodes** ≈ 94k LLM calls at ~3k prompt / ~150 output tokens ≈ 300M prefill + 14M decode tokens. On 4×A100 with vLLM tensor-parallel and continuous batching this is ~1.5–2 node-days including tool latency and retries.

**REPLICATION TIER (committed, reduced):**
- E1 with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on the 8 decisive conditions, 1 seed: 8×600 = **3,600 episodes**, <0.5 node-day. Guards against the result being an artifact of one model's context handling.
- E2 ALFWorld, 6 conditions (C0, C1(7), C2(7), C4, C7a, C8a), n=200, 1 seed, Qwen2.5-14B: **1,200 episodes** × ~30 steps ≈ 36k calls with longer prompts ≈ 1 node-day. Directional replication in a long-horizon setting only; explicitly under-powered for point estimates.

**TOTAL: 19,200 episodes, ~130k LLM calls, ~3 node-days.** Frontier API: ~2,000 distillation calls (one-off) + ~1,400 reconstruction calls (C7a) + ~1,400 compression calls (C9) + 200 for E2 ≈ 5,000 calls, well under $200.

**DROPPED FROM THE PREVIOUS DESIGN AND WHY:** WebShop (E3) — a third environment adds no identification power and cost a full node-day. Qwen3-32B — 8B vs 14B already spans the model-size question at a third the cost. The third curation method (conflict pruning) — the two retained methods bracket the length axis (reconstruction shortens; A-MEM organization need not), which is what the confound claim needs. A long-context ablation — the context window is not binding at 7 items, so it does not test the mechanism.

**ANALYSIS.**
(a) Paired fix/break tables for every condition against C0 and against C1(7), with exact McNemar tests and Holm correction within the condition family.
(b) Mixed-effects logistic regression of success on three regressors — relevant-content tokens, decoy/filler tokens, number of injected items — with instance random intercept. Central quantitative claim: the coefficients on relevant and decoy tokens are both significantly negative and statistically indistinguishable from each other, while the marginal effect of *relevant content* is concentrated in the first item.
(c) Budget curve: success vs. injected tokens for the relevant (C1(1),C1(3),C1(7)) and decoy (C2 series) arms. The load hypothesis predicts approximately parallel curves offset by a small constant equal to the content value.
(d) **Re-examination table:** for each of the two curation methods, its headline delta over C1(7) at natural length, and its delta over C8 at matched budget, with the noise floor printed alongside and an explicit verdict column (survives / halved / ties).

**PRE-REGISTERED FIDELITY GATE.** A curation baseline enters the re-examination table only if, at natural length on the dev split, it reproduces a positive delta over C1(7) in the direction and rough magnitude reported in its source. If it does not, we report it as unreproduced and exclude it from the table rather than claiming a budget confound for a baseline we failed to build.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.** (i) C7a reconstruction under the C8a per-instance token-matched comparison — if it still beats budget-matched raw retrieval by more than the measured noise floor, the content-side account is vindicated and we say so. (ii) C7b organized memory at matched budget. (iii) C10 cross-encoder reranker at fixed k=7 — wins if content *selection*, not volume, is the lever; this is a labeled condition in the grid, not a narrative aside. (iv) C6 oracle gold trajectory — if the oracle is also flat, our decomposition is fine but the bank was worthless, and we report that instead.

**ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.** C2(7) removes relevance while holding tokens; C3(7) keeps relevance while inflating tokens — together these are the core identification. C2u(7) checks that same-environment decoys are not smuggling in generic scaffolding transfer. C4/C5 separate item multiplicity from token count. C9 separates compression from situational grounding inside reconstruction. Position ablation on the 8 decisive E1 conditions (memory at the prompt head vs. immediately before the action step, free — reuses the same episodes with one extra rendering) checks for primacy/recency artifacts. Shuffled-bank sanity control confirms the retriever is functioning.

**CONSTRUCTIVE BASELINE.** BudgetFirst: raw top-k with k tuned once on a 100-instance dev split, no curation, no API calls. If BudgetFirst matches the curation methods, that is the practical payload of the paper.

**MANIPULATION CHECK.** Rate at which agent reasoning traces cite or paraphrase injected decoy vs. relevant content, so that "decoys are trivially ignorable" is measured rather than assumed.
Falsifiable Predictions:
1. **Decoys reproduce the harm.** C2(7) recovers ≥60% of the accuracy drop of C1(7) relative to C1(1). (Refuted if C2(7) is within noise of C1(1) while C1(7) harms — that would mean harm requires topically-relevant-but-mismatched content and the content-side literature is right.)
2. **Parallel curves, small offset.** The success-vs-injected-tokens curves for relevant and decoy arms are approximately parallel; the vertical offset (total content value across seven items) is <3 points on E1, i.e. smaller than the load cost of going from 1 to 7 items.
3. **Saturation at one item.** In the mixed-effects fit, C1(3) and C1(7) do not exceed C1(1) in content value beyond noise; the practical optimum k on E1 is 1 (or 2), not 5–10 as deployed.
4. **Curation gains are budget artifacts.** Each of the two curation methods' advantage over raw retrieval shrinks by ≥half under per-instance token matching (C8), and at least one ties its budget-matched baseline within the noise floor. Additionally, C9 (compression without situational grounding) captures ≥half of C7a's gain over C1(7).
5. **BudgetFirst is competitive.** Tuned-k raw retrieval lands within 2 points of the best curation method on E1 at zero API cost.

**REFUTATION.** If C2(7)/C2u(7) are harmless while C1(7) harms, the load account is dead. If both curation methods retain their full advantage under C8 and C9 captures little of C7a's gain, the confound claim fails and we report that published curation gains are genuine. If C10 (reranker) beats C1(7) by more than the noise floor, content selection is a first-order lever and the "volume is the design variable" framing is wrong. All three are publishable and all three are different papers; we commit in advance to reporting whichever occurs, with the pre-registered grid unchanged.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Fully paired: every test instance is evaluated under every condition on the same seed schedule, so all comparisons are within-instance. Primary test is the exact McNemar test on fix/break counts per condition pair with Holm correction across the condition family; secondary is the mixed-effects logistic regression described above, with 95% CIs from instance-level bootstrap (10k resamples).

**Noise floor.** For each of the eight decisive conditions we hold a null replicate — the identical condition re-run under a different decoding seed — and report the distribution of apparent deltas. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. Pilot work in this setting saw re-scoring drift of 5–14 points on small held-out sets, so this is load-bearing, not decorative.

**Minimum detectable effect.** At n=600 paired instances on E1 with an expected discordant-pair rate of 12–18% (72–108 discordant pairs), McNemar detects a net swing of ~4 percentage points at 80% power, α=0.05. At n=200 on ALFWorld the MDE is ~7–8 points. We pre-register that E1 carries every quantitative claim, that the 8B run and E2 are directional replication only, and that sub-MDE differences will not be interpreted as evidence in either direction. Note that predictions 1, 4 and 5 are ratio/equivalence claims: for the "ties within noise floor" component of prediction 4 we report a TOST equivalence test at a ±4-point margin rather than treating a non-significant McNemar as a null.

Every reported delta ships with its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding large symmetric churn is a different finding from a genuinely inert intervention.
Preprint Collision Check:
The search this round returned ten relevant items across six queries (the tool hit its call limit again, so coverage is six queries, not exhaustive — I report what was actually returned).

**Closest methodological threat: Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297, 2026).** It builds precisely the move this proposal depends on — disentangling context-length effects from content/signal loss, with paired comparisons, and quantifying "what fraction of degradation is signal loss versus pure distractor reduction." It **collides on method but not on target**: it operates on static long-context QA benchmarks where the removed content is answer-bearing evidence, so its central tension is a length/signal tradeoff. Our setting has no answer-bearing term — injected experience is procedural — which is why we can make the stronger and more surprising prediction (content value saturates at one item; the optimum k is 1). It does not evaluate any agent-memory curation method. Honest assessment: if that group extends the method to agent memory injection, the decomposition half of this paper is scooped and only the re-examination table survives. That table is why we kept two curation methods rather than one.

**Closest target works being challenged.** A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.12110) — the canonical "sophisticated organization improves memory" paper, instantiated here as C7b. MemHarness (arXiv 2607.28272, 2026) — argues negative transfer comes from the abstraction gap and that reconstruction fixes it; instantiated as C7a; reconstruction changes content and length simultaneously, which is exactly what C8a/C9 separate. MRAgent (arXiv:2606.06036, 2026) — a second, independent "reconstruction not retrieval" graph-memory paper; we do not reimplement it but it is cited as evidence the confound is spreading across the subfield, and its non-inclusion is a scope decision we state. RecMem (arXiv:2605.16045) and the memory survey (arXiv:2605.06716) confirm pruning/organization/reconstruction are the current SOTA curation mechanisms.

**Partial precedents for budget matching.** AtomicRAG (arXiv:2604.20844) runs a "robustness under fixed context budgets" analysis where all methods are truncated to a common budget — but in general RAG, on average rather than per-instance, and not as a test of whether a method's gain is a budget artifact. Context Rot (Chroma) supplies the premise that raw token count degrades performance independent of relevance.

**What the search did not find.** No paper applying length-matched, topically-irrelevant-filler controls to agentic memory curation methods to attribute their benefit or harm to token count rather than content. That is the gap. I state plainly that this is the result of six queries and that an appendix-level length-matched ablation inside MemHarness or A-MEM would reduce our contribution from "correction" to "systematization across methods" — which is why the fidelity gate and the re-examination table are written to stand on their own even in that case.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Reimplementation fidelity.** C7a/C7b are built from published descriptions, not released code; a weak reimplementation could tie its budget-matched baseline for reasons unrelated to the load hypothesis. Mitigated by the pre-registered fidelity gate (a baseline must first reproduce a positive delta over C1(7) at natural length on dev, or be reported as unreproduced and excluded). This is the single largest threat to prediction 4.
2. **Model specificity.** A long-context or distillation-heavy model may be robust to injection volume. We span 8B and 14B and report per-model budget curves; "harm vanishes at larger scale" is an informative outcome, not a failure, but with two models we cannot claim a scaling trend.
3. **Decoy validity.** Same-environment decoys might be trivially ignorable in a way real items are not; C2u (unrelated environment) and the citation-rate manipulation check bound this, but neither fully rules it out.
4. **Single primary environment.** All quantitative claims rest on E1; ALFWorld at n=200 is under-powered by design (MDE ~7–8 points) and can only confirm or fail to confirm direction. We chose depth on one environment over breadth because the paired/MDE design is the paper's selling point and cannot survive being spread thin. If E2 contradicts E1 directionally, we report the conflict rather than dropping E2.
5. **Partly a qualifying result.** Its value depends on the null being informative, which is why the null-replicate protocol, stated MDE and TOST equivalence tests are load-bearing rather than optional.
6. **Alternative mechanism.** If C4 (padded single item) is harmless while C5 (many truncated items) harms, the driver is item multiplicity, not token count, and the framing shifts from "injection budget" to "interference among competing exemplars." Still a clean finding, but the practical recommendation changes from "cap tokens" to "cap items," and we would say so rather than reinterpreting it as support for the budget claim.

Name: memory_dropout_coadaptation
Title: Don't Co-Adapt: A Bank-Swap Diagnostic for Prompt Optimizers Coupled to Self-Editing Memory, and Which Fix Actually Survives Bank Turnover
Short Hypothesis: When a reflective prompt optimizer evolves instructions while a retrieved experience memory is injected, it exploits the specific bank present at optimization time; because self-editing banks turn over in deployment, the resulting instruction is brittle and much of its measured gain does not survive a bank swap. The fragility is a property of the *optimization-time context distribution*, not of the deployment-time injection budget: randomizing that distribution during optimization (masking the injected memory block with probability p) should reduce the bank-dependence gap more than any deployment-side knob applied to an already co-adapted instruction, including reducing top-k at test time. The claim is not about dropout as a device: if shard resampling of the bank works equally well, the hypothesis survives and the instantiation changes; if deployment-time top-k tuning removes the gap just as well, the hypothesis is refuted and we say so.
Related Work:
MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024) jointly optimizes instructions and demonstrations, but the demonstration set is bootstrapped once and then frozen, so the context distribution at optimization time equals the one at deployment: no turnover, hence no co-adaptation risk to study. GEPA and other reflective prompt-evolution methods optimize instruction text against a fixed pipeline with retrieval and memory held constant. On the other side, ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (ICML 2025), and Skill Set Optimization (ICML 2024) continually rewrite a bank of insights or workflows while keeping the instruction fixed and hand-written; they measure transfer of the memory and never robustness of the prompt to memory churn. Practitioner frameworks that stack both components optimize the prompt with memory switched on and report end-to-end wins — exactly the co-adapted regime we argue is pathological.

We do not claim novelty for the intervention. Stochastic masking of an input block is standard (input dropout, domain randomization, and — as a reviewer correctly noted — Fusion-in-Decoder-style stochastic document dropping and randomized retrieved-context masking in RAG training curricula). We treat those as the mechanistic priors for the device and position accordingly.

The contribution is therefore stated comparatively rather than as priority on a mechanism: (i) a bank-swap protocol that measures optimizer–memory co-adaptation in accuracy points with item-paired statistics and a measured null-replicate floor; (ii) a head-to-head, cost-annotated comparison of the five candidate fixes an engineer would actually consider — optimization-time memory dropout, bank-shard randomization, deployment-time injection-budget (top-k) reduction, write-path bank curation, and full re-optimization on every bank change; and (iii) a test of whether the effect is memory-specific or a generic context-perturbation effect, via a length-matched neutral-block control run inside the primary grid rather than as an afterthought.

We removed the citation to "When Continual Learning Moves to Memory" that appeared in an earlier draft.
