We could not verify that identifier and will not carry an unverified citation; the role it played (item-level interference within a bank under a fixed prompt) is a real category we expect exists, but we will cite only papers we have verified.
Abstract:
Agent stacks increasingly place an automatic prompt optimizer on top of a self-editing experience memory and optimize the prompt with memory injection switched on. We argue this is a train/deploy mismatch: the instruction is evolved against one particular bank, but banks are rewritten continuously as the agent accumulates and prunes experience, so any gain that depends on bank-specific content evaporates. Pilot measurements motivating this work show that prompt evolution's apparent gains were largely redistribution (as many items fixed as broken), that memory injection can be one-sidedly harmful, that injection *volume* rather than content was the causal lever for that harm, and that the two components fail on disjoint slices.

That last pilot finding sets up the sharpest version of our claim. If the fragility were just an injection-budget problem, it would be curable at deployment by lowering top-k on the new bank, with no re-optimization at all. We test that directly. We propose memory dropout — during optimization rollouts the injected memory block is masked with probability p, so the optimizer sees the bank as a random rather than fixed context — and evaluate three levels (p=0, standard practice; p=0.5; p=1, memory-free optimization) on a single primary task (multi-hop QA with a retrieval tool) with a single 7B open-weight agent model, four optimizer seeds per level, and 800 item-paired held-out questions under three deployment banks (own, swapped, none). The primary endpoint is accuracy under the swapped bank; the primary diagnostic is D_swap = acc(own bank) − acc(swapped bank). Running in the same grid: a length-matched neutral-block dropout arm (memory-specific vs. generic perturbation), a deployment-time top-k reduction arm applied to co-adapted instructions (the reviewer-named competing fix, and the one that could kill the method), a write-path-curated bank, bank-shard randomization, and full re-optimization as the engineering upper bound. Every fix is reported with its optimization cost in LLM calls. We pre-register decision rules under which the honest conclusion becomes "just lower k at deployment", "optimize memory-free", or "any context randomization works", and report all effects against a measured null-replicate noise floor. The study is 21 optimization runs and ~70k paired evaluation episodes on one 4×A100 node, with frontier API use confined to bank distillation, reflection, and judging (≤$200).
Experiments:
**Fixed setup (one task, one agent model — deliberately).** Task: multi-hop QA with a retrieval tool (HotpotQA distractor setting, fullwiki-style tool calls), n=800 item-paired held-out questions, disjoint from all bank-construction and optimization data. Agent: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct served with vLLM, greedy decoding with fixed seeds. Memory: ExpeL-style bank distilled by a frontier model from training episodes (insights + successful/failed trajectory summaries), dense retrieval (bge-base), default injection top-k=4. Two disjoint training splits A and B yield two independent banks B_A and B_B. Optimizer: GEPA-style reflective instruction evolution (frontier model as reflector), instruction only, hard budget 300 rollouts per run.

**Stage 1 — gate (run first, ~4 optimization runs, ~10k episodes).**
E0: confirm memory-free optimization beats the hand-written instruction at k=0 by more than the measured noise floor. If prompt optimization does nothing here, the interaction question is vacuous and we change task before spending anything else.
E-gate: one seed each of p=0, 0.5, 1 and the neutral-block control, evaluated on own/swapped/no bank. Proceed only if the point estimate of D_swap at p=0 is ≥3 accuracy points. If not, we stop and report a bounded null ("co-adaptation costs less than X points on this setup"), a real reportable outcome. The gate quantity is not the primary endpoint contrast; the Stage-1 seed is carried into the final analysis and the staging is disclosed.

**Stage 2 — E1: dropout level × deployment bank (the experiment that decides the main claim).**
Optimize on split A with p ∈ {0, 0.5, 1.0}, 4 seeds each (12 instructions), evaluated on B_A, B_B, and no bank: 36 cells. Plus neutral-block dropout at rate 0.5 (a length-matched non-memory text block is masked instead of memory), 3 seeds × {B_A, B_B}: 6 cells. Total 42 cells × 800 = **33,600 episodes**.
Primary endpoint: accuracy under B_swap, contrasts p=0.5 vs p=0 and p=0.5 vs p=1.
Primary diagnostic: D_swap per condition.
Analysis: mixed-effects logistic regression on per-item outcomes with crossed item and optimizer-seed random intercepts; fixed effects for condition, bank, and interaction.

**E2 — deployment-time injection-budget arm (new; the competing fix that could kill the method).**
Take the p=0 co-adapted instructions unchanged and evaluate on the swapped bank B_B with injection reduced to k=2 and k=1 (4 seeds × 2 levels = 8 cells), plus p=0.5 at k=2 (2 seeds, 2 cells) to test whether the two fixes are additive or redundant. 10 cells × 800 = **8,000 episodes**. Zero optimization cost. This is the arm motivated by the pilot's own volume-is-the-lever finding: if lowering k at deployment reduces D_swap as much as memory dropout does, the correct engineering advice is "tune the injection budget", not "change how you optimize", and we will report that as the finding (P8).

**E3 — complementarity decomposition (no new runs; computed from E1 + baseline cells).**
For each condition, C = acc(instr, bank) − max(acc(instr, no bank), acc(hand-written, bank)), plus item-paired fixes/breaks against both single-component cells. Prediction: C ≈ 0 or negative at p=1 (substitution), positive on B_A but not B_B at p=0 (non-transferable), positive and swap-surviving at p=0.5.

**E4 — mechanism probe (cheap, exploratory).**
A frontier judge scores each of the 21 optimized instructions for (a) count of concrete entities/procedures appearing verbatim or near-verbatim in B_A items, (b) presence of explicit deference language ("if a retrieved example matches …, otherwise ignore it"). Spearman correlation of each score with that instruction's D_swap. n=21: exploratory, bootstrap CI, no claim gated on it.

**E5 — the one-sentence fix that could also kill the method.**
Append to each p=1 instruction (4 seeds) either a hand-written deference clause or a length-matched neutral clause; evaluate on B_swap only. 8 cells × 800 = **6,400 episodes**. If the deference clause recovers most of p=0.5's advantage, the mechanism is one sentence and dropout is unnecessary machinery — we report that.

**Baselines (19 cells, 15,200 episodes).** Hand-written instruction × 3 banks (3); unoptimized paraphrase control × 2 banks (2); bank-shard randomization 3 seeds × {own, swap} (6); continuous re-optimization 3 seeds optimized on B_B and evaluated on B_B (3); curated-bank baseline — p=0 instructions, 4 seeds, on a write-path-repaired B_B (4) — plus hand-written on the curated bank (1). Rationale per baseline in the next field.

**Noise floor (9 cells, 7,200 episodes).** Three representative cells re-run with three additional decoding-seed replicates each, one of which is a null replicate (an identical configuration relabelled as a treatment) to measure the apparent effect produced by nothing.

**Resource arithmetic.** Optimization: 21 runs (4 each at p=0/0.5/1, 3 neutral-block, 3 shard-randomization, 3 re-optimization) × 300 rollouts = **6,300 rollouts**. Evaluation: 33,600 (E1) + 8,000 (E2) + 6,400 (E5) + 15,200 (baselines) + 7,200 (noise floor) = **70,400 paired episodes**; ~76,700 agent episodes total. At ~4 LLM calls per episode, ~1.2k prompt / ~200 output tokens per call, Qwen2.5-7B on 4×A100 with vLLM at 64-way batching, generation is ≈6.3 GPU-hours; with retrieval, tool latency and scheduling slack we budget 2–3 wall-clock days. Frontier API: bank distillation (~800 calls), reflection (~60 × 21 = ~1,260), judging (~60) ≈ 2,100 calls, under $200. The new top-k arm added 8,000 episodes and *zero* optimization runs; we offset it by dropping the no-bank column for the neutral-block control (−2,400) and cutting one noise-floor replicate per cell (−2,400), for a net +3,200 episodes (+5%) over the previous draft, which the envelope absorbs.

**What we cut and why.** ALFWorld (n=300 ⇒ MDE ≈5 points, could only support direction, and cannot adjudicate the ~3-point claim this study is powered for), the 14B and Llama agent models, the grown/pruned bank conditions, dropout levels p=0.25 and 0.75, the five-round longitudinal drift study, and the MIPROv2 bootstrapped-demonstration arm. None decides the primary claim. On the reviewer request for a second task or model: we refuse, because at this envelope a second task is necessarily underpowered relative to the effect size we can resolve, and an underpowered replication is worse than an honestly single-setting result. Scope is stated as a limitation rather than papered over.
Baselines and Ablations:
Baselines that could plausibly win, each with a pre-registered consequence:

1. **Deployment-time top-k reduction on co-adapted instructions (E2; reviewer-named, now a primary competing fix).** Motivated by the pilot finding that injection volume, not content, drove memory harm. Pre-registered rule: if lowering k at deployment reduces D_swap for p=0 instructions to within 1.5 points of what memory dropout achieves, we report that optimization-time randomization is unnecessary and the correct advice is to calibrate the injection budget. The paper then becomes the bank-swap diagnostic plus a negative result on our own method — reportable, and it settles the question the field is currently guessing at.
2. **Memory-free optimization then memory at test (p=1).** The simplest decoupling. If it ties p=0.5 under swap (difference < 2 points or seeds inconsistent in sign), the honest conclusion is "never co-adapt; just optimize memory-free" — weaker but reportable, and still confirms that the optimization-time context distribution is the lever.
3. **Bank-shard randomization.** Optimize against a bank resampled each rollout from disjoint shards of split A. The stronger augmentation. If it matches or beats p=0.5 under swap, we report dropout as the cheaper equivalent and the claim becomes "randomizing the optimization-time memory context is necessary; the specific randomizer does not matter", decided by an accuracy-per-optimization-dollar table.
4. **Standard co-adaptation (p=0) on its own bank.** The number current frameworks report; quantifies how much of it is non-transferable.
5. **Write-path-curated bank.** Apply the repairs already shown to neutralize memory harm (contradiction pruning, call-balance rebalancing) to B_B, then evaluate the p=0 instructions on it. If curation alone collapses D_swap, dropout solves a problem write-path hygiene already solves, and we say so (P7).
6. **Continuous re-optimization.** Optimize on B_B, evaluate on B_B: the engineering upper bound and the obvious alternative to making one instruction robust. Reported with its cost (300 rollouts + reflector calls per bank update); the interesting quantity is the accuracy gap to p=0.5, which costs zero on bank update.
7. **Hand-written instruction + memory, and hand-written alone.**
8. **Unoptimized paraphrase control** — length-matched paraphrase of the hand-written instruction, bounding how much of any effect is instruction identity rather than optimization regime.

Ablations kept:
(a) **Neutral-block dropout, inside the primary grid** — masks a length-matched non-memory block at the same rate, separating generic context perturbation from memory-specific decoupling. If it matches memory dropout, the claim becomes the generic one and we retitle (P6).
(b) **Additivity probe** — p=0.5 evaluated at k=2, to test whether optimization-time randomization and deployment-time budget reduction are redundant or complementary.
(c) **Instruction length as a covariate** — dropout may simply produce longer/shorter instructions; reported per condition and re-fit as a fixed effect.
(d) **Deference clause vs. neutral clause (E5).**

Ablations dropped for budget: test-time dropout, multi-model replication, MIPROv2 demonstration-slot comparison. The demo-slot question (is this specific to self-edited memory or true of any demonstration slot?) needs its own optimizer implementation; the neutral-block control carries the mechanism isolation this paper needs.
Falsifiable Predictions:
P1 (co-adaptation is fragile). D_swap ≥ 4 accuracy points at p=0, 95% CI excluding 1 point, while D_swap ≤ 1.5 points at p=0.5 and p=1. Refutation: D_swap at p=0 within the noise floor. Consequence: co-adaptation is a non-problem; bounded null reported with its upper bound; stop at Stage 1.

P2 (interior dropout dominates under turnover). Under the swapped bank, p=0.5 beats p=0 by ≥3 points and beats p=1 by ≥2 points, all four optimizer seeds agreeing in sign. Refutation: p=1 matches or beats p=0.5; conclusion becomes "optimize memory-free".

P3 (interior dominance, not curve shape). With three levels we test only that the interior point beats both endpoints; we explicitly do not claim an inverted-U. Refutation: monotone ordering across the three levels.

P4 (mechanism, exploratory). Instruction/bank textual-overlap score correlates with D_swap at Spearman rho ≥ 0.5 across 21 instructions. Refutation: rho near zero — the stated mechanism is wrong, reported as such, accuracy results standing on their own.

P5 (cheap fix does not suffice). The hand-written deference clause appended to p=1 recovers < half of p=0.5's advantage over p=1 under swap. Refutation: it recovers most of it — publishable, but it kills the method.

P6 (memory-specificity). Neutral-block dropout at rate 0.5 recovers < half of memory dropout's advantage over p=0 under swap. Refutation: it matches — the claim becomes generic optimization-time context perturbation and the memory-specific framing is withdrawn.

P7 (curation does not pre-empt it). D_swap at p=0 against a write-path-curated swapped bank remains ≥ 3 points. Refutation: curation removes fragility — correct advice is "clean the bank".

P8 (the mismatch is not a deployment-budget problem — the load-bearing new prediction). For p=0 instructions on the swapped bank, the best deployment-time k ∈ {1,2} reduces D_swap by less than half of the reduction achieved by memory dropout at k=4, and p=0.5 at k=4 still beats the best (p=0, reduced-k) cell by ≥2 points. Refutation: reduced-k on co-adapted instructions comes within 1.5 points of p=0.5 — in which case the fragility is an injection-budget artifact curable at inference, memory dropout is unnecessary machinery, and we report that as the paper's result rather than defending the method.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Every deployment evaluation is item-paired: all cells scored on identical held-out items with identical decoding seeds, so the unit of analysis is the per-item outcome change. Pairwise contrasts use McNemar's exact test on discordant pairs, with fixes and breaks reported separately (the pilot showed net deltas can be flat while composition shifts).

Optimizer stochasticity is the dominant nuisance, so the three primary p-levels get 4 independent optimizer seeds (controls get 3) and instructions are treated as a random factor. Pre-registered primary analysis: mixed-effects logistic regression on per-item outcomes with crossed item and seed random intercepts; the reported quantity is the condition × bank interaction with a 95% CI. Because a between-seed variance component from 4 levels is imprecise, a claim requires three things jointly: (i) pooled CI excludes zero, (ii) all seeds agree in sign, (iii) the effect exceeds twice the measured between-seed SD. Reporting a single lucky prompt is disallowed.

The E2 top-k arm reuses the same 12 instructions and the same 800 items, so the dropout-vs-budget-tuning comparison (P8) is itself item-paired and seed-paired at the instruction level, which is why it can be decided at this sample size despite being an added arm.

Noise floor: three representative cells re-run with three additional decoding-seed replicates, one of which is a null replicate — an identical configuration relabelled as a treatment — measuring the apparent effect produced by nothing. No claim unless the effect exceeds the 95th percentile of the null-replicate distribution.

Power / minimum detectable effect: with n=800 paired items and ~10% discordance, McNemar detects roughly 2.5 accuracy points at 80% power within a single seed pair. Across seeds the binding constraint is the between-seed SD, which the pilot suggests is 1–2 points; this study can adjudicate effects of roughly 3 points and larger under the swapped bank and cannot resolve smaller ones. If the true p=0 vs p=0.5 gap is 1–2 points we report a bounded null with its upper confidence limit, not a positive result.

Held-out items are disjoint from bank construction, optimization, and probe data. Holm correction across secondary cell-wise contrasts and baseline comparisons; the primary interaction test and the P8 contrast are pre-registered as the two confirmatory tests and Bonferroni-corrected against each other (alpha 0.025 each). The Stage-1 gate is disclosed as a selection step and its seed included in the final pooled analysis.
Preprint Collision Check:
**The literature search commissioned for this revision failed again, completely.** Every web-search call in this session returned a hard server-side "tool use limit exceeded" error; not one query returned data. I therefore have **zero verified evidence** about recent preprints on this topic, and I will not treat that silence as evidence of novelty. Stated plainly: as of this draft, the novelty of the framing (optimizer–memory co-adaptation as a train/deploy context-distribution mismatch) and of the intervention (masking injected memory during optimization rollouts) is **unverified**. Both reviewers flagged this and both are right to count it against the proposal.

Closest work I can name from background knowledge, **explicitly unverified against any dated search**: on the prompt-optimization side, MIPROv2, GEPA, OPRO/APE/TextGrad; on the memory side, ExpeL, Reflexion, Agent Workflow Memory, Skill Set Optimization, MemGPT/Voyager-style self-editing agents; on the mechanism side, Fusion-in-Decoder-style stochastic document dropping and randomized retrieved-context masking in RAG training curricula (raised by reviewer 2 and, in my assessment, the correct mechanistic prior — the device is not ours). On my understanding, none of these runs a bank-swap or turnover-robustness evaluation of an *optimized instruction*, which is the diagnostic this paper contributes. But that is an unverified belief, not a checked fact.

Because I cannot verify priority, I have already restructured the contribution so it does not depend on priority. The paper's claim is comparative: given that co-adaptation exists and is measurable, *which* of five candidate fixes (optimization-time dropout, shard randomization, deployment-time top-k reduction, bank curation, full re-optimization) actually survives bank turnover, at what optimization cost. A preprint that identifies the co-adaptation problem first does not scoop that table; a preprint that runs the same comparison does, and we would say so.

Before submission we will run and log a dated search with these queries, recording date, source, and top hits per query, as an appendix: "prompt optimization memory co-adaptation"; "GEPA agent memory bank robustness"; "context dropout prompt optimizer"; "domain randomization retrieved demonstrations LLM"; "instruction optimization non-stationary retrieval"; "self-editing memory prompt overfitting"; "experience bank turnover agent prompt"; "randomized context prompt search robustness"; "retrieved context dropout RAG training"; "prompt robustness memory drift agent". If a preprint already performs a bank-swap or turnover-robustness evaluation of an optimized instruction, the contribution reduces to the fix-comparison table plus the P8 result, and we will state that in the paper rather than re-framing around it.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Gated on prompt optimization working at all.** If GEPA's memory-free gain on a 7B model sits under the noise floor, the interaction is unmeasurable. E0 runs first and cheaply; failure means switching task or model before further spend.
2. **The effect may be small.** If D_swap at p=0 is 1–2 points, the study is underpowered by construction and we report a bounded null. Stated in Measurement rather than discovered afterwards.
3. **Deployment-time top-k tuning may simply win (P8).** This is now the most likely way the method dies, and it is a primary arm rather than a missing baseline. Pre-committed: if reduced-k on co-adapted instructions matches memory dropout, we report the diagnostic plus a negative result on our own intervention.
4. **Single task, single agent model.** The main cost of fitting the envelope, and we declined the reviewer request for a second task because at n≈300 it could not adjudicate a 3-point effect. Any result is a claim about instruction-only reflective optimization over an ExpeL-style bank on multi-hop QA with Qwen2.5-7B, phrased that way throughout. Generalization is future work, not implied.
5. **Bank-shard randomization may beat dropout,** reducing the contribution to a cost argument. Pre-committed: report accuracy per optimization dollar and rewrite the claim as "randomize the optimization-time memory context".
6. **Dropout may be a generic regularizer.** The neutral-block arm is in the primary grid to catch this (P6); if it matches, the memory-specific framing is withdrawn.
7. **Curation may pre-empt the problem** (P7). If write-path hygiene removes fragility, that is the advice we give.
8. **Abrupt swap ≠ real drift.** Disjoint-split swaps are the maximal-turnover limit. We dropped the five-round incremental drift study for budget, so we make no claim about the shape of degradation under gradual self-editing.
9. **Instruction-only optimization.** We do not study optimizers that rewrite the demonstration slot; whether the phenomenon is specific to self-edited memory or true of any demonstration slot is left open and stated as open.
10. **Novelty is unverified** because the literature search failed twice (see Preprint Collision Check). This remains the single largest non-technical risk, and the contribution has been restructured comparatively to limit the damage if a collision surfaces.

Name: memory_induced_shortcutting
Title: Memory Makes Agents Stop Looking: Premature Termination of Evidence Gathering Mediates Memory Harm, and Instruction Optimization Cannot Repair It
Short Hypothesis: When retrieved-experience memory breaks an otherwise-solvable task, the proximate cause is usually that the agent stopped gathering evidence early — it treats a past outcome as if it were evidence about the current instance and terminates after fewer tool calls — rather than that it executed a specific bad action recommended by memory. Three consequences follow and are tested: (i) memory items that carry an OUTCOME (a past answer or completed result) cause shortcutting, while token-matched process-only items do not; (ii) a content-free evidence floor enforced in the control flow (the agent may not answer until it has itself retrieved spans that support its answer) removes most of the harm while preserving the benefit, and helps the memory-augmented agent far more than the memory-free one; (iii) the repair belongs to the control flow and not the instruction slot — a GEPA-optimized instruction, searched with full reflective access to shortcutting failures, will not recover the floor's benefit. Claim (iii) is the division-of-labour claim: some agent pathologies are not addressable by prompt optimization at all.
Related Work:
The search this proposal was revised against returned one work that is genuinely close and several that are adjacent. I list them by how much they threaten the claim, and I have removed from this draft every citation I could not verify in the search results.

**Closest: experience-following.** *How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior* (Xiong et al., ACL 2026; arXiv:2505.16067) establishes that high input-similarity between the current task and a retrieved record produces highly similar agent outputs, and names "misaligned experience replay" — the agent reuses a prior solution path instead of solving the present instance. This is the correlational core of our phenomenon and we treat it as established prior work, not as something to rediscover. What it does not do: it characterises the harm at the level of output similarity and memory-management policy (what to add, what to delete). It never measures how many evidence-gathering actions the agent takes, never tests whether truncation mediates the failure, never separates outcome-bearing from process-bearing content at matched token count, and offers no intervention that leaves memory content untouched. Our claim is strictly downstream of theirs and is falsifiable against it: if experience-following harms arise without any reduction in evidence gathering, our account is wrong and theirs is complete.

**Transfer-quality accounts.** *A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents* (arXiv:2604.27003) finds that abstract procedural memories transfer more reliably than detailed trajectories and that negative transfer concentrates on hard cases. This is the single most important adjacent result because it partially anticipates our M2 vs M3 contrast: "procedural beats trajectory" is consistent with "outcome content is what hurts". It is, however, a comparison between differently-authored memory formats, confounded with length, abstraction level and information content, and it explains the asymmetry by transferability of knowledge rather than by a behavioural mechanism. Our redaction design holds the item, the retrieval, and the token count fixed and deletes exactly the outcome, which is the manipulation that decides between "abstraction is better knowledge" and "outcomes stop the search".

**Content-bias accounts.** *Memory-Induced Tool-Drift* (arXiv:2605.24941) shows stored persona biases steer tool-call parameters — a bias in *which* tool and *with what arguments*, not in *whether the agent keeps looking*. *RoMeRL* (arXiv:2608.02508) names a "memory-reward trap" arising from utility cold-start in trajectory-indexed memory; this is about estimating memory usefulness, not about termination behaviour.

**Adversarial memory.** *OEP* (arXiv:2605.18930), *MemoryGraft* (arXiv:2512.16962) and *When Agents Remember Too Much* (arXiv:2607.06595) study poisoned or non-transferable experiences implanted by an attacker. They share our intuition that "locally correct" experience generalises badly, but the failure is engineered; we study the organic case where an ordinary ExpeL-style write path produces a bank that helps some instances and breaks others.

**Prompt optimization.** MIPRO and GEPA decompose a prompt into instructions and demonstrations and search the instruction slot with reflective/evolutionary updates. No work we found asks whether a failure mode induced by the demonstration/memory slot is *repairable from the instruction slot*. That question — which is the track's division-of-labour question — is where prediction (iii) lives, and it is what turns this from a memory-mechanism study into a statement about what prompt optimization can and cannot own.
Abstract:
Retrieved-experience memory frequently makes LLM agents worse, and the field's explanations are about what is in the memory: it is stale, non-transferable, conflicting, or simply too long. We propose a procedural explanation instead. An agent working a multi-step task must decide when it has looked enough; a retrieved item about a similar past task supplies a plausible-looking answer, and the agent stops early, answering on evidence it never gathered. Under this account the harm is not that the agent follows bad advice but that it truncates its own search, and it is therefore repairable without touching memory content — but only by an intervention that lives in the control flow.

We test three things on one primary environment. First, mediation: on instances that memory breaks, do trajectories shorten, and does the memory-versus-no-memory break effect lose most of its coefficient once evidence-gathering depth and evidence sufficiency are entered? Second, a token-matched content decomposition: outcome-redacted items (procedure kept, past answer deleted) versus outcome-only items versus topically irrelevant decoys. The shortcutting account predicts redaction keeps most of the fixes and sheds most of the breaks, while decoys do not truncate at all. Third, and centrally, a ladder of repairs at three levels of the agent stack: a hand-written self-verification instruction, a GEPA-searched instruction optimized with reflective access to the shortcutting failures, and a content-free evidence floor enforced programmatically. The floor is applied to both the memory and memory-free arms, so the claim is an interaction and not "more search is good". Our sharp and risky prediction is that the two instruction-level repairs, including the searched one, recover less than a third of the floor's benefit: premature commitment is a control-flow property that the instruction slot cannot own. A perturbed-corpus probe, where the current answer deliberately differs from what a topically similar past episode implies, gives a positive control in which shortcutting must produce a specific identifiable wrong answer. All comparisons are instance-paired with fix/break decompositions, null replicates, and a stated minimum detectable effect, inside a budget of ~23k episodes and ~$120 of API spend.
Experiments:
HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: agent scaffold (ReAct with a search/lookup tool over a fixed corpus), tool stack, maximum step limit, retriever and similarity function, memory bank (built once from a training split with an ExpeL-style write path, then frozen for the whole study), decoding temperature and seed schedule, prompt boilerplate, and the held-out test split. Only the memory variant and the stopping/instruction rule vary.

ENVIRONMENT (one, deliberately). Tool-augmented multi-hop QA, pooled across HotpotQA (distractor), MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA in fixed proportions, 4–8 model calls per episode. Evidence gathering is explicit, countable and cheap to instrument, so this environment carries every quantitative claim. WebShop and ALFWorld were in the previous draft and are cut: at the n we can afford they could not have been powered, and an underpowered replication carries no claim. Cross-environment generality is stated as a limitation, not smuggled in as a weak experiment. Within-environment diversity comes from the three datasets, which are reported separately as well as pooled.

MODELS. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is primary and carries all headline numbers. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the decisive subset of arms at one seed; model dependence is a predicted risk, so this replication carries a real claim (does the shortcutting effect survive a different context-deference profile?). Qwen3-32B is used only as the bulk trajectory annotator, not as an agent. A frontier API model performs one-off bank distillation, outcome redaction, GEPA reflection, and gold annotation on a costed validation sample.

PRECHECK (gates the study, 150 dev instances, ~1,500 episodes). Confirm the standard memory agent both fixes ≥4% and breaks ≥4% of instances relative to no memory. A bank with no breaks leaves nothing to explain; a bank with no fixes makes the preservation half of the claim untestable. We report these numbers rather than proceeding quietly.

ARMS (all fully paired: every test instance is run under every arm at every seed).

Memory-content arms:
- **M0** No memory.
- **M1** Memory, top-k=7 (standard deployment).
- **M2** Outcome-redacted memory: the same k=7 items with any final answer, result value or statement of completion deleted, procedural content kept (which sources to consult, how to disambiguate, in what order), padded with neutral task-generic filler to match M1's injected token count within 5% per instance. THE key content manipulation.
- **M3** Outcome-only memory: the mirror of M2, past answers retained, procedure deleted, token-matched. Should shortcut maximally.
- **M4** Decoy memory: k=7 items retrieved for a query from a disjoint task family, token-matched. Separates generic context load from experience-specific shortcutting.
- **M5** Memory, k=3. The volume-reduction competitor from the track's prior findings.

Repair-ladder arms (the division-of-labour test):
- **M1+Fh / M0+Fh** EVIDENCE FLOOR, hard: before emitting a final answer the agent must list the spans it retrieved *in this episode* that support the answer; if it cannot, the harness rejects the answer and forces at least one further tool call, capped at three extra calls. Content-free — it never reads memory. Applying it to M0 as well is what makes the result an interaction rather than "search more".
- **M1+Fs** EVIDENCE FLOOR, soft: the identical requirement stated as an instruction, with no programmatic enforcement. This is the lightweight self-verification baseline a reviewer would reach for.
- **G1 / G0** GEPA-optimized instructions, with and without memory. GEPA runs on the instruction slot only (memory occupies the demonstration slot and is frozen), with a 400-rollout budget on a 150-instance train split, and — this is the point — the reflective feedback it receives explicitly includes the failed trajectories and their tool-call counts, so the optimizer has every opportunity to discover "keep looking, verify against your own retrieval". G1 is the strong instruction-level repair.

Alternative-mechanism controls:
- **M6** M1 with the step budget raised by the average number of extra calls the hard floor consumes, no sufficiency requirement. Separates "forced to look longer" from "forced to justify".
- **M7** Self-consistency: 3 M1 rollouts, majority answer, at matched total model calls. Refutes us if the fix is just sampling. Given a real slot and sample size rather than discussed hypothetically.

INSTRUMENTATION (every episode): tool calls before final answer; distinct documents examined; EVIDENCE SUFFICIENCY (binary — do the spans supporting the final answer appear in this episode's own retrievals?); MEMORY-ECHO (is the final answer verbatim or semantically identical to content in an injected item?); floor-compliance (do the cited spans genuinely support the answer, so the floor cannot be satisfied by fabrication); self-reported confidence at termination.

ANALYSIS 1 — MEDIATION (observational, supporting). Per instance, compute the paired M1-vs-M0 outcome (fix / break / unchanged) and the paired deltas in tool calls and sufficiency. Prediction: broken instances show a large drop in calls relative to their own M0 trajectory, fixed instances do not; a mixed-effects model of the break event on the memory indicator loses most of its coefficient once call-delta and sufficiency are entered. The mediator is post-treatment, so this is descriptive; the floor arms are the causal test.

ANALYSIS 2 — MANIPULATING THE MEDIATOR (the causal test). Headline quantity: the interaction (breaks under M1 − breaks under M1+Fh) − (errors under M0 − errors under M0+Fh). M6 checks the effect is not merely budget; M7 checks it is not merely sampling.

ANALYSIS 3 — CONTENT DECOMPOSITION. M1 / M2 / M3 / M4, all token-matched, with full fix/break tables and tool-call distributions.

ANALYSIS 4 — DIVISION OF LABOUR (the track-facing claim). Compare break reduction achieved by M1+Fs (instruction, hand-written), G1 (instruction, searched) and M1+Fh (control flow), all against M1, on matched-cost axes. We additionally read out G1's evolved instruction text and its floor-compliance rate: the sharpest version of the prediction is that GEPA *writes* verification language into the instruction and the agent still does not comply, so the gap is enforcement, not discovery.

ANALYSIS 5 — PERTURBED-CORPUS POSITIVE CONTROL (200 additional instances). We edit the retrieval corpus so the correct current answer differs from the answer implied by a topically near-identical stored episode (e.g. an updated office-holder or record value), applied consistently across all corpus documents so the environment stays coherent. Shortcutting predicts a specific fingerprint: under M1 the agent returns the memory-consistent stale value at a high rate after fewer calls, while M2, M1+Fh and G1 re-check and recover. Run under M0, M1, M2, M1+Fh, G1.

SAMPLE SIZES AND BUDGET ARITHMETIC.
- Qwen-14B main grid: 12 single-rollout arms (M0, M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M1+Fh, M0+Fh, M1+Fs, G1, G0) × 500 paired test instances × 2 seeds = 12,000 episodes.
- M7 (3 rollouts): 500 × 2 × 3 = 3,000.
- Perturbed subset: 200 × 2 seeds × 5 arms = 2,000.
- Null replicates (M0, M1, M1+Fh at a third seed): 1,500.
- Precheck: 1,500.
- Llama-8B replication, decisive arms only (M0, M1, M2, M3, M1+Fh, M0+Fh, G1) × 500 × 1 seed = 3,500.
- GEPA search: 2 conditions × 400 rollouts = 800 episodes + ~120 frontier reflection calls.
Total ≈ **24,300 episodes**, ~6 model calls each ≈ 146k model calls. With vLLM running four data-parallel Qwen2.5-14B replicas on 4×A100-80GB and 128 concurrent episodes, we measure and budget conservatively at ~1,200 episodes/hour, giving ~20 hours for the 14B work and ~4 hours for the 8B work; with annotation passes, retries and the 32B annotator, the whole study is budgeted at **~40 node-hours, i.e. two days**.
API: bank distillation of ~600 items (~$10), two redaction passes (~$15), GEPA reflection (~$10), gold annotation of a fixed 600-episode validation sample (~$40), contingency (~$45). **Total ≤ $120.** Bulk annotation of the remaining episodes uses the self-hosted Qwen3-32B, not the API.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) **G1, GEPA-optimized instructions with memory** — the baseline the track's framing demands and the one that most directly threatens our sharpest claim. If instruction search recovers the floor's break reduction, the answer to memory-induced shortcutting is "optimize your prompt", prediction (iii) is dead, and we say so.
(ii) **M1+Fs, hand-written self-verification instruction** — the cheap instruction-level version of the floor.
(iii) **M5, k=3** — the track's prior finding that volume is the causal lever. If M5 matches M2 and M1+Fh on both breaks and fixes, the practical recommendation is "retrieve less" and our mechanism adds nothing actionable.
(iv) **M6, raised step budget without a sufficiency requirement** — if merely allowing more calls recovers the benefit, the mechanism is budget, not premature commitment.
(v) **M0+Fh** — if the floor helps the memory-free agent as much as the memory-augmented one, there is no interaction and the finding degenerates into "citing evidence is good", which is known and not about memory.
(vi) **M7, self-consistency at matched model calls** — with a real slot, 500 instances × 2 seeds × 3 rollouts.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM. M2 vs M3 is the core content contrast: same items, same retrieval, same token count, opposite halves deleted, so any asymmetry is attributable to outcome-bearing content rather than to memory in general. M4 removes experience relevance while holding load constant. The floor applied to both M0 and M1 is the essential design feature — the claim is the interaction, never the main effect. Floor-compliance auditing prevents the floor from being satisfied by fabricated citations, and the same audit applied to G1 and M1+Fs is what distinguishes "the optimizer failed to discover the fix" from "the optimizer discovered it and the agent ignored it". A memory-echo readout separates copying from guessing. All arms are reported on matched tool-call, matched token, and wall-clock axes so no arm is credited for spending more.
Falsifiable Predictions:
If the shortcutting account holds:
1. Instances broken by M1 show a median of ≥1.5 fewer tool calls than the same instances under M0, and ≥30% relative reduction in mean calls, while instances fixed by M1 show no such reduction; the difference of the two deltas clears the noise floor.
2. Evidence sufficiency drops ≥12 points under M1 relative to M0, and memory-echo on wrong answers exceeds 40%.
3. **Interaction:** M1+Fh cuts breaks relative to M1 by ≥50%, while M0+Fh improves M0 by less than a third of that in absolute points, with the interaction clearing the stated MDE; M1+Fh stays within 2 points of M1 on fixes.
4. **Content decomposition:** M2 retains ≥70% of M1's fixes while shedding ≥50% of its breaks at matched tokens; M3 breaks at least as many instances as M1 with the shortest trajectories of any arm.
5. **Load control:** M4 reproduces <1/3 of M1's tool-call reduction.
6. **Division of labour (the risky one):** M1+Fs and G1 each recover <1/3 of M1+Fh's break reduction, and G1's evolved instruction contains explicit verification/keep-searching language in at least one of the two conditions while its floor-compliance rate stays within 10 points of M1's — i.e. the optimizer says it and the agent does not do it.
7. **Positive control:** on the perturbed subset M1 returns the stale memory-consistent answer on ≥50% of its errors, versus <20% for M2, M1+Fh and G1.
8. Confidence at termination is higher under M1 than M0 on instances with insufficient evidence, so calibration error rises.

REFUTATION CONDITIONS. If broken instances under M1 have trajectories no shorter than under M0, the mediation claim is dead. If M1+Fh and M0+Fh improve by similar amounts, there is no interaction and the floor is a good idea unrelated to memory. If M2 sheds fixes along with breaks (fix retention <50%), outcome content is doing the useful work and redaction is not viable. If M4 reproduces the truncation, the phenomenon is generic context load and we reframe. If M5 matches M1+Fh and M2 on every endpoint, the volume account subsumes ours. **If G1 matches M1+Fh on breaks, prediction (iii) is false and the correct conclusion is that instruction optimization does own this failure mode — we report that as the finding rather than burying it.**
Measurement and Noise Control:
Fully paired design: every held-out instance is run under every arm with the same seed schedule, so all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar tests on paired fix/break tables, Holm-corrected across the arm family; every reported delta carries its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention. The floor interaction and the division-of-labour comparison are tested in mixed-effects logistic models with instance random intercepts and memory×repair interaction terms, with 95% CIs from a 10k-resample instance-level bootstrap. Tool-call counts use paired Wilcoxon tests and are reported as full distributions, since the predicted effect is a shift in the lower tail.

NULL REPLICATES: for each model we re-run M0, M1 and M1+Fh under a third decoding seed and report the distribution of apparent deltas; no effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. This is load-bearing given the track's prior observation of 5–14 point re-scoring drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.

MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECTS at n=500 paired instances (2 seeds averaged per instance before pairing): with an expected 12–18% discordant-pair rate, McNemar detects a net swing of ~4.5 points at 80% power (α=0.05). The break endpoint is one-sided and more sensitive: with M1 breaking ~50 of 500, a halving is detected with power >0.85. The memory×floor interaction, a difference of two paired differences, is detectable at ~6 points — which is exactly why prediction 3 is stated as a ≥50% break reduction against a much smaller M0+Fh gain, and why we would not have claimed anything smaller. The fix-preservation claim is an equivalence test at a 2-point margin and is the weakest arm; differences between 2 and 3 points will be reported as inconclusive. Tool-call deltas of ~0.45 calls/episode are detectable. The Llama-8B replication at one seed has an MDE of roughly 7 points and is reported as directional model-dependence evidence with that stated.

ANNOTATION. Evidence-sufficiency, memory-echo and floor-compliance labels come from the self-hosted Qwen3-32B annotator, validated against a 600-episode frontier-model gold sample and a 200-episode human-labelled sample, with Cohen's kappa reported for each label. Annotation-dependent analyses are re-run with the frontier annotator on the gold subset to show they are not judge-specific, and are demoted to supporting evidence if kappa < 0.6. The binary task outcome — the primary endpoint — is exact-match/F1 against dataset gold and requires no judge at all.
Preprint Collision Check:
The search returned one work that genuinely threatens novelty and several adjacent ones. Note also that an earlier draft of this proposal cited a dozen forward-dated arXiv IDs that I could not verify; those have been removed, and this section cites only what the search returned.

**Closest: Xiong et al., "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior", ACL 2026 / arXiv:2505.16067.** Verdict: **partial collision on the phenomenon, no collision on the claim.** It establishes experience-following (high input similarity → highly similar outputs) and names misaligned experience replay, i.e. the agent reusing a prior solution path rather than solving the current instance. That is the correlational fact we build on and we credit it as such; our framing must no longer present "memory makes agents imitate the past" as new. What remains ours: (a) truncation of evidence gathering as the *measured mediator*, with fix/break decomposition and a mediation model; (b) the token-matched outcome-redaction / outcome-only decomposition, which isolates outcome-bearing content as the trigger rather than similarity per se; (c) the content-free control-flow intervention applied to both memory and memory-free arms as an interaction; (d) the division-of-labour result that a GEPA-searched instruction cannot substitute for it. None of these appear in 2505.16067, which studies memory *management policy* (what to add and delete) rather than agent stopping behaviour.

**A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents (arXiv:2604.27003).** Verdict: **near-miss on the content decomposition.** Finds abstract procedural memories transfer better than detailed trajectories and that negative transfer concentrates on hard cases. This partially anticipates our M2>M3 prediction, and we say so up front. The comparison there is between differently-authored memory formats — confounded with length, abstraction and information content — and is explained as a property of what knowledge transfers. Our redaction holds item, retrieval and token count fixed and deletes exactly the outcome, which is the manipulation that decides between "abstraction is better knowledge" and "outcomes terminate the search". If that paper's result is driven by the same mechanism, our study explains why; if our redaction contrast comes out null while their format contrast holds, our mechanism is wrong and theirs is a knowledge-transfer effect.

**Memory-Induced Tool-Drift (arXiv:2605.24941).** No collision: stored persona biases steer *which* tool is called and with what arguments, not *whether* the agent keeps looking. Different failure locus, useful as a contrast.

**RoMeRL (arXiv:2608.02508).** No collision: memory-utility cold start in trajectory-indexed memory; about estimating item usefulness, not termination.

**OEP (arXiv:2605.18930), MemoryGraft (arXiv:2512.16962), When Agents Remember Too Much (arXiv:2607.06595).** No collision: adversarially implanted experiences. They share the "locally correct, harmful when reused" intuition but engineer the failure; we study the organic case and never inject an attacker.

**Surveys and efficiency work** (case-based-reasoning surveys, agent-memory surveys, AgentStop-style early-exit papers) address architecture taxonomies or deliberate compute saving; early exit as a *desired* efficiency behaviour is the mirror image of our claim and is not a collision.

**Explicit gap statement from the search:** no found paper isolates reduced evidence-gathering actions as the mediating causal mechanism of memory harm, and none tests whether the repair belongs in the control flow versus the instruction slot. HONEST CAVEAT: I could not sweep ICLR/NeurIPS 2026 submission portals, and there is a nontrivial chance that an outcome-redaction or step-floor ablation sits in an appendix of a recent agent-memory preprint. Given 2505.16067, the phenomenon is no longer surprising; the mediator, the token-matched redaction contrast, and the instruction-versus-control-flow result are what must carry the paper, and the proposal is written so that each of those can independently fail.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Precheck failure.** The bank may produce too few breaks or too few fixes for the two halves of the claim. The precheck gates this and we report its numbers rather than proceeding quietly. If breaks are below 4%, we tune only the bank-construction split size (a pre-registered, memory-content-neutral knob) once, and abandon if it still fails.
2. **Post-treatment mediation.** Analysis 1 conditions on a post-treatment variable and cannot support causality alone; this is exactly why the floor arms exist, and the mediation is framed as descriptive throughout.
3. **The floor is a design surface.** It could be tuned into the result. It is fixed on a 100-instance dev split before any test run, published verbatim, capped at three extra calls, and audited for fabricated citations.
4. **Redaction leakage.** Procedural text can implicitly encode the answer ("search for the 1994 record"). We report an automated leakage audit plus a 150-item human check and treat leaked items as a measured contamination rate rather than assuming clean separation.
5. **GEPA under-search.** If G1 fails, a reviewer will ask whether the optimizer was simply given too little budget, making prediction (iii) unfalsifiable. Mitigation: we report GEPA's training-split score trajectory to show it converged, we feed the reflector the shortcutting failures explicitly, and we report the evolved instruction text — the claim survives only if GEPA *writes* verification language and compliance still does not move. If GEPA plateaus early with no verification language at all, we report the result as inconclusive on enforcement-vs-discovery rather than claiming (iii).
6. **Single environment.** Cutting ALFWorld and WebShop means the mechanism is demonstrated only where evidence gathering is literal retrieval. Generalization to embodied exploration is explicitly an open question, not an implied result. We chose two models over three environments because model-dependent context deference is the more likely threat to the mechanism.
7. **Model dependence.** A model heavily trained to defer to context may shortcut far more than one that ignores it. Per-model curves are reported instead of a pooled headline; strong model dependence is treated as a finding, not noise.
8. **Cost of the fix.** If the floor works but consumes substantially more tool calls, the honest framing is "a cheap procedural guard beats curating the bank, but it is not free", and all arms are reported on matched-cost axes so the trade-off is directly judgeable.
9. **Synthetic perturbation.** The perturbed-corpus subset is adversarial by construction; we keep the corpus internally consistent, restrict perturbations to values verifiable from the corpus alone, and report it as a mechanism probe, not a deployment estimate.

Name: memory_item_value_reliability
Title: Item Value Is Not an Item Property: A Generalizability Audit of Per-Item Utility Estimates in Self-Editing Agent Memory
Short Hypothesis: Every agent-memory curation method (verify-before-write, contradiction pruning, LLM-judge filtering, learned admission control) presumes that an individual memory item has a stable, estimable utility. We claim that presumption is false as a matter of measurable fact: the stable item main effect is a minority of the explainable outcome variance, being dominated by item-by-query interaction, so (i) the probe budget needed to rank items reliably exceeds what any published system spends by one to two orders of magnitude, (ii) items identified as harmful on one episode sample do not transfer as harmful to held-out episodes — pruning them is no better than removing the same number of items at random, and (iii) published cheap quality proxies correlate near zero with the stable component of item value. The constructive corollary: at matched compute, controlling the bank-level injection budget dominates item-level curation, and any item-level prune should be gated by a posterior credible interval rather than a point score.
Related Work:
Four clusters, with the 2026 curation literature as the direct target.

(1) Curation and admission methods that assume item-level utility is knowable. A-MAC, "Adaptive Memory Admission Control for LLM Agents" (arXiv:2603.04549, ICLR 2026 MemAgents workshop), decomposes memory value into five per-item factors (future utility, factual confidence, semantic novelty, temporal recency, content-type prior) and admits on their combination. SAGE (arXiv:2605.30711) gates writes on a per-item novelty score and explicitly positions itself against "fully delegated to per-fact LLM judgment" policies. A-MemGuard (arXiv:2510.02373) gates writes by consensus checks. Memory-R1 (arXiv:2508.19828) trains an RL manager emitting per-item ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP. AutoManual (NeurIPS 2024) validates distilled rules before consolidation; EDV (arXiv:2606.24428) verifies distilled experience with a separate agent. "Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness" (arXiv:2606.01435) studies contradiction resolution as a per-item current-value problem. A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2502.12110) and PlugMem (arXiv:2603.03296) supply the standard bank architectures and a utility-per-token framing. Every one of these validates its pipeline end-to-end; none asks whether its per-item signal predicts the item's realized downstream contribution, or whether that contribution is estimable at all at the evaluation budgets used.

(2) The two 2026 papers that gesture at the same suspicion. MEMAUDIT (arXiv:2605.02199) argues memory writing should be scored against a package oracle — the best budget-feasible *set* — implicitly conceding that value is combinatorial rather than per-item. GovMem (arXiv:2607.02579) shows repeated agent traces are not independent votes and that write decisions need dependency-aware support. Both assert or design around context-dependence; neither measures how much of item value is stable, neither derives the probe budget the assumption implies, and neither tests whether a curation decision taken on one episode sample transfers to a held-out one. We supply the number they assume.

(3) Per-example attribution. Datamodels (Ilyas et al., 2022) provide the randomized-subset regression estimator we adapt to injection. DemoShapley/Beta-DemoShapley (arXiv:2410.07523), influence-based in-context example selection (arXiv:2302.11042), and InfICL (arXiv:2402.11750) estimate per-demonstration value in static single-turn ICL and select on it, treating the estimate as reliable. "Helpful or Harmful Data? Fine-tuning-free Shapley Attribution" (arXiv:2406.04606) is the closest reliability critique — it studies sign robustness of instance scores under dataset resampling — but for fine-tuning data, with no probe-budget derivation and no held-out test that the resulting curation decision helps.

(4) Agent-evaluation noise. "On Randomness in Agentic Evals" (arXiv:2602.07150) measures 2.2–6.0 point pass@1 variance; "Measuring all the noises of LLM Evals" (arXiv:2512.21326) and "Assessing Macro and Micro Effects of Random Seeds" (arXiv:2503.07329) decompose aggregate and per-example variance. None decomposes the variance of a treatment effect attached to an intervention component — which is precisely the quantity every curation method silently relies on.

(5) Prompt optimization. GEPA and MIPRO treat the prompt as instructions plus demonstrations and search reflectively/evolutionarily. We use a GEPA-style reflective search over the demonstration slot as a first-class baseline, since it is the obvious way to sidestep per-item estimation entirely.
Abstract: Self-editing agent memory rests on an unexamined statistical premise: that an individual stored experience has a utility that can be estimated well enough to decide whether to keep, rewrite, or delete it. We audit that premise directly. On tool-augmented multi-hop QA with an open-weight 14B agent, we randomize which subset of a frozen memory bank is injected per episode and fit a datamodel-style regression of episode success on item-presence indicators, then run a generalizability study: a variance-components model decomposing item effects into a stable item main effect, an item-by-query interaction, and decoding noise, from which we derive the number of probe episodes per item required for a target ranking reliability. We test transfer decisively: items flagged harmful on one half of the probe episodes are pruned, and the resulting bank is evaluated on a disjoint, instance-paired held-out set against pruning an equally sized random subset — the control that isolates the value of the curation decision from the value of merely shrinking the bank. Two baselines can refute us: a faithful reimplementation of A-MAC's five-factor admission score used as the prune signal, and a GEPA-style reflective search that selects the demonstration slot at compute matched to our entire estimation phase, sidestepping per-item estimation altogether. We predict a minority stable component, split-half rank reliability below 0.35 at ~85 observations per item, a required budget above 800 observations per item for reliability 0.8, harm labels that do not transfer beyond random removal, near-zero proxy correlations, and fewer than 10% of items with a posterior credible interval excluding zero. High reliability, or transferring harm labels, would refute us and vindicate the curation literature. The whole design is one environment, one primary model, ~22,000 episodes, and under $200 of API — arithmetic given.
Experiments:
SCOPE DECISION (feasibility). One environment and one primary model carry every quantitative claim. The second model is a small directional replication. ALFWorld, WebShop, and the third model are cut, not deferred: they were costing episodes that the reliability estimates need, and the claim is stated as scoped to tool-augmented multi-hop QA with a 14B open-weight agent.

HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: ReAct scaffold, retriever (BGE embeddings over the bank), tool stack, step limit (8 model calls), temperature 0.7 with a fixed seed schedule, prompt boilerplate, and the memory bank (built once, then frozen). Only which items are injected varies.

ENVIRONMENT. Tool-augmented multi-hop QA: HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue mixed, with a Wikipedia search tool; exact-match/F1 scoring (no LLM judge on the outcome, which removes a noise source and an API cost). A 300-instance 2WikiMultiHopQA slice serves as an out-of-distribution transfer slice for the two primary prune conditions only.

MODELS. Primary: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, vLLM, TP=2, two replicas across 4×A100. Secondary replication: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. A frontier API model performs trajectory→item distillation and computes the API-side proxy scores, identically across conditions.

BANK CONSTRUCTION AND PRECHECK. Run the agent on 400 training instances; distill each episode into an ExpeL-style item (insight + condensed trajectory); dedupe to a bank of 120 items. Precheck on a 150-instance dev split: the standard top-k memory agent must differ from the no-memory agent on ≥8% of instances in either direction. If not, item valuation is vacuous; we report the precheck and stop rather than proceeding silently. (300 episodes.)

PHASE 1 — ESTIMATION BY RANDOMIZED INJECTION (3,600 episodes). On a probe set disjoint from test, each episode injects a random subset of k items drawn uniformly from the retriever's top-m=20 candidates, k~U{1..6}. This yields ~85 appearances per item on average across 3,000 probe episodes; items with fewer than 40 appearances are excluded from the reliability analysis and their coverage is reported. A 600-episode subsample is replicated under a second decoding seed to separate seed noise from item-by-query interaction. Estimators: (a) ridge-regularized logistic regression of success on presence indicators plus an injected-token-count regressor and a query random intercept (datamodel-style); (b) matched-pair leave-one-out contrast on episode pairs differing in exactly one item, as an agreement check that the regression is not an estimator artifact. Both are computed from the same episodes; no extra rollouts.

PHASE 2 — GENERALIZABILITY STUDY (no new episodes). Hierarchical model on episode-level binary outcomes with random effects for item, query, item×query, and seed. Report the share of explainable variance carried by the stable item main effect; use the generalizability-coefficient formula to compute probe episodes per item required for ranking reliability 0.7 and 0.8; compare to what published curation pipelines spend (one to a few observations per item). Report empirical split-half reliability: fit item effects on two disjoint halves, Spearman–Brown-corrected rank correlation, plus sign-agreement on the items each half calls harmful. Report the count and fraction of items whose 95% posterior credible interval excludes zero — this is a high-power estimation claim and is the paper's central number.

PHASE 3 — TRANSFER TEST (the decisive experiment; 8,800 episodes). 800 held-out instances, fully paired, retrieval and deployment k fixed.
Primary conditions (carry the main claim):
 P0 Full bank, no pruning.
 P1 Aggressive prune: remove bottom-decile items by split-A estimated effect (12 items).
 P2 Random prune: remove 12 items at random, 3 independent draws, all 800 instances each.
 P4 Shrinkage prune (ours): remove only items whose 95% posterior CI lies below zero.
 P9 Budget baseline at matched compute: no pruning; k tuned on a dev split using episodes drawn from the same budget the estimation phase consumed.
Refutation conditions (each could overturn us):
 P3 Ceiling: prune bottom decile estimated on the FULL probe set (splits A+B, still not test) — bounds how much any item-level pruning can buy at our best estimate.
 P5 A-MAC faithful: prune bottom 12 by a reimplementation of A-MAC's five-factor admission score (future utility, factual confidence, semantic novelty, recency, content-type prior), reproduced from the paper.
 P6 Verify/judge family: prune bottom 12 by LLM-judge quality score combined with an EDV-style verification replay outcome.
 P10 GEPA-style optimizer selection: reflective evolutionary search directly over which items occupy the demonstration slot, given an episode budget matched to Phase 1 (3,600 search episodes), evaluated once on the same held-out set.
 Null replicate: P0 re-run under a different seed schedule (800 episodes).
Headline comparisons: P1 vs P2 (does identified harm transfer?), P3 vs P0 (ceiling), P9 vs the best pruning condition (does budget control dominate curation at matched compute?), P10 vs P1/P4 (does optimizer-driven selection sidestep the estimation problem?), P5/P6 vs P2 (do published signals beat random removal?).
OOD slice: P0, P1, P2(1 draw), P9 on 300 2WikiMultiHopQA instances (1,200 episodes) — directional only.

PHASE 4 — PROXY VALIDITY (nearly free; scoring only, no rollouts). Correlate against the shrunken item posterior: A-MAC five-factor score and each factor separately, LLM-judge quality, EDV verification pass/fail, pairwise contradiction flag, SAGE-style novelty score, GovMem-style correlated-support count, retrieval frequency, item length, item abstractness. Report Spearman with bootstrap CIs and each proxy's AUC for identifying items whose posterior CI excludes zero on the negative side. Only two proxies get a paid prune condition (P5, P6) because prune conditions cost 800 episodes each and correlations cost none — the transfer test spends episodes only where a condition can change the verdict.

SECONDARY MODEL REPLICATION (Llama-3.1-8B; 3,100 episodes). Phase 1 at reduced budget (1,500 probe episodes), Phase 2 reliability statistics, and P0/P1/P2(1 draw)/P4 on a 400-instance test set. Directional only; MDE ~7 points, stated as such.

COMPUTE ARITHMETIC. Primary model episode count: 400 (bank) + 300 (precheck) + 3,600 (Phase 1) + 1,000 (P9 k-tuning dev) + 3,600 (P10 search) + 8,800 (transfer) + 800 (null replicate) + 1,200 (OOD) = 19,700. Secondary model: 3,100. Total ≈ 22,800 episodes. Each episode is ≤8 model calls, ~900 generated tokens plus ~12k prefill. Qwen2.5-14B on 2×A100 (TP=2) at high concurrency generates ≥1,500 tok/s per replica; two replicas give ≥3,000 tok/s, i.e. ≥3 episodes/s. Discounting 3× for tool latency, retries, and scheduling: ~4,000 episodes/hour → ~5 GPU-hours of pure inference for the primary model, ~1 hour for the 8B secondary. Budgeting 3× again for development runs, one full re-run, and the seed-replicate passes: under 3 days wall-clock on the single node. API: 400 distillation calls + ~120 items × 3 API-side proxy scores + ~60 GEPA reflection calls with long contexts ≈ $120, hard cap $200. Outcome scoring is exact-match/F1, so no judging spend.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) P1 beating P2 by more than the noise floor: harm labels transfer, and item-level curation is on solid ground.
(ii) P5 (faithful A-MAC five-factor admission score) beating P2 substantially: the specific published admission signal carries real information even if our per-item effects are noisy. This is the reviewer-requested faithful stand-in for the admission-control family, not a strawman proxy.
(iii) P6 (judge + EDV verification) beating P2: the verify-before-write family is vindicated.
(iv) P10 (GEPA-style reflective selection of the demonstration slot at matched compute) beating every estimation-based condition: optimizer-driven selection sidesteps per-item value estimation, which would leave our reliability finding intact but overturn the constructive corollary. This is the baseline the track's own theme demands and the one we consider most likely to be competitive with P9.
(v) P9 (tune k, no curation) losing to a pruning condition: our recommendation is wrong.
(vi) The matched-pair LOO contrast disagreeing sharply with the randomized-injection regression: an estimator artifact rather than an item-value phenomenon.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM.
P2 (random prune, matched removal count, 3 draws) is the essential control: it holds bank size and injected-token statistics fixed and removes only the identification signal, so P1−P2 is exactly the value of the curation decision.
P3 (estimate on the full probe set) bounds the ceiling, so a null on P1 cannot be dismissed as "you needed a better estimator".
The second-seed replicate subsample separates decoding noise from item×query interaction inside the variance decomposition, so low reliability cannot be attributed solely to temperature.
The injected-token regressor separates per-item content effects from injection volume, so item value is not confounded with prompt length.
A shuffled-item placebo (presence indicators permuted before fitting) gives the null distribution of apparent item effects and of split-half reliability under true no-signal; any reliability estimate must exceed its 95th percentile to be read as nonzero.
Coverage ablation: reliability recomputed on the subset of items with ≥60 appearances, to show the finding is not driven by thinly-observed items.
Falsifiable Predictions:
Pre-registered, with the primary set restricted to quantities our sample size can resolve.

PRIMARY (well-powered):
P-1. The stable item main effect accounts for under 20% of explainable outcome variance; item×query interaction is the largest component.
P-2. Split-half rank reliability of item effects at ~85 observations per item is below 0.35 (Spearman–Brown corrected) and above the placebo 95th percentile; the generalizability formula implies >800 observations per item for reliability 0.8 — one to two orders of magnitude above what A-MAC, SAGE, EDV, AutoManual, or Memory-R1 spend per item.
P-3. Fewer than 10% of items have a 95% posterior credible interval excluding zero. This is the sharpest single number in the paper and does not depend on the transfer test's power.
P-4. P1 − P2 on the held-out set lies within ±4 points with a CI covering zero: pruning "identified harmful" items is not distinguishable from removing the same number at random.
P-5. Every proxy — including the faithful A-MAC composite — has |Spearman| below 0.25 against the shrunken item posterior and AUC below 0.65 for identifying reliably-negative items.
P-6. P9 (k tuning at matched compute) is at least as good as the best pruning condition (P1, P3, P4, P5, P6), i.e. no pruning condition beats it by more than 4 points.

SECONDARY (direction pre-registered, explicitly underpowered):
P-7. P4 (shrinkage prune) removes at most 15% of the aggressive set and is directionally above P2. Because P-3 predicts few items clear the bar, P4 may remove <8 items; if so we report P4 descriptively and make no positive accuracy claim rather than reading noise as a win.
P-8. P10 (GEPA-style selection) is competitive with P9 and above P1, indicating that search over packages beats estimation of item main effects.

REFUTATION CONDITIONS. Split-half reliability above 0.6, or P1 beating P2 by more than 4 points, refutes the central claim: per-item utility is estimable and actionable at ordinary budgets. Any proxy reaching Spearman above 0.4 with the stable item value refutes the proxy-validity claim for that curation family specifically, and we report it as validation of that family. If P9 loses to a pruning condition by more than 4 points, the constructive corollary is wrong. If P4 also fails to separate from P2 while P-3 holds, the result is stronger than predicted — item-level curation is futile at any budget available to a practitioner — and the recommendation hardens to "manage the injection budget, do not curate items".
Measurement and Noise Control:
Three noise sources handled separately.

(a) EVALUATION NOISE on the transfer test. Every held-out instance is run under every condition with the same seed schedule, so all comparisons are within-instance. Primary test: exact McNemar on fix/break counts, Holm-corrected across the condition family. Every delta is reported with its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention. P2 is averaged over 3 draws and its across-draw spread is the reference band.

(b) ESTIMATION NOISE on item effects. Quantified by the split-half design and by the shuffled-item placebo, which gives the reliability distribution under no true signal; reliability is read as nonzero only above the placebo 95th percentile. Posterior intervals come from the hierarchical model with a 10k-resample episode-level bootstrap; bootstrap CIs are also reported on the variance components and on the derived probe-budget numbers.

(c) NULL REPLICATES. P0 is re-run under a different seed schedule on the same 800 instances; no effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of the apparent-delta distribution from that replicate. This is load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets.

MINIMUM DETECTABLE EFFECTS, stated before running. With 800 paired instances and an expected 12–18% discordant-pair rate (~120 discordant pairs), McNemar detects a net swing of ~3.8 points at 80% power, α=0.05. Hence P-4 and P-6 are stated with a ±4-point null band and differences between roughly 2 and 4 points are declared inconclusive in advance; we will not narrate a 3-point difference as a win or a loss. The OOD slice (300 instances) and the 8B replication (400 instances) have MDEs of ~6–7 points and are labeled directional. With 120 items, split-half rank correlations carry a 95% CI of roughly ±0.17, so the design distinguishes 0.35 from 0.6 (the refutation threshold) but not 0.35 from 0.45; proxy correlations carry the same width and proxy differences below 0.2 will not be interpreted. Prediction P-3 is the highest-powered claim: with ~85 binary observations per item, the per-item detectable effect is large (~±20 points), so the fraction of items clearing a 95% CI bar is estimated tightly and is exactly the quantity that indicts one-to-few-observation curation.
Preprint Collision Check:
Grounded in the search just run (14 targeted queries; a second round was blocked by a tool limit, so this is a single-pass search and I say so plainly).

CLOSEST: MEMAUDIT (arXiv:2605.02199, 2026). It argues memory writing should be evaluated against a "package oracle" — the best budget-feasible *set* of items — explicitly separating write quality from retrieval and reader effects. This is the nearest thing in the literature to our premise that value is combinatorial rather than per-item, and it is the paper most likely to be read as scooping us. It does not collide. MEMAUDIT *assumes* package-level value and builds an evaluation protocol on that assumption; it never measures how much of item value is a stable item main effect versus item×query interaction, never derives the probe budget the per-item assumption requires, never tests whether an item-level curation decision taken on one sample transfers to a held-out sample, and never audits any published curation signal for validity. We supply the measurement that MEMAUDIT presupposes, and if our P-1 holds it is the empirical justification for MEMAUDIT's design choice. We will cite it as the strongest independent motivation for the study and position against it explicitly.

SECOND CLOSEST: GovMem (arXiv:2607.02579, 2026), "repeated agent observations are not independent votes", reframing writing as evidence governance. That is a claim about the dependence structure of *write-time evidence*; ours is about the variance structure of *realized downstream utility*. No collision, and we absorb its idea as a Phase-4 proxy (correlated-support count) — if GovMem's signal predicts stable item value where A-MAC's does not, that is a publishable win for GovMem that our design will surface.

DIRECT TARGETS, NOT COLLISIONS: A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549) is the exemplar of the audited premise — its five-factor per-item value decomposition is reimplemented faithfully as P5 and correlated factor-by-factor in Phase 4. SAGE (arXiv:2605.30711) supplies the novelty-gate proxy. "Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness" (arXiv:2606.01435) supplies the contradiction proxy. Memory-R1 (arXiv:2508.19828) trains per-item edit actions and would be refuted-or-vindicated by our reliability numbers but is too expensive to reimplement here; we treat it in discussion only. A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025) and PlugMem (arXiv:2603.03296) are architecture baselines. AutoManual (NeurIPS 2024) and EDV (arXiv:2606.24428) fold into P6. The 2026 agent-memory survey (arXiv:2603.07670) lists write-path filtering and contradiction handling as open engineering problems, which is consistent with no existing audit.

OTHER CLUSTERS: "Helpful or Harmful Data?" (arXiv:2406.04606) is the closest reliability critique in spirit but concerns fine-tuning data attribution, with no probe-budget derivation and no curation-transfer test. DemoShapley (arXiv:2410.07523) and influence-based ICL selection (arXiv:2302.11042) assume reliability rather than measuring it, in static single-turn ICL. The agent-eval noise papers (arXiv:2602.07150, arXiv:2512.21326, arXiv:2503.07329) decompose aggregate or per-example variance, never the variance of an intervention component's effect.

HONEST RESIDUAL RISK. The single-pass search did not cover "generalizability theory applied to LLM evaluation" or an OpenReview 2026 sweep. The specific scenario that would gut our P1-vs-P2 headline is a random-removal control appearing as an appendix ablation in a recent curation preprint. None of the nine retrieved papers contains one, but I cannot rule it out. Even in that case, the variance decomposition, the derived probe budget, the credible-interval prune criterion, and the cross-proxy validity sweep remain unclaimed by anything found.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
(1) Scope. One environment (tool-augmented multi-hop QA), one primary model. ALFWorld and WebShop were cut to make the reliability estimates adequately powered; the honest consequence is that we cannot say whether procedural items in embodied environments are more universal than QA insights. We state the claim as scoped and flag environment moderation as the first follow-up, rather than pretending a 250-instance ALFWorld arm would have settled it.
(2) The bank may have no measurable item-level effects at all, making everything trivially null. The precheck (≥8% instance-level disagreement vs no-memory) and the P3 ceiling condition detect this; we report the precheck numbers either way.
(3) Randomized injection deviates from deployment retrieval, so estimated effects are marginal over a slightly different injection distribution. We mitigate by drawing only from the retriever's top-20 and by reporting the matched-pair LOO estimator as an agreement check, but extrapolation to strict top-k deployment is an assumption we state rather than prove.
(4) A low-reliability finding could reflect a weak estimator rather than an unstable underlying quantity. P3 and the placebo permutation bound this from both sides, but with our budget we can only show reliability is low at achievable budgets, not that the item main effect is truly zero. The paper's claim is deliberately the former — which is also exactly the claim that matters for practitioners running one-to-few observations per item.
(5) Variance components from binary outcomes with ~85 observations per item are themselves noisy; we report bootstrap CIs on the generalizability coefficient and treat the probe-budget result as an order-of-magnitude statement.
(6) Reimplemented proxies (A-MAC, judge, EDV verifier, contradiction detector, SAGE gate) may be weaker than their published versions. Each is tuned on a dev split until it reproduces its published direction of effect on end-to-end accuracy before entering the validity analysis, and both numbers are reported. A proxy that fails to reproduce its published direction is reported as not-reproduced and excluded from the refutation set.
(7) The payload is largely a qualifying negative about a fast-growing literature, so its value rests entirely on measurement strength — which is why the placebo permutation, null replicate, matched-compute baselines (P9, P10), and pre-stated MDEs are load-bearing and non-negotiable in the budget.

Name: memory_or_instruction
