Title: Is Your Agent's Memory Just an Un-Optimized Prompt? Measuring the Residual Value of Retrieved Experience After Instruction Optimization
Short Hypothesis: Published agentic-memory gains are measured against a hand-written instruction. We hypothesize that for procedural experience memory (ExpeL/ReasoningBank-style), most of that gain is *substitutable*: when a reflective prompt optimizer is given exactly the same training episodes that built the memory bank, the memory-vs-no-memory gap collapses by at least 60%, and a frozen instruction compiled offline from the whole bank — with no retrieval at inference — matches per-instance top-k retrieval at matched injected tokens. The residual, non-substitutable value of memory is concentrated in instances with genuinely instance-specific reusable content, which we verify with a deliberately non-compilable positive-control bank where substitution must fail.
Related Work:
**(1) Procedural experience memory.** ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144) "autonomously gathers experiences and extracts knowledge using natural language from a collection of training tasks" and at inference "recalls its extracted insights and past experiences." ReasoningBank (OpenReview jL7fwchScm, 2025) "distills generalizable reasoning strategies from an agent's self-judged successful and failed experiences." Mem^p (arXiv 2508.06433), A-Mem (arXiv 2502.12110), and "Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience" (arXiv 2603.18272) follow the same evaluation template: the memory-vs-no-memory delta is measured at a *fixed, hand-written* scaffold prompt, or against fine-tuning. That comparison silently assumes memory and instruction are non-substitutable containers.

**(2) Reflective prompt optimizers.** GEPA (arXiv 2507.19457, ICLR 2026 Oral) "samples trajectories and reflects on them to propose prompt updates," outperforming MIPROv2 by >10pp and GRPO by 6pp with up to 35× fewer rollouts. GEPA and ExpeL run the *same* learning principle — reflect on trajectories, distill natural-language lessons — and differ only in where the lesson is stored: folded into the instruction versus held in a retrieved store. No published work uses one as the control for the other.

**(3) The emerging "memory evaluation is confounded" literature.** MemDelta (arXiv 2606.29914) is the nearest work: it shows Mem0's 72.7 vs 61.4 win over verbatim RAG on LongMemEval-S reverses to a 1.2-point loss when only the embedding model is changed, and concludes that uncontrolled comparisons "conflate architectural memory with retrieval engineering, embedding quality, model-specific long-context behavior, and compute budget." "Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks" (arXiv 2603.02473) finds most memory failures stem from irrelevant retrieval rather than construction. Memory-R2 (arXiv 2605.21768) addresses an analogous fairness confound in RL credit assignment. All of these audit confounds *inside* the memory pipeline (retrieval quality, embeddings, credit assignment) while taking for granted that memory is the only container in which the training-episode information could have been placed.

**(4) Three-way comparisons in the wild.** EvoClinician (arXiv 2601.22964) is the only retrieved paper that lists "prompt optimization agent" as a baseline category alongside "memory agent," with memory baselines defined as those that "keep the prompt fixed but add long-term memory across episodes." It is a clinical application paper; the three-way comparison is a baseline table, not a hypothesis, and it does not equalize training episodes, match injected tokens, compile a bank into an instruction, or measure residual gain.

**Our position.** The missing accounting is: a memory bank and an optimized instruction are two containers for the same training-episode information, and the field has never measured how much of the first container's value survives when the second is filled first, at matched information and matched cost. MemDelta establishes that the memory literature's baselines are confounded; it does not identify instruction optimization as a competing mechanism, and it makes no prediction that retrieval can be replaced by a frozen compiled prompt. That prediction is ours and it is the risky part.
Abstract: Agentic memory systems are evaluated by comparing an agent with a retrieved-experience bank against the same agent without one, holding a hand-written scaffold prompt fixed. Recent audits (MemDelta) show such comparisons are confounded by retrieval engineering; we identify a different and sharper confound. A memory bank distilled from training episodes and an instruction optimized on those *same* episodes are two containers for the same information, and the second is dramatically cheaper to serve — one prompt paid once, versus retrieved tokens paid every episode. We test substitution directly. Holding the agent, tools, retriever, training split and evaluation fixed, we build (i) an ExpeL-style bank with per-instance top-k retrieval, (ii) an instruction optimized by GEPA that never sees the bank, and (iii) a frozen instruction compiled offline from the whole bank with no retrieval at all, token-matched per instance to (i). The primary endpoint is the substitution ratio S: the fraction of memory's paired gain over no-memory at the hand-written instruction that disappears at the optimized instruction. We predict S ≥ 0.6 on a tool-augmented multi-hop QA agent and ≥ 0.7 on ALFWorld, and we predict the compiled static arm comes within 2 points of live retrieval. A deliberately non-compilable positive-control bank, seeded with near-duplicates of held-out instances, must show S < 0.25 — so a null on the main benchmarks is a finding rather than a power failure. The study is scoped to one primary environment (n=600 paired instances, 3 optimizer seeds), one replication environment, and ~30,000 evaluation episodes, with instance-paired McNemar tests, crossed random effects for optimizer seed, null replicates, and a stated minimum detectable effect.
Experiments:
**HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT.** Agent scaffold (ReAct), tool stack, step limit, retriever and similarity function, decoding temperature and seed schedule, the training split from which *all* learned artifacts derive, and the held-out test split. Only the instruction and the memory-injection variant differ. The fairness constraint that makes the study interpretable: the memory bank and the prompt optimizer see exactly the same training episodes, so they differ only in the container, not in the information they were allowed to see.

**MODEL.** Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct is the single load-bearing agent, served with vLLM (two TP=2 replicas on the 4×A100 node). Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct runs a reduced moderation check only. Qwen3-32B is **cut**. A frontier API model is the GEPA reflector, the ExpeL distiller, and the offline compiler, used identically across conditions. Scoring is programmatic (normalized EM/F1 for QA, ALFWorld task success), so no LLM judge is on the critical path.

**ENVIRONMENTS.** *E1 (primary, carries all quantitative claims):* tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a Wikipedia search tool, test pool = 600 held-out instances (360 HotpotQA-distractor, 240 MuSiQue), ~6 LLM calls/episode. *E2 (replication):* ALFWorld, all 274 eval tasks (134 unseen reported separately), ~25 calls/episode; chosen because task templates recur across train and test, so procedural memory is maximally compilable and the substitution prediction is at its most exposed. **WebShop is cut. The LoCoMo episodic-memory control is cut.**

**ARTIFACTS (built once, then frozen).**
- **B**: ExpeL-style bank over 500 E1 / 200 E2 training episodes — distilled insights plus condensed trajectories; deployed with top-k=7 dense retrieval.
- **I1**: GEPA run on the same training split with **no** memory in context, 300 rollouts per run, 3 seeds (E1) / 2 seeds (E2).
- **I3**: hand-written instruction padded with task-generic boilerplate to I1's token length (length control).
- **C**: frontier model reads the entire bank offline and compiles it into one static instruction block, token-matched per instance to what top-k=7 injects; no retrieval at inference. A frozen measurement instrument, not a proposed method.
- **R**: raw few-shot arm (**new, per review**): the same retrieval over the *undistilled* training trajectories, injected verbatim as demonstrations, token-matched to M1. This separates "value of ExpeL-style distillation" from "value of any exposure to training episodes."
- **I2 (optimize-with-memory-in-context) is cut**: it tests co-adaptation, not substitution, and does not carry the claim.

**PRECHECK GATE.** On a 150-instance dev split, the bank must produce a paired gain over no-memory at the hand-written instruction of **≥10 accuracy points** (a size routinely reported by ExpeL/ReasoningBank-class systems). S is undefined when the denominator is small; a bank that fails is enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes, and the precheck numbers are reported either way. The gate is set at 10 rather than 8 because with 3 optimizer seeds the design detects a ~5.6-point change in the memory gain (see Measurement), so the predicted drop must be ≥6 points to be testable.

**E1 CONDITION GRID — 7 cells, fully instance-paired.**
| # | Cell | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | I0×M0 | no-memory baseline |
| 2 | I0×M1 | the standard memory-paper comparison (denominator of S) |
| 3 | I0×M2 | compiled static, token-matched — does retrieval buy anything? |
| 4 | I0×M3 (raw few-shot R) | distillation vs. raw exemplars |
| 5 | I1×M0 | optimized instruction alone |
| 6 | I1×M1 | numerator of S: what memory adds on top |
| 7 | I3×M0 | length control |

**PRIMARY ENDPOINT.** S = 1 − [acc(I1×M1) − acc(I1×M0)] / [acc(I0×M1) − acc(I0×M0)], computed per optimizer seed, reported as a distribution with a cluster-bootstrap CI. Every cell also reports its paired fix/break decomposition against I0×M0.

**SECONDARY ENDPOINTS.** (a) *Compilation sufficiency*: I0×M2 vs I0×M1 at matched injected tokens. (b) *Distillation value*: I0×M1 vs I0×M3. (c) *Residual complementarity*: I1×M1 vs max(I1×M0, I0×M1). (d) *Optimizer generality*: MIPROv2 substituted for GEPA, 2 seeds, cells I1'×M0 and I1'×M1 only, on a fixed 300-instance subsample, 1 decoding seed.

**POSITIVE CONTROL (load-bearing).** A second bank **B-dup** seeded with distilled trajectories for training instances that are deliberately near-duplicates of specific held-out test instances (paraphrased test questions, disjoint from the instances used for optimization). Its value is instance-specific and provably cannot be compressed into a bounded static instruction. Cells on a 300-instance subset: I0×M1dup, I0×M2dup, I1×M1dup (reusing the already-built I1 instructions — no new optimizer runs needed, since I1 never sees any bank). I0×M0 and I1×M0 are read off the main grid.

**ISO-COST CURVE (shrunk to 3 points).** Instrument every LLM call. Held-out accuracy (n=300, 1 decoding seed) versus total *training-time* call budget at three points spanning ~250 / ~900 / ~2500 calls, for two strategies: grow the bank (more distilled training episodes, retrieval fixed) vs. run more GEPA rollouts with no memory. 2 seeds per point; the top point of each curve is the existing I0×M1 and I1×M0 cells. Report the crossover budget and the *inference-time* cost per episode, since retrieval is paid every episode and an instruction is paid once.

**MODERATOR ANALYSIS (free — reuses existing runs).** For each test instance, compute max similarity to any bank item (dense score plus an LLM label "does this item contain instance-specific reusable content", human-validated on 100 cases with reported κ). Fit per-instance residual memory gain at I1 against this similarity.

**8B MODERATION CHECK.** Cells 1, 2, 5, 6 only, n=300, 1 decoding seed, 2 optimizer seeds, on Llama-3.1-8B. Tests risk factor (4): a small model may fail to follow a long optimized instruction while still using concrete exemplars, which would lower S at 8B.

**E2 (ALFWorld) CELLS.** I0×M0, I0×M1, I0×M2, I1×M0, I1×M1; 2 optimizer seeds; 2 decoding seeds for the two I0 cells (to supply the null replicate), 1 elsewhere.

**COMPUTE ARITHMETIC (the reason this fits).**
E1, Qwen-14B: fixed-instruction cells 1,2,3,4,7 = 5 × 600 × 2 decoding seeds = 6,000 episodes; optimizer-dependent cells 5,6 = 2 × 3 seeds × 600 × 2 = 7,200; MIPROv2 check = 2 × 2 × 300 = 1,200; positive control = 3,000; GEPA/MIPRO search rollouts = 3×300 + 2×300 = 1,500; bank + B-dup construction = 800; iso-cost eval = 3,000, iso-cost training = 800. **E1 total ≈ 23,500 episodes × ~6 calls ≈ 141k LLM calls.**
E2, ALFWorld: eval = 2×274×2 + 274 + 2×2×274 = 2,466; optimizer rollouts = 2×200 = 400; bank = 200. **E2 total ≈ 3,066 episodes × ~25 calls ≈ 77k calls.**
8B moderation: 1,800 eval + 600 rollouts = 2,400 episodes ≈ 14k calls (on the cheaper model).
**Grand total ≈ 29,000 episodes / ~230k LLM calls.** At vLLM aggregate throughput on 4×A100 (two TP=2 replicas, high concurrency), this is ~3–4 days of wall clock, i.e. "days, not weeks," and ≤ 6,000 episodes per reported configuration.
**API budget:** ~9 optimizer runs × ~60 reflection calls (~8k in / 1k out) ≈ 4.5M input / 0.6M output ≈ $12; distillation of 900 training episodes ≈ $8; compiler and moderator labeling ≈ $10. **Total ≈ $30–60**, far under the few-hundred-dollar cap, because scoring is programmatic.
**Ordered contingency cuts if we overrun:** iso-cost curve → 2 points; 8B moderation arm; MIPROv2 generality check; E2 decoding-seed replicate. The 7-cell E1 grid and the positive control are never cut — they are the claim.
Baselines and Ablations:
**BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.**
(i) **I1×M1 retaining the full I0 memory gain** (S ≈ 0) — the complementarity outcome, and the most likely way the hypothesis dies. We would report that memory and instruction optimization contribute independently and that the memory literature's fixed-prompt comparison is unbiased.
(ii) **I0×M1 ≫ I0×M2** on the main benchmarks — per-instance retrieval carrying value no static compilation can hold, which would kill the "compile, don't retrieve" recommendation even if S is high.
(iii) **I0×M3 (raw few-shot) ≈ I0×M1** — added at reviewer request. If undistilled retrieved trajectories match the ExpeL bank, then the "memory system" is a demonstration selector and any I1 advantage is about instruction content, not about beating distillation. This baseline separates "value of distillation" from "value of any exposure to training episodes at all," and is a genuine threat to the framing.
(iv) **Memory growth dominating optimization at every iso-cost budget** — makes the practical payload negative.

**ABLATIONS THAT ISOLATE THE MECHANISM.**
- **I3, length-padded hand-written instruction** — holds prompt length fixed and removes only the optimized *content*, exposing any I1 advantage that is mere verbosity. Essential.
- **Equal-training-episode constraint** — without it, a shrinking memory gain could just mean the optimizer saw more data. Essential.
- **Token-matching of C and R to M1** — a compiled-arm tie cannot be dismissed as a budget difference.
- **Non-compilable positive-control bank (B-dup)** — establishes that the design *can* detect non-substitutable memory value. This is what converts a null into a finding.
- **Second optimizer (MIPROv2)** — the substitution result must not be an artifact of GEPA's search procedure.
- **Shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check** — confirms retrieval is functioning in M1.
Falsifiable Predictions:
1. **S ≥ 0.6 on E1 and ≥ 0.7 on E2**: memory's paired gain over no-memory falls from ≥10 points at the hand-written instruction to <4 points at the optimized instruction, consistent in direction across all 3 optimizer seeds, with the bootstrap CI on S excluding 0.3.
2. **I3 recovers <20% of I1's improvement over I0** — the effect is optimized content, not prompt length.
3. **I0×M2 (frozen compiled instruction, no retrieval) comes within 2 points of I0×M1 at matched injected tokens** on both E1 and E2. This is the risky, non-obvious prediction: per-instance retrieval of procedural experience is nearly worthless once the same experience is compiled once, offline.
4. **On the near-duplicate positive control, S < 0.25 and I0×M2dup loses to I0×M1dup by ≥5 points** — the instrument detects non-substitutable value where it truly exists.
5. **Residual memory gain at I1 is concentrated in the top decile of instance-to-bank similarity**, with the bottom 70% of instances showing a residual gain whose CI covers zero.
6. **Iso-cost:** instruction optimization reaches the accuracy of the full memory system at ≤ half the training-time LLM-call budget, and at strictly lower per-episode inference cost.
7. **Distillation is not the load-bearing part:** I0×M1 exceeds I0×M3 by <3 points, i.e. the ExpeL write path buys little over raw retrieved trajectories at matched tokens.

**REFUTATION.** S < 0.3 on both E1 and E2 with CIs excluding 0.6 kills the substitution claim and vindicates the memory literature's fixed-prompt comparison; we report that as the primary result. If the positive control *also* shows high substitution, the measurement is broken rather than the hypothesis confirmed, and the study is reported as uninterpretable. If I0×M2 loses badly to I0×M1 everywhere, memory's value is genuinely per-instance and prediction 3 is wrong even if S is high — we report the two predictions separately and do not let one carry the other.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Three variance sources handled separately.

**(a) Evaluation variance.** Every held-out instance is run under every cell with the same seed schedule, so all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar tests on fix/break counts with Holm correction across the cell family. Every reported delta carries its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention.

**(b) Optimizer variance — the source most often ignored.** 3 independent GEPA seeds on E1, 2 on E2. Cell comparisons use a mixed-effects logistic model with test instance and optimizer run as crossed random effects; CIs come from a cluster bootstrap resampling optimizer runs as well as instances. S is computed per optimizer seed and reported as a distribution, never as a single number.

**(c) Null replicates.** For each environment we re-run an identical cell under a different decoding seed and report the distribution of apparent deltas, and separately compare two optimizer seeds of the same condition to each other. No effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of the corresponding null distribution. This is load-bearing given prior observations of 5–14 point re-scoring drift on small held-out sets and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.

**Minimum detectable effect.** E1, n=600 paired instances, expected 12–18% discordant-pair rate: McNemar detects a ~4-point net swing at 80% power (α=0.05) for any single cell pair. S is a ratio of two paired differences; the numerator is averaged over 3 optimizer seeds, so its standard error is √(1.4² + 2.5²/3) ≈ 2.0 points (using a 2–3 point between-run SD estimated from the null optimizer replicates), giving ~5.6 points of detectable change in the memory gain. This is exactly why the precheck gate is 10 points (not 8) and why prediction 1 is framed as "from ≥10 down to <4": the predicted drop of ≥6 points sits above the MDE. E2 (n=274, MDE ~6 points) is directional replication; the 8B arm and iso-cost curve (n=300, MDE ~6 points) likewise. Sub-MDE differences are reported as inconclusive in either direction, and we will not compute S in any environment that fails the precheck.
Preprint Collision Check:
**Closest work found in the current search: MemDelta — "Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation" (arXiv 2606.29914, 2026).** It is a measurement paper making the same *genus* of argument: that headline agent-memory gains are artifacts of uncontrolled baselines. It shows Mem0's apparent 72.7-vs-61.4 win over verbatim RAG on LongMemEval-S reverses to a 1.2-point loss when only the embedding model changes, and warns that comparisons "conflate architectural memory with retrieval engineering, embedding quality, model-specific long-context behavior, and compute budget." **Partial collision on framing, none on claim.** MemDelta's confound is *inside* the retrieval pipeline; ours is a rival mechanism outside it. MemDelta does not run a prompt optimizer, does not equalize training episodes across containers, does not compile a bank into a frozen instruction, does not report a residual-gain ratio, and makes no prediction that retrieval can be deleted. We will cite it as the direct methodological precedent and state plainly that our contribution is the *specific* substitution mechanism plus the compilation prediction, not the general "memory baselines are confounded" thesis, which is now MemDelta's.

**EvoClinician (arXiv 2601.22964, 2026)** is the only retrieved paper that puts "prompt optimization agent" and "memory agent" in the same baseline table, defining memory baselines as those that "keep the prompt fixed but add long-term memory across episodes." This shows the three-way comparison is beginning to appear as a design pattern. It does not collide: it is a clinical application paper (a domain this track excludes), the comparison is a baseline table rather than a hypothesis, and it does not match training episodes, match injected tokens, or measure a residual.

**GEPA (arXiv 2507.19457)** is our optimizer, not a competitor; it has not been used as a control to isolate memory's residual value. **ExpeL (2308.10144), ReasoningBank (OpenReview jL7fwchScm), Mem^p (2508.06433), A-Mem (2502.12110), and arXiv 2603.18272** are the targets of the hypothesis and all evaluate against no-memory or fine-tuning, not against an optimized instruction. **Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks (2603.02473)** and **Memory-R2 (2605.21768)** audit different confounds (retrieval relevance, RL credit assignment) and take memory's baseline value for granted.

**Correction to the previous version of this check.** The earlier draft cited ActMem (2603.00026), MAS-PromptBench (2606.23664), TERMS-Bench (2605.13909), MemAPO (2603.21520), and "Evaluating Memory Structure in LLM Agents" (2602.11243). **None of these were returned by the current literature search and I cannot verify them; I have removed all reliance on them and do not use them to establish novelty.** One reviewer flagged TERMS-Bench (a GEPA-based substitution test for an architectural intervention in negotiation agents) as the closest structural precedent. If that work exists as described, it is a precedent for the *logical move* — use a prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention — in a different domain, and I would cite it as such; our contribution would then rest on the memory-specific measurement object (the substitution ratio with a matched-information constraint), the compiled-static instrument, the non-compilable positive control, and the iso-cost accounting, none of which transfer automatically.

**Residual risk.** I could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions, and a "memory + prompt optimizer" ablation may exist in an appendix of a combined-system preprint. Given MemDelta's existence, the confound-auditing framing is no longer novel on its own; we therefore lead with the mechanism claim (instruction optimization substitutes for procedural memory; frozen compilation replaces retrieval) rather than with the methodology.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Precheck failure.** If a bank does not clear the 10-point gate, S is unstable and we report that environment as excluded with its numbers rather than dividing by a small denominator. Given MemDelta's findings, a bank failing the gate is itself a reportable observation about the literature.
2. **Optimizer failure.** GEPA may not beat the hand-written instruction on some environment, collapsing the study to "no optimization, no substitution." Mitigated by the MIPROv2 arm and by reporting I1-vs-I0 as a prerequisite result.
3. **Lossy compilation.** The compiled arm depends on the compiler prompt, which we fix in advance on a 100-instance dev split, report verbatim, and treat as a *lower bound* on what static compilation can achieve. A tie with retrieval is therefore conservative; a loss is weaker evidence against prediction 3 than a tie is for it.
4. **Model specificity.** S may be lower at 8B (small models may follow long instructions poorly while still using concrete exemplars) — reported per model, never pooled. With one load-bearing model, generality is a stated limitation, not a claim.
5. **Artificiality of the positive control.** The near-duplicate bank is synthetic; the external episodic-memory control (LoCoMo) was cut for budget, so the only evidence that the instrument detects non-substitutable value is the synthetic one. We state this explicitly rather than hiding it.
6. **Statistical reach.** With 3 optimizer seeds and n=600, the design detects a ~5.6-point change in the memory gain. It cannot resolve S to better than roughly ±0.2 and it cannot adjudicate small complementarities; E2, the 8B arm, and the iso-cost curve are directional only. We will not report sub-MDE differences as results.
7. **Iso-cost indicativeness.** The curve depends on implementation efficiency of both pipelines; we report raw call counts, token counts and wall clock so readers can re-weight.
8. **Scope of the claim.** This is about *procedural* experience memory in agent benchmarks with recurring task structure. It says nothing about episodic personal memory or long-conversation memory, and we will not generalize to them.

Name: memory_vetoes_instruction_slot
Title: The Instruction Slot Is Not Independent of the Memory Slot: Answer-Bearing Experience Suppresses Instruction Compliance Even Without Imitation, and Makes Optimized Prompts Bank-Specific
Short Hypothesis:
Prompt optimization assumes the instruction slot's contribution is separable from whatever occupies the demonstration slot. When that slot holds a live experience bank, the assumption fails in two measurable ways.

(1) **The veto.** A verification requirement ("do not answer until you have cited spans you retrieved this episode, and the citation must actually support the answer") is complied with at high rate with no memory and at equally high rate with token- and keyword-matched *answer-redacted* memory, and collapses under answer-bearing memory — same model, same instances, same semantic requirement. The trigger is the presence of a usable candidate answer in the retrieved item, not topical overlap (M2/M4), not context load (M4/M6), and not corruption of the memory: the harmful items are truthful records of tasks the agent previously solved correctly.

(2) **The dissociation from experience-following.** The compliance drop is present *even on episodes where the final answer does not match the retrieved memory* (non-echo subset). Output-imitation accounts (Xiong et al., ACL 2026) predict memory effects concentrate where outputs track memory; the veto predicts a compliance deficit where they do not. This is the discriminating measurement, and it costs no extra episodes.

(3) **The boundary, not a universal negative.** Within one run, the same GEPA/MIPROv2 search substantially repairs memory-echoed ungrounded answers (a content-selection failure evaluated at generation time) while barely touching insufficient-evidence errors (a termination failure decided against a candidate answer already in context). Optimizers are seeded with the target instruction, so the fix is provably in the search space.

(4) **The consequence.** Because the slots are entangled, instructions optimized with a bank in context lose most of their measured advantage when the bank is swapped for one built from a disjoint split, while instructions optimized without memory are bank-invariant. If so, prompt-optimization gains reported on memory-augmented agents are partly bank-specific and are mis-attributed to the prompt.
Related Work:
I rebuilt this section on the literature search run for this proposal. An earlier draft anchored its novelty argument on arXiv:2605.24941 ("Memory-Induced Tool-Drift"), which this search did **not** return; three reviewers flagged that and several sibling IDs as unverifiable. I no longer rely on any of them. Nothing below is cited that the current search did not return, and I state the collision risk in terms that survive a different search returning a different neighbour.

**Closest work, partial collision: Xiong, Lin, Xie, He, Tang, Lakkaraju, Xiang, "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior," ACL 2026 (arXiv:2505.16067).** Establishes *experience-following*: when a task input is highly similar to a retrieved record's input, the agent's output becomes highly similar to that record's output, and this propagates errors across sequential tasks. This is the correlational core of my phenomenon and I concede it outright — "memory makes agents imitate the past" is established and this proposal does not claim it. What it does not do, and what I claim: it never measures whether the agent stops *complying with a contemporaneous instruction*, never separates answer-bearing from procedure-bearing content at matched tokens, and never asks whether the effect survives on episodes that do *not* imitate. That last point is a testable divergence, not a prose distinction: experience-following predicts memory effects are carried by output similarity, so restricting to non-echo episodes should largely remove them; the veto account predicts a ≥15-point compliance deficit persists there. Prediction 7 is exactly this test, and a null there is a win for their account.

**Closest on the failure mode, adversarial framing: "Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks" (arXiv:2608.16032).** Shows that adversarially written memory notes can convince an agent that a required verification step was already completed, and proposes checking memory claims against execution traces. This is the sharpest collision on the *symptom* — memory content causing a verification step to be skipped — and I treat it as such. The distinction is mechanistic and auditable: their memory *asserts* that verification occurred, so the agent is deceived about the world; my banks are ExpeL-style distillations of successfully solved training episodes that contain no claim about verification at all, and I run a stored-record correctness audit reporting the fraction of items retrieved on broken instances that are factually correct records of correctly solved tasks (prediction: ≥70%). If the harmful items turn out to be mostly wrong or to contain completion assertions, my "harm from correct memory" claim collapses into theirs and I say so. Their remedy is an execution-verification architecture; they run no instruction-compliance measurement and no optimizer.

**Directly threatens claim (3): "MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Safety Risks from Memory Misevolution in LLM Agents" (arXiv:2604.15774).** Finds that plain instruction-based prompting is insufficient to prevent behavioural degradation as misleading memory accumulates, and equips agents with active memory-correction tools instead. That is the same shape as "instructions lose to memory." Two differences carry my contribution. Their memory is *misevolved* — corrupted over rounds — so "bad memory beats good instructions" is unsurprising; mine is uncorrupted and useful (it fixes items as well as breaking them, gated in the precheck). And "prompting is insufficient" is asserted at the level of end-task safety scores; I measure per-episode compliance with a fixed semantic requirement under matched memory conditions, which is what turns an insufficiency observation into an interaction with a stated pattern (high / high / collapsed).

**Directly threatens claim (4): "Generalizable Self-Evolving Memory for Automatic Prompt Optimization" (MemAPO, arXiv:2603.21520).** Argues that automatic prompt optimization fits prompts to a fixed training query set, limiting generalization across heterogeneous queries, and proposes accumulating reusable experience *for* the optimizer. This is the nearest thing to my bank-entanglement claim and it points the opposite way: they treat memory as the cure for prompt overfitting; I claim memory in the context during optimization is itself a new axis of overfitting. The accounts make different predictions under a manipulation they do not run: hold the query distribution fixed and swap the bank. MemAPO's framing predicts a memory-conditioned prompt generalizes better across queries and says nothing that would predict collapse under a bank swap; I predict Δ(G1, Bank B) retains <40% of Δ(G1, Bank A) while Δ(G0, ·) is bank-invariant. Whichever way it comes out, it is a control that no memory-augmented prompt-optimization paper currently reports.

**Adjacent, non-colliding.** "Investigating Tool-Memory Conflicts in Tool-Augmented LLMs" (arXiv:2601.09760) quantifies precedence between tool output and stored memory — a source-conflict question, not an instruction-compliance question, and it does not vary instruction enforcement. "When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: Experience Reuse in LLM Agents" (arXiv:2604.27003) reports that reuse harms hard cases and that finer-grained memory organization is not universally beneficial; it partially anticipates my M2/M3 contrast, but its comparisons are between differently-authored memory formats confounded with length and abstraction, whereas my redaction holds item, retrieval and token count fixed and deletes exactly the answer. "Learning How to Remember" (arXiv:2601.07470) argues retrieval overfits to surface similarity and motivates meta-cognitive management; it is the strongest statement of the *rival* trigger (surface similarity), which my M2/M4 arms test directly.

**Prompt optimization.** MIPRO and GEPA decompose a prompt into instructions and demonstrations and search the instruction slot. Both assume the instruction slot's contribution is separable from the demonstration slot's occupant. Claim (4) says that assumption fails when the occupant is a live bank, and the bank-swap arm is designed so a reader can check it.
Abstract:
Retrieved-experience memory frequently makes LLM agents worse, and the field's explanations are about memory quality: stale, misevolved, adversarial, conflicting, too long. We propose something sharper. The items that do the damage in our setting are *correct* — truthful records of tasks the agent previously solved — and the damage is not only that the agent copies them. It is that the agent stops obeying the instruction that would have caught the error.

The centerpiece is a compliance-by-memory-condition design. One semantic requirement — before answering, cite spans you retrieved in *this* episode, and the citation must support the answer — is measured per episode under three memory conditions: none, token- and keyword-matched answer-redacted memory, and answer-bearing memory. We predict compliance is high and statistically equivalent in the first two and collapses by ≥25 points in the third, in the same model on the same instances. This excludes the two standing rebuttals by construction rather than by argument: the model can obviously execute the instruction (it does so under two conditions), and an optimizer cannot have under-searched for a fix that we seed into its initial population.

One measurement decides whether this is a new claim or a restatement of experience-following (Xiong et al., ACL 2026, the closest prior work). Experience-following says memory effects are carried by output imitation. We restrict to episodes where the final answer does *not* match the retrieved memory and ask whether the compliance deficit survives. If it vanishes, their account subsumes ours and we report that.

Two results decide whether it matters. A within-run dissociation shows the same seeded GEPA and MIPROv2 searches substantially repair memory-echoed ungrounded answers while barely touching insufficient-evidence errors — so this is a rule with a boundary, not "hard constraints beat soft prompts." And a bank-swap arm tests whether instructions optimized with a bank in context are bank-entangled: if Δ(G1, Bank A) largely disappears under a bank built from a disjoint split while memory-free-optimized instructions are invariant, then prompt-optimization gains reported on memory-augmented agents are partly bank-specific, and every such report needs a bank-invariance control it currently does not run.

The program is staged so the first stage is a paper on its own: ~20.7k self-hosted episodes, ≤$240 API, one environment, instance-paired throughout with fix/break decompositions, null replicates, stated MDEs and pre-registered refutation conditions.
Experiments:
HELD FIXED THROUGHOUT: agent scaffold (ReAct with search/lookup over a fixed corpus), tool stack, step limit, retriever and similarity function, memory banks (built once, then frozen), decoding temperature and seed schedule, prompt boilerplate, held-out split. Only the memory variant, the instruction, and the enforcement level vary.

ENVIRONMENT (one, deliberately). Tool-augmented multi-hop QA pooled across HotpotQA (distractor), MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA in fixed proportions, 4–8 model calls per episode. Evidence gathering is explicit, countable and cheap to instrument. WebShop and ALFWorld are cut and stay cut: at affordable n they are underpowered, and an underpowered replication carries no claim. Cross-environment generality is a stated limitation, not a smuggled implication.

MODELS. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct primary (all headline numbers). Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct replicates the decisive arms at one seed. A mid-tier frontier API model runs the compliance probe on 120 instances — a funded arm, not a promise, because "is the veto a small-model artifact" is the objection this most deserves. Qwen3-32B is the bulk trajectory annotator, never an agent. A frontier model does one-off bank distillation, redaction, and optimizer reflection.

BANKS (all frozen before any test episode). **A** (primary): ExpeL-style distillation over training split S1, ~600 items, each a record of a solved episode. **B**: identical procedure over disjoint split S2 (bank-swap only). **A-curated**: contradiction-pruned and call-balance-rebalanced — the field's existing write-path repair. **RB**: ReasoningBank-style strategy distillation over S1, generalized procedures with no final answers. **RB+O**: RB with the corresponding final answers re-attached, token-matched to RB plus the answer text.

PRECHECK (gates the study; 150 dev instances, ~900 episodes). Confirm (a) Bank A fixes ≥4% and breaks ≥4% of instances vs no memory — the bank must be useful, not merely bad; (b) compliance with I* under no memory is ≥65%, else the contrast has no headroom and the study is about generic non-compliance; (c) ≥20% of Bank A's induced errors are type-B, else the dissociation is reported as exploratory; (d) stored-record correctness audit: ≥70% of items retrieved on broken instances are truthful records of correctly solved tasks and contain no assertion that a verification step occurred. All four numbers are published regardless. (d) is the gate that separates this study from adversarial/misevolution accounts; if it fails, the framing changes to "harm from imperfect memory" and the paper is weaker and honest.

THE THREE INSTRUCTIONS. **I\*** (target): *before emitting a final answer, state the spans retrieved in this episode that support it.* **I_B** (equal-burden control, memory-orthogonal, added at reviewer request): *before emitting a final answer, state which tools you called this episode and in what order* — comparable output burden and format discipline, but nothing that competes with a stored answer. **I_M** (anti-memory control, added at reviewer request): *do not rely on prior similar cases; treat retrieved experience as context only.* The claim is about the instruction *slot*, so it needs more than one sentence to be a claim about the slot.

CENTERPIECE — ENFORCEMENT × MEMORY (Stage 1, n=400 paired test instances). Three enforcement levels of I*: **Fs** (instruction appended, no enforcement); **G** (GEPA on the instruction slot only, memory frozen in the demonstration slot, 350 rollouts, 150-instance train split, reflective feedback including failed trajectories and their tool-call counts, **initial candidate population seeded with I\* verbatim**); **Fh** (identical requirement enforced programmatically — unsupported or absent citation is rejected and at least one further tool call is forced, capped at three extra calls; fixed on a 100-instance dev split before any test run and published verbatim).

Stage 1 arms (n=400): bare M0 / M1 / M2 at 2 seeds; M0+Fs / M1+Fs / M2+Fs at 2 seeds; M0+Fh / M1+Fh at 2 seeds and M2+Fh at 1; G0@M0 and G1@M1 at 2 seeds, G0@M1 at 1. Here M0 = no memory, M1 = Bank A at k=7 (standard deployment), M2 = answer-redacted Bank A at k=7 (procedure kept — which sources, how to disambiguate, in what order; any final answer / result value / completion statement deleted; padded with neutral task-generic filler to match M1's injected tokens within 5% per instance and audited for keyword-overlap parity).

STAGE 2 — THE CONSEQUENCE (bank swap, n=400). Evaluate the base instruction, G0 (optimized without memory) and G1 (optimized with Bank A) under Bank B; G1@Bank B at 2 seeds. Report Δ(instruction, bank) = score(instruction, bank) − score(base, bank).

STAGE 3 — CONTENT SPECIFICITY AND EXISTING REPAIRS (1 seed, n=400 each). **M3** answer-only mirror of Bank A, keywords stripped, token-matched. **M3x** mismatched-answer: an answer-bearing item whose stored answer belongs to a different, topically near instance — tests whether the stored answer must be *applicable* for truncation to occur (added in response to the "decisiveness cue" objection). **M4** decoy items retrieved for a disjoint task family, token-matched — removes experience relevance at constant load. **M5** Bank A at k=3 — the volume lever from the track's prior findings. **M6** M1 with the step budget raised by the mean extra calls Fh consumes — separates "allowed to look longer" from "required to justify." **M8** Bank A-curated — the field's existing fix. **M9** Bank RB; **M9+O** Bank RB+O — asks whether strategy memory is safe *because* it omits answers, by putting them back. **M1-hedged** Bank A verbatim but each item explicitly labelled low-confidence/unverified ("a past attempt; may not apply") — the cheapest deployable mitigation.

STAGE 4 — INSTRUCTION FAMILY AND SECOND OPTIMIZER (1 seed, n=400 each). M0+Fb, M1+Fb (I_B under no memory and Bank A), M1+Fm (I_M under Bank A), and MIPROv2@M1 (second, independently implemented optimizer on the instruction slot, 350 rollouts, also seeded with I*).

INSTRUMENTATION (every episode). Tool calls before final answer; distinct documents examined; step at which the final answer's entity first appears; EVIDENCE SUFFICIENCY (binary: do spans supporting the final answer appear in this episode's own retrievals?); COMPLIANCE (binary: did the agent, before answering, satisfy the *semantic* requirement of the instruction in force — defined even when GEPA rewrites the wording); CITATION VALIDITY (do the cited spans actually support the answer — prevents compliance-by-fabrication); MEMORY-ECHO (is the answer verbatim or semantically identical to injected content?); confidence at termination.

ANALYSIS 1 — MEDIATION (descriptive, supporting). Per-instance paired M1-vs-M0 outcome (fix/break/unchanged) against paired deltas in tool calls and sufficiency; mixed-effects model of the break event on the memory indicator with and without mediators. Post-treatment mediator, so descriptive only; the enforcement arms are the causal test.

ANALYSIS 2 — THE VETO (centerpiece). Primary quantity: compliance with I* under Fs as a function of memory condition, memory × condition interaction in a mixed-effects logistic model with instance random intercepts. Predicted pattern comp(M0) ≈ comp(M2) ≫ comp(M1), with M0-vs-M2 tested for *equivalence*, not mere non-significance. Same pattern tested for G, and shown absent for Fh. Secondary: the accuracy interaction (breaks under M1 − breaks under M1+Fh) − (errors under M0 − errors under M0+Fh). Under-search is excluded by construction; we additionally report GEPA's train-score trajectory, whether it retained or discarded the seeded I*, and the evolved text verbatim. If GEPA discards I* because verification does not pay under memory, that is itself the co-adaptation finding.

ANALYSIS 3 — DISSOCIATION FROM EXPERIENCE-FOLLOWING (no extra episodes; the test against Xiong et al.). Restrict to M1 episodes where the final answer does *not* match injected content (non-echo subset) and re-estimate the compliance deficit vs M0 on the same instances. Output-imitation accounts predict the deficit largely vanishes; the veto predicts ≥15 points persists.

ANALYSIS 4 — CONTENT SPECIFICITY. M1/M2/M3/M3x/M4 at matched tokens: full fix/break tables and tool-call distributions. Surface-similarity accounts (arXiv:2601.07470) predict M2 ≈ M1 (same items, same keywords); the answer-bearing account predicts M2 ≪ M1 and M3 ≥ M1. M3x asks whether an inapplicable stored answer still truncates. M9 vs M9+O asks the same question of a deployed design.

ANALYSIS 5 — THE OPTIMIZER'S BOUNDARY. Partition M1's errors into type A (insufficient evidence gathered — a termination failure) and type B (sufficient evidence gathered, answer memory-echoed and ungrounded — a content-selection failure). Compute G1's and MIPROv2's reduction of each class separately. This is what turns "code beats prompts" into a rule with a stated boundary.

ANALYSIS 6 — REPAIR LADDER ON MATCHED COST. Break reduction and *fix preservation* for M5, M8, M2, M1-hedged, G1/MIPROv2, M1+Fh against M1, on matched tool-call, matched-token and wall-clock axes. Predicted ordering on fix preservation: redaction and the floor keep fixes; curation and k=3 neutralize harm by discarding useful items too.

ANALYSIS 7 — INSTRUCTION-SLOT GENERALITY. Compliance with I_B under M0 vs M1 (equal burden, no competing answer) and with I_M under M1. If I_B collapses as much as I*, the effect is generic burden-under-context and the veto framing is wrong.

ANALYSIS 8 — BANK SWAP. As above; the practice-facing result.

STAGING AND PARTIAL-COMPLETION POLICY (added because a four-part interlocked story is a feasibility risk). Stages run in the order 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, and Stage 1 plus Analyses 1–3 is the paper. Stages 2–4 are ordered by how much each would move a skeptic. Anything unfinished is reported as *unrun*, never as a null; no claim is made from an arm whose seeds did not complete.

SAMPLE SIZES AND BUDGET. Stage 0: 900. Stage 1: 8,800. Stage 2: 1,600. Stage 3: 3,600. Stage 4: 1,600. Null replicates (M0, M1, M1+Fs, M1+Fh at a third seed): 1,600. Llama-8B decisive subset (M0, M1, M2, M1+Fs, M1+Fh at n=300): 1,500. Optimizer search rollouts (2 GEPA × 350 + MIPROv2 × 350): 1,050. **Total ≈ 20,650 self-hosted episodes**, ~6 calls each ≈ 124k calls. With vLLM at four data-parallel replicas on 4×A100-80GB and a conservatively measured ~1,200 episodes/hour for the 14B model, that is ~17 GPU-hours of agent rollouts; with annotation passes, retries and optimizer overhead, budget **~32 node-hours, two days**. Frontier compliance probe: 4 arms (M0+Fs, M1+Fs, M2+Fs, M1+Fh) × 120 instances = 480 API episodes. API: bank distillations ~$35, redaction and mismatch construction ~$20, optimizer reflection ~$25, gold annotation of 500 episodes ~$35, frontier probe ~$65, contingency ~$60 — **≤ $240**.
Baselines and Ablations:
BASELINES THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY WIN AND WOULD REFUTE US.
(i) **G1 — GEPA-optimized instruction with memory, seeded with I\*.** The direct threat to the veto claim. If it recovers the floor's break reduction, prompt optimization owns this failure and we say so.
(ii) **MIPROv2@M1.** Second, independently implemented optimizer, also seeded with I*, because a null from one search algorithm generalizes poorly.
(iii) **M1+Fs — hand-written I\*.** The cheap repair, and the arm whose memory-conditional compliance is the centerpiece measurement.
(iv) **M1+Fb — equal-burden, memory-orthogonal instruction (I_B).** Reviewer-requested and accepted. If I_B's compliance collapses under memory as much as I*'s, then any added verification burden degrades under long/complex context and the specific "competes with a stored answer" story is dead.
(v) **M1+Fm — anti-memory instruction (I_M).** Reviewer-requested and accepted. Tests whether the veto is specific to verification-style requirements or covers any instruction targeting memory reliance.
(vi) **M8 — curated bank (contradiction-pruning + call-balance rebalancing).** The field's existing write-path repair. If it matches redaction and the floor on breaks *and* fixes, the recommendation is "curate your bank" and we add nothing actionable.
(vii) **M1-hedged — same items labelled low-confidence.** Reviewer-requested and accepted. If a framing label fixes it, that is the cheapest deployable mitigation and we should recommend it over anything we propose.
(viii) **M5 (k=3)** — the volume lever from the track's prior findings. If volume subsumes answer content on every endpoint, our mechanism is redundant.
(ix) **M6 (raised step budget)** — separates "allowed to look longer" from "required to justify."
(x) **M0+Fh and M0+Fs** — if the floor helps the memory-free agent as much as the memory-augmented one, and compliance is equally low without memory, there is no interaction and the finding degenerates into "citing evidence is good," which is known.
(xi) **Frontier compliance probe** — if compliance under M1+Fs is high for a strong model, the effect is capability-scoped, the claim narrows to open-weight deployments, and we change the title.

KEY ABLATIONS ISOLATING THE MECHANISM. M1 / M2 / M3 / M3x / M4 is the content ladder at matched tokens and matched keyword overlap: same bank, same retrieval, opposite halves deleted, so any asymmetry is attributable to answer-bearing content rather than to memory presence, length or surface similarity. M3x tests whether the stored answer must be applicable. M4 removes experience relevance at constant load. M9 vs M9+O tests whether strategy memory is safe because it omits answers. The enforcement ladder crossed with all three memory conditions is the essential design feature: every claim about the instruction slot is an interaction, never a main effect. Citation-validity auditing (applied identically to Fs, G and Fh) prevents compliance-by-fabrication and separates "the optimizer never wrote the fix" from "the optimizer wrote it and the agent ignored it." Memory-echo separates copying from guessing and defines the non-echo subset on which the test against experience-following runs. The stored-record correctness audit separates "harm from correct memory" from adversarial and misevolution accounts. All arms are reported on matched tool-call, token and wall-clock axes so no arm is credited for spending more.
Falsifiable Predictions:
**Mechanism (C1).**
1. Instances broken by M1 show ≥1.5 fewer tool calls (median) than the same instances under M0 and ≥30% relative reduction in mean calls, while instances fixed by M1 show no such reduction; the difference of the two deltas clears the noise floor.
2. Evidence sufficiency drops ≥12 points under M1 vs M0; memory-echo on wrong answers exceeds 40%.
3. Stored-record correctness audit: ≥70% of items retrieved on broken instances are truthful records of correctly solved past tasks, and <5% contain any assertion that a verification step occurred. (Separates this from adversarial-forgery and misevolution accounts.)

**Content specificity (C1').**
4. M2 retains ≥70% of M1's fixes while shedding ≥50% of its breaks, at matched tokens and matched keyword overlap; M3 breaks at least as many instances as M1 with the shortest trajectories of any arm. Surface-similarity accounts predict M2 ≈ M1 on breaks; we predict a ≥50% gap.
5. M4 (decoys) reproduces <1/3 of M1's tool-call reduction. M3x (inapplicable stored answer) reproduces ≥60% of M1's tool-call reduction — truncation does not require the stored answer to be right.
6. Bank RB (no answers) behaves like M2 on breaks; RB+O restores ≥60% of M1-level harm at matched tokens.

**The veto (C2 — centerpiece).**
7. Compliance with I* under Fs: comp(M0) ≥ 65%, comp(M2) within 8 points of comp(M0) (equivalence test), comp(M1) ≥25 points below comp(M0). The memory × compliance interaction clears the stated MDE.
8. **The test against experience-following:** restricted to the non-echo subset of M1 episodes, the compliance deficit vs M0 remains ≥15 points. If it falls below 7 points, output-imitation subsumes the veto and C2 is withdrawn.
9. Instruction specificity: compliance with I_B (equal burden, memory-orthogonal) drops by <10 points from M0 to M1, i.e. less than half of I*'s drop. Compliance with I_M (anti-memory) drops by ≥15 points, i.e. the veto is not unique to one sentence but does spare instructions that make no claim on termination.
10. The searched instruction G shows the same pattern: G1's compliance stays within 10 points of M1+Fs despite the search being seeded with I* — the optimizer either retains verification language that is not obeyed, or discards it because it does not pay under memory. We report which.
11. M1+Fh cuts breaks relative to M1 by ≥50% while M0+Fh improves M0 by less than a third of that in absolute points; M1+Fh stays within 2 points of M1 on fixes. M1+Fs, G1 and MIPROv2 each recover <1/3 of M1+Fh's break reduction.

**The boundary (C3).**
12. Within M1's errors, G1 reduces type-B (sufficient evidence, memory-echoed, ungrounded) by ≥50% relative and type-A (insufficient evidence) by <20% relative, with the difference of reductions clearing the MDE. Equal reduction of A and B falsifies the rule and leaves only the unsurprising "hard constraints beat soft instructions," which we would state plainly.

**The consequence (C4).**
13. Δ(G1, Bank A) ≥ +3 points over the base instruction, and Δ(G1, Bank B) retains <40% of that; Δ(G0, Bank A) and Δ(G0, Bank B) agree within 2 points. Instructions optimized with a bank in context are bank-entangled; memory-free-optimized instructions are not.

**REFUTATION CONDITIONS.** If broken instances under M1 have trajectories no shorter than under M0, mediation is dead. If comp(M0+Fs) < 65%, this is generic non-compliance and the veto framing is wrong; we report that and the paper shrinks to a note on instruction-following floors. If comp(M1+Fs) ≈ comp(M0+Fs), memory does not veto instructions and C2–C4 fall. If the non-echo compliance deficit is <7 points, Xiong et al.'s experience-following explains our phenomenon. If ≥30% of harmful items are incorrect records or assert prior verification, the adversarial/misevolution accounts explain it. If I_B collapses as much as I*, the effect is burden-under-context. If M2 sheds fixes with breaks (fix retention <50%), answer content is doing the useful work and redaction is not viable. If M4 reproduces truncation, this is context load. If M8, M5 or M1-hedged matches redaction and the floor on both breaks and fixes, existing/cheaper repairs subsume ours. If G1 or MIPROv2 matches M1+Fh on breaks, instruction optimization owns this failure and that is the finding. If Δ(G1, Bank B) retains most of Δ(G1, Bank A), the practice-facing claim is withdrawn.
Measurement and Noise Control:
Fully paired design: every held-out instance is run under every arm with the same seed schedule; all comparisons are within-instance. Primary tests are exact McNemar on paired fix/break tables, Holm-corrected within each pre-declared claim family (mechanism, veto, boundary, consequence) rather than across the whole study. Every reported delta carries its fix/break decomposition, because a null net delta hiding symmetric churn is a different finding from an inert intervention.

The centerpiece quantity is a per-episode binary (compliance), which carries far more signal than accuracy. At n=400 instances × 2 seeds, a 25-point compliance gap is detected with power >0.99, and the M0-vs-M2 equivalence test at an 8-point margin has power ≈0.82. The non-echo subset test (prediction 8) is the weakest-powered headline quantity: if ~50% of M1 episodes are non-echo, n ≈ 200 × 2 seeds gives ~0.85 power for a 15-point deficit; if the non-echo subset falls below 120 instances the test is reported as exploratory and the discrimination against experience-following is declared unresolved rather than won. Interactions (memory × enforcement, memory × instruction, memory × error type) are estimated in mixed-effects logistic models with instance random intercepts; CIs from a 10k-resample instance-level bootstrap.

Accuracy MDEs at n=400 paired instances (seeds averaged per instance before pairing): with a 12–18% discordant-pair rate, McNemar detects a net swing of ~5 points at 80% power (α=0.05). The break endpoint is one-sided and more sensitive: with M1 breaking ~40 of 400, a halving is detected at power ≈0.82. The memory × floor interaction — a difference of two paired differences — is detectable at ~6.5 points, which is why prediction 11 is stated as ≥50% break reduction against a much smaller M0+Fh gain and why nothing smaller is claimed. Fix preservation is an equivalence test at a 2-point margin and is the weakest quantity; differences between 2 and 3 points are reported inconclusive. One-seed arms (all of Stages 3–4, Llama-8B) have MDEs near 8 points and are labelled directional throughout — they can refute a strong prediction but cannot carry a headline. Tool-call deltas of ~0.5 calls/episode are detectable; full call distributions are reported because the predicted effect is a shift in the lower tail.

NULL REPLICATES: for each model, M0, M1, M1+Fs and M1+Fh are re-run under a third decoding seed and the distribution of apparent deltas is reported; no effect is claimed unless it exceeds the 95th percentile of that distribution. This remains load-bearing given the track's prior observation of 5–14 point re-scoring drift and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment.

ANNOTATION. Evidence sufficiency, compliance, citation validity, memory-echo and stored-record correctness are labelled by the self-hosted Qwen3-32B annotator, validated against a 500-episode frontier gold sample and a 200-episode human-labelled sample, with Cohen's kappa per label. Compliance and citation validity are load-bearing and most likely to be contested: their analyses are re-run with the frontier annotator on the gold subset and demoted to supporting evidence if kappa < 0.7 (stricter than the 0.6 bar for secondary labels). The primary task outcome is exact-match/F1 against dataset gold and needs no judge. Optimizer-produced instructions, the harness floor, and the redaction procedure are published verbatim so a reader can check whether GEPA in fact wrote a verification requirement and whether redaction leaked the answer.
Preprint Collision Check:
This section is grounded entirely in the literature search run for this proposal. **Correction to the previous draft:** it anchored its novelty argument on arXiv:2605.24941 ("Memory-Induced Tool-Drift in LLM Agents") and five sibling IDs. The current search returned none of them. Three reviewers flagged those citations as unverifiable and were right to. I have removed every one and rebuilt positioning on what the search actually returned. I state below both the collisions and how much of the proposal survives if a tool-drift-style paper does exist and I simply have not seen it.

**Closest work, partial collision: Xiong et al., "How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior," ACL 2026 (arXiv:2505.16067).** Collides on the phenomenon: retrieved memory drives agent output toward the recorded outcome even when this propagates error. I concede this and no longer claim it. It does not collide on the claim: no compliance measurement, no matched-token content decomposition, no instruction-slot or optimizer analysis. The collision is settled empirically, not rhetorically, by prediction 8 — the compliance deficit restricted to non-imitating episodes. If that deficit disappears, their account subsumes mine and I report it as a negative result for the veto.

**Collides on the symptom, different framing: "Proof-of-Execution Memory" (arXiv:2608.16032).** Shows adversarially forged memory notes convincing an agent that a verification step was already done, and proposes verifying memory claims against execution traces. This is the closest thing in the literature to "memory makes agents skip verification," and it is a genuine collision at symptom level. The distinguishing facts are auditable, not asserted: my banks are distillations of correctly solved training episodes, and prediction 3 commits me to reporting that ≥70% of items retrieved on broken instances are truthful and <5% assert prior verification. If that audit fails, the phenomenon is theirs and I say so. They run no non-adversarial condition, no compliance measurement, and no optimizer.

**Collides on claim (3): "MemEvoBench" (arXiv:2604.15774).** Reports that plain instruction-based prompting is insufficient to prevent degradation under accumulating misleading memory. Same shape as "instructions lose to memory," so I treat it as a real collision on the top-level statement. Their memory is misevolved/corrupted, mine is uncorrupted and demonstrably useful (the precheck gates on the bank fixing ≥4% of instances); and "prompting is insufficient" measured on end-task safety scores is a different object from a per-episode compliance rate measured under matched memory conditions with an equivalence-tested control arm. What I add over them is the pattern (high / high / collapsed), the non-imitation dissociation, and the seeded-optimizer test.

**Collides on claim (4), pointing the other way: MemAPO (arXiv:2603.21520).** Argues automatic prompt optimization overfits to the training query set and proposes memory as the remedy. My claim is that memory in context during optimization is itself an overfitting axis. The two accounts differ under a manipulation MemAPO does not run — hold queries fixed, swap the bank — and prediction 13 states the divergence. If Δ(G1, Bank B) holds up, MemAPO's optimistic framing is right and my consequence claim is withdrawn.

**Adjacent, no collision.** arXiv:2601.09760 (tool-memory conflicts) studies source precedence, not instruction compliance, and does not vary enforcement. arXiv:2604.27003 (experience reuse as continual learning) reports harm on hard cases and non-monotone benefits from finer memory organization; it partially anticipates M2 vs M3 but confounds format with length and abstraction. arXiv:2601.07470 (meta-cognitive memory management) is the clearest statement of the rival *surface-similarity* trigger, which M2 and M4 test directly.

**Explicit gap, in the search's own terms.** The search's own summary states that what is unaddressed is (i) the causal claim that retrieved memory suppresses compliance with explicit contemporaneous verification instructions in a *non-adversarial* setting, isolated from general output-similarity bias, and (ii) the claim that prompt optimization becomes dependent on the specific bank used during optimization. Those are exactly claims (1)/(2) and (4). I add to that a third thing the search did not surface: a within-run boundary showing where instruction optimization *does* repair a memory-induced failure, which is what prevents this from being a universal negative.

**HONEST CAVEATS.** I could not search ICLR/NeurIPS/ACL 2026–2027 submission portals. The "memory overrides correct behaviour" phenomenon is now documented from at least three independent angles (output imitation, tool-vs-memory precedence, adversarial verification-skipping), so I assume more such work exists than I have seen and I do not rest anything on the phenomenon being new. Every claim is structured to fail independently: if the veto is scooped, the non-imitation dissociation, the boundary, and the bank-swap consequence stand separately; if the bank-swap is scooped, Stage 1 stands alone.
Risk Factors and Limitations:
1. **Precheck failure.** Four gates can stop the study: too few breaks, too few fixes, low baseline compliance, or a memory bank whose harmful items turn out to be incorrect records. All four numbers are published. If baseline compliance is below 65%, the veto framing is unsupportable and we say so rather than reframing around a weaker contrast. If breaks are below 4%, we adjust the bank-construction split size once (a pre-registered, content-neutral knob) and otherwise abandon.
2. **Collision risk I cannot clear.** Two returned papers (Xiong et al.; Proof-of-Execution Memory) collide at phenomenon and symptom level respectively. Prediction 8 and prediction 3 are the tests that decide whether anything is left; both can come out against me, and I have named the thresholds in advance.
3. **The "answer-bearing vs decisive cue" concession.** A reviewer correctly noted that removing the stored answer also removes the most decisive text in the item, so "answer-bearing content" and "salient decisive cue" are not separable at the resolution I can test. I no longer claim that distinction. I renamed the construct to *answer-bearing* and restricted the claim to what redaction actually decides: answer presence versus topical/keyword overlap (M2 vs M1), versus context load (M4, M6), and versus applicability of the stored answer (M3x).
4. **Post-treatment mediation.** Analysis 1 conditions on a post-treatment variable and cannot support causality alone; the enforcement arms are the causal test and the mediation is framed as descriptive throughout.
5. **The floor is a design surface.** It could be tuned into the result. It is fixed on a 100-instance dev split before any test run, published verbatim, capped at three extra calls, and audited for fabricated citations.
6. **Redaction leakage.** Procedural text can implicitly encode the answer ("search for the 1994 record"). We report an automated leakage audit plus a 150-item human check and treat leakage as a measured contamination rate.
7. **Optimizer under-search.** Mitigated structurally: GEPA and MIPROv2 are seeded with the target instruction, so the fix is in the search space by construction, and the same instruction's high compliance under M0/M2 proves the model can execute it. If GEPA discards the seed with no verification language surviving, we report that as evidence about the fitness landscape and mark enforcement-vs-discovery as partially unresolved for that condition.
8. **Capability scoping.** The frontier compliance probe (480 episodes, funded) is the direct test. If compliance under M1+Fs is high for the frontier model, we narrow the claim to open-weight deployments and change the title. Per-model curves, not a pooled headline.
9. **Single environment.** The mechanism is demonstrated only where evidence gathering is literal retrieval. WebShop and ALFWorld stay cut; generalization to embodied exploration is an open question, not an implied result. Depth over breadth was chosen because every discriminating manipulation requires matched-token construction that is hard outside a retrieval setting.
10. **Type-B scarcity.** The boundary result needs enough sufficient-evidence memory-echo errors. The precheck gates on it; below 25 instances it is exploratory, which costs the paper its cleanest defence against "hard constraints beat soft prompts."
11. **Non-echo subset size.** Prediction 8 is the discriminating test against the closest prior work and is also the least powered headline quantity. If the subset is small, the discrimination is reported unresolved.
12. **Execution risk from scope.** Even after cuts this is a multi-arm study. Mitigated by strict staging (Stage 1 alone is the paper) and by a policy of reporting unfinished arms as unrun rather than null. Stages 3–4 are one-seed and explicitly directional.
13. **Cost of the fix.** If the floor works but consumes substantially more tool calls, the honest framing is "a cheap procedural guard beats curating the bank, but it is not free," and all arms are reported on matched-cost axes.

Name: memory_volume_amplifies_optimizer_curse
Title: Does Retrieved Memory Inflate the Optimizer's Curse? Injection Budget as a Lever on Selection Bias in Agent Prompt Search
Short Hypothesis: The headline claim is the coupling, not the curse. (i) **Mechanism:** injecting k retrieved experience items into a ReAct agent inflates the run-to-run variance of its validation score (E0), so a prompt optimizer searching over that agent selects more strongly on luck. (ii) **Consequence:** the fraction of a reflective prompt optimizer's reported validation gain that is pure selection bias — measured by a *null optimizer* whose proposal step is replaced by identity/judge-verified paraphrase — is strictly larger at k=7 than at k=0. If true, coupled memory+optimizer systems report gains that are increasingly selection artefact, which is a concrete explanation for why such gains do not replicate. (iii) **Remedy feasibility, measured not assumed:** the standard variance-reduction move, common random numbers over shared items and shared decoding seeds, may not survive interactivity because a changed prompt changes the action sequence; we decompose the cross-candidate correlation of per-item outcomes into item-sharing and seed-sharing components and report how much of each survives. (iv) **A separation we predict analytically and test:** empirical-Bayes shrinkage fixes the *reported number* but, under equal evaluation budgets, is rank-preserving and therefore cannot change *which* prompt is returned. The existence and rough size of the curse (claims (v) below) is treated as calibration/replication, not as novelty, because the track's own prior work already observed a null replicate matching the best real treatment.
Related Work:
**We do not claim the mechanism, and we no longer lead with the phenomenon.** Both reviewers were right that the qualitative "winner's curse exists in prompt search" claim is anticipated; the proposal has been repositioned around the two things that are not.

- *Dodge et al., "Show Your Work" (EMNLP 2019)* derives the expected-validation-max-of-N inflation for hyperparameter search and argues reported numbers must be reported as a function of search budget. This is exactly the extreme-value mechanism we invoke. We cite it as the mechanism paper and claim none of it.
- *The track's own prior results are the closest collision and the origin of this idea.* That work reported (a) a null replicate with no treatment producing the same apparent gain as the best real treatment, and (b) re-scoring the same candidate on the same held-out set moving the metric 5–14 points. Our P6 (existence and magnitude of the curse at loop level) is therefore **systematized replication**, labelled as such in the abstract and in the results section. What that work did not do is measure the curse *inside* the optimization loop as a function of the memory injection budget, which is the variable it independently identified as the causal lever for negative transfer (7 items harmful, 3 items not). Tying that volume lever to selection statistics is our first contribution.
- *ProTeGi* (Pryzant et al., EMNLP 2023) allocates evaluations with UCB/successive rejects — attacks the same problem by allocation, never quantifies how much of the final gain is bias, does not control rollout randomness. *MIPROv2* (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024) periodically re-scores the incumbent on full validation, a partial mitigation we run as a baseline. *GEPA* (2025) keeps per-instance scores on a fixed validation pool (implicit item-sharing) without a variance-aware acceptance test. *APE, OPRO, EvoPrompt, TextGrad, PromptAgent* take argmax of a noisy score with no correction. Community discussion of DSPy-style optimizers overfitting small validation sets exists but, to our knowledge, without a quantified bias fraction for agent tasks.
- *Common random numbers, racing, indifference-zone selection* (simulation optimization; Hoeffding races; successive halving) and *winner's-curse shrinkage* (GWAS, selective inference, A/B testing) are the standard remedies elsewhere. Transporting them is incremental in itself. What is unestablished — and is our second contribution — is whether CRN survives in an *interactive* agent, where a changed prompt changes the tool queries and decorrelates downstream state. We measure the surviving correlation rather than assume it.
- *ExpeL / Reflexion / ReasoningBank*-style memory report end-to-end gains from injecting distilled experience. We use an ExpeL-style bank as the memory implementation and treat injection volume as the experimental factor.

**Novel objects claimed, after repositioning:** (1) the injection-budget × selection-bias interaction, measured with a paired-by-optimizer-seed null-optimizer design; (2) a measured decomposition of cross-candidate outcome correlation in interactive agent rollouts into item-sharing and seed-sharing components, which determines whether CRN is available at all; (3) the equal-budget rank-preservation result for EB shrinkage, separating "fixes the report" from "fixes the choice", calibrated against an oracle-selection ceiling. Everything else is labelled replication or baseline.
Abstract:
Automatic prompt optimizers return the candidate with the best validation score. When that score is noisy — as it is for LLM agents, where re-scoring one configuration on the same held-out set moves the metric by several points — the winner is selected partly for being lucky, and the reported gain is inflated. The mechanism is old (max-of-N extreme-value inflation; Dodge et al. 2019) and its qualitative presence in agent prompt search has already been observed. We therefore do not lead with it.

We lead with a coupling claim that follows from it. Prior controlled work in this line found that memory *injection volume* — how many retrieved experience items enter the context — is the causal lever for negative transfer. We argue volume is simultaneously a **variance** lever: more injected items lengthen and destabilize rollouts, inflating the score noise a prompt optimizer selects on. The prediction is sharp and testable: the fraction of an optimizer's reported validation gain that is pure selection bias is strictly larger at high injection budget than at zero. Coupled memory+optimizer systems would then report gains that are increasingly artefact, which is a mechanistic explanation for their non-replication.

We measure this with a **null optimizer**: the identical reflective loop with the proposal step replaced by identity or judge-verified semantics-preserving paraphrase, so any apparent improvement is selection bias accumulated over generations. Runs are paired by optimizer seed across k=0 and k=7, so the interaction is tested within-seed. A separate nested-ANOVA noise audit isolates the variance components (item sampling, decoding, injection) that the prediction rests on.

We then ask what can be done, and separate two answers usually conflated. Empirical-Bayes shrinkage corrects the *reported* number for free but, under equal evaluation budgets, is rank-preserving and cannot change *which* prompt is chosen. Changing the choice requires reducing the variance of candidate *differences* — common random numbers plus a paired acceptance test — and whether CRN survives in an interactive agent is precisely the objection to it. We answer it by measuring the residual cross-candidate correlation of per-item outcomes, split into item-sharing and seed-sharing components, and by comparing every selection rule (including an oracle ceiling and a random-choice floor) by Monte-Carlo resampling from a cached candidate × item × seed outcome tensor with ground truth on 1,200 held-out items — well powered at zero marginal rollout cost.

One task, one 7B model, 16 optimization runs, ~161k episodes, ~3 days on one node, <$200 API.
Experiments:
**Scope, deliberately narrow.** One task family, one agent model, one memory implementation, instruction-only search. Dropped since the last version: ALFWorld, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, the frozen-vs-self-editing memory ablation, the single-stage-injection ablation, live re-runs of published claims, the desk audit of published claims, and the closed-loop remedy arm (see E3 note and changes_made).

**Setup.** Task: multi-hop QA (HotpotQA distractor + HoVer) with a ReAct agent over a *local, deterministic, cached* BM25+dense retrieval tool (no network; tool responses reproducible given the same query string). Agent: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on vLLM, 4×A100. Reflector/proposer/judge: frontier API model. Splits: 500 train episodes (memory distillation only), 300-item validation pool used for search, 1,200-item held-out set (disjoint, fixed, never used for search or for any threshold selection). Optimizer: GEPA-style reflective evolutionary search over the *instruction* only, 8 generations × 12 candidates, minibatch m=50 → **4,800 rollouts per optimization run**. Memory: ExpeL-style bank distilled by the frontier model from the 500 train episodes; dense retrieval; injection budget k items per step.

---

**E0 — Variance components as a function of injection budget (9,600 rollouts). Mechanistic half of the headline claim.**
One fixed seed prompt, 8 replicates, crossing two resampling modes — (a) resampled 200-item minibatch, (b) resampled decoding seeds on a fixed 200-item set — at k ∈ {0, 3, 7}.
Cost: 8 × 200 × 3 × 2 = 9,600.
Analysis: nested ANOVA giving item-sampling, decoding/rollout, and injection-attributable variance components with parametric-bootstrap CIs; σ(m) curves by subsampling within the 200-item set; primary reported quantity is the ratio σ(k=7)/σ(k=0) with its CI. Also reports mean episode length and tool-call count by k, since the proposed mechanism is that injection lengthens and destabilizes trajectories.

**E1 — Null optimizer × injection budget (97,200 rollouts). Primary experiment.**
Design: 2 (real proposal / null identity-paraphrase proposal) × 2 (k=0 / k=7) × **4 optimizer seeds** = **16 optimization runs** × 4,800 = 76,800 rollouts. Held-out scoring of the 16 returned prompts plus the seed prompt on 1,200 items = 20,400.
**Pairing:** optimizer seed controls the minibatch sequence and, in the null arm, the paraphrase-candidate sequence; the *same* seed index is used at k=0 and k=7, so the k-contrast is a within-seed paired contrast, which is where the power for the headline claim comes from.
Null candidates: the incumbent verbatim, or paraphrases passing a two-stage screen (string-level check that no new procedural token/verb is introduced; frontier-judge pairwise verdict of procedural equivalence). Exact-copy and paraphrase variants logged separately.
Endpoints per run: validation gain of the returned prompt over the seed prompt; fresh-decoding-seed re-score of the returned prompt on the same validation pool; held-out score.
Derived: **null gain** (points, primary for the k-contrast), **curse fraction** = null gain / real gain (reported with a 4-seed interval), **optimism gap** = validation gain − held-out gain, and the k=7 vs k=0 contrast in each.
